selection: All newly discovered matching records in this collection; no fixed paper-count quota.

papers.title: Photomechanical engineering of immunogenic whole-cell vaccines by laser-induced vapor nanobubbles for bladder cancer prophylaxis
papers.authors: Sabando-Garcia, N.; G. Caelles, A.; Traba, N.; Pages, J.; Cabrera, C.; Garcia Hidalgo, A.; Punj, D.; Braeckmans, K.; F. Valledor, A.; Chomiciute, G.; Abasolo, I.; Julian, E.; Sanchez, S.; Fraire, J. C.
papers.abstract: Whole-cell cancer vaccines can provide broad tumor-antigen repertoires, but their efficacy depends on manufacturing methods that inactivate tumor cells while preserving immunogenic danger signals. Here we show that laser-induced vapor nanobubbles (VNB) generated from dextran-coated iron oxide nanoparticles provide a drug-free photomechanical route to engineer immunogenic whole-cell vaccines against bladder cancer. Using MB49 murine urothelial carcinoma cells, we established VNB conditions that induced rapid tumor-cell killing together with calreticulin exposure and extracellular ATP and HMGB1 release. Rapid cell killing and calreticulin exposure were also reproduced in the molecularly distinct UPPL1541 bladder cancer model, supporting the generalizability of the early photomechanical response across bladder cancer cell lines. Vaccination with VNB-killed MB49 cells reduced tumor incidence and growth after subcutaneous challenge and enhanced splenocyte-mediated antitumor activity against MB49 cells. In an orthotopic bladder cancer model, vaccination prevented MRI-detectable tumor formation and was associated with marked early bladder enrichment of CD8 T cells and inflammatory monocytes. A single administration of the VNB-generated vaccine preparation showed no evident local or systemic toxicity during seven days of follow-up. These findings provide proof of concept for an externally triggered, drug-free manufacturing approach in which short laser irradiation induces rapid photomechanical killing of tumor cells on demand, generating immunogenic whole-tumor-cell vaccine preparations for further evaluation in therapeutic, post-resection and tumor-derived settings.

papers.title: Rapid generation of antibody conformational ensembles using machine learning
papers.authors: Rao, P. V.; Sommer, D.; Davidson, D.; Alberstein, R. G.; Ludwiczak, J.; Kleinhenz, J.; Vani, B.; Park, E.; Lee, J. H.; Izadi, S.; Kiefer, J. R.; Bonneau, R.; Mahajan, S. P.; Watkins, A. M.; Dreyer, F. A.
papers.abstract: We introduce Cadense, a generative framework for antibody ensemble prediction that produces diverse Fv structures from sequence, informed by conformational dynamics. While a valuable resource, static structure prediction provides only a single snapshot of dynamic proteins, whose motions influence their binding and other properties. This is particularly relevant for antibodies, an important class of molecules for drug discovery, where flexible complementarity determining region (CDR) loops are difficult to model with static approaches. Cadense addresses this gap by generating ensembles that match conformational and biophysical property distributions from molecular dynamics (MD), while reducing the computational burden from days of simulation to seconds of generation. We show Cadense ensembles can recover both apo and holo conformations of the same antibody and serve as effective input to physics-based docking, capturing the conformational flexibility important to properly model antibody antigen interactions. Together, these results establish Cadense as a useful tool for antibody conformational ensemble generation with the promise to enable faster, dynamics-aware antibody design.

papers.title: Bioinformatic pipeline for functional inference of Rickettsia akari hypothetical proteins reveals virulence-associated and effector candidates
papers.authors: Kaliukanov, S.; Csicsay, F.; Skultety, L.; Quevedo Diaz, M. A.
papers.abstract: Background Rickettsia akari, the causative agent of rickettsialpox, is an obligate intracellular pathogen with a highly reduced genome encoding numerous hypothetical proteins (HPs) of unknown function. Many of these HPs are expressed during host-cell infection, yet their roles in bacterial physiology and potential contribution to virulence remain unclear. Methodology/Principal Findings We performed an integrative in silico characterization of 54 R. akari HPs previously identified by mass spectrometry in purified bacterial cells. Using a benchmarked computational workflow, we predicted their physicochemical properties, subcellular localization, putative secretion signals, protein folds, potential interaction partners, and evolutionary conservation. Most HPs were predicted to be thermostable. The majority of HPs were predicted to be cytoplasmic (37.00%) or membrane-associated (29.63%). Predicted features associated with the type IV secretion system were more frequent than those associated with type I secretion. Network and structural analyses identified candidate HPs with features consistent with potential roles in outer membrane assembly, host-cell interaction, and immune modulation, including predicted peptidyl-prolyl cis/trans isomerases, oxidoreductases, methyltransferases, and putative E3 ubiquitin ligases. Several HPs were predicted to be antigenic and showed conservation across multiple rickettsial genomes. Molecular docking and normal mode analysis supported the plausibility of selected predicted protein-protein and protein-ligand interactions. Evolutionary analyses indicated predominant purifying selection among the analyzed HPs. A8GP20 showed elevated sequence divergence and warrants further investigation as a potential effector candidate. Conclusions/Significance Our findings prioritize A8GPG8, A8GP63, A8GNV4, A8GMM8, A8GM41, A8GMJ7, A8GMI5, A8GP20, A8GN23, A8GMB4, A8GM08, and A8GM39 as promising candidates for experimental validation of their predicted functions and potential roles in R. akari biology and pathogenicity. This work provides an integrative and reproducible bioinformatic framework to guide functional discovery in R. akari and related neglected intracellular pathogens, and identifies candidate proteins for future studies of rickettsial pathogenesis, antigen discovery, and therapeutic target development.

papers.title: Cholinergic modulation engages a CHRM1-IL-17 neuroimmune axis to promote diabetic wound repair
papers.authors: Li, Z.; Theocharidis, G.; Lee, S.; Kalavros, N.; Nagalakshmi, S. U.; Contreras, M.; Valsami, E.-A.; Nam, H.; Guan, M.; Chu, G.; Mezghani, I.; Wang, E.; Sumpio, B. J.; Hou, J.; Gennari-Felipe, M.; Gilman, J.; Lafuente-Gomez, N.; Maeso Aragon, L.; Dimitrakakis, N.; Arruda de Amaral, A.; Wang, S.; Vlachos, I. S.; Mooney, D. J.; Veves, A.
papers.abstract: Chronic non-healing wounds are a major complication of diabetes, where persistent inflammation fails to transition into effective tissue repair (1-3). Here we identify cholinergic modulation as a mechanism that promotes productive inflammation and diabetic wound healing. Using a healing-associated fibroblast signature derived from single-cell profiling of human diabetic foot ulcers (3), we identified the acetylcholinesterase (AChE) inhibitor metrifonate as a candidate inducer of reparative wound programs. Topical delivery accelerated healing in diabetic mice and increased acetylcholine availability within the wound. Complementary receptor pharmacology identified muscarinic acetylcholine receptor 1 (CHRM1) as the principal receptor mediating the reparative response. Transcriptomic and cellular analyses revealed early induction of IL-17-associated inflammatory programs and enrichment of CHRM1NK1.1 innate lymphocytes. Depletion of NK1.1 cells or neutralization of IL-17A abolished the pro-healing effect, whereas spatial transcriptomics revealed treatment-associated organization of NK cells within vascular niches. Localized treatment further promoted repair in diabetic porcine wounds and human skin models. Together, these findings identify a CHRM1-IL-17 neuroimmune axis linking cholinergic modulation to diabetic wound repair and establish local AChE inhibition as a potential therapeutic strategy for chronic wounds.

papers.title: Distinct Consequences of BCOR and BCORL1 Mutations in Myeloid Neoplasms and Bone Marrow Failure.
papers.authors: Marumo A, Durmaz A, Haddad C, Mandala A, de Almeida Sartori F, Abushamma A, Unlu S, Gu X, Brady Z, D'Addona M, Lakhotiya K, Guarnera L, Yoshida M, Toma MM, Orland MD, Bravo-Perez C, Gurnari C, Takahashi K, Skorski T, Hutter S, Haferlach T, Wlodarski M, Visconte V, Maciejewski JP.
papers.abstract: BCOR and BCORL1 (BCOR/L1) mutations are observed in both myeloid neoplasms (MN) and bone marrow failure syndromes (BMF), but their clinical significance may differ. We analyzed 11 340 patients and identified 418 BCOR/L1-mutated patients, focusing on differences between MN and BMF. Compared with MN, BMF was associated with younger age, a higher frequency of normal karyotype, a greater proportion of missense mutations, and significantly lower variant allele frequencies (VAFs). We next compared BCOR/L1-mutated cases with wild-type cases. In MN, BCOR/L1 mutations were associated with older age, inferior survival, and a higher number of co-occurring mutations, whereas in BMF, they were associated with a higher prevalence of PNH clones. Single-cell DNA sequencing and VAF-based analysis demonstrated that BCOR/L1 mutations were usually secondary in MN but primary events in BMF. Longitudinal sequencing revealed that BCOR/L1-mutant clones often contracted or disappeared over time, even in progression, suggesting limited clonal fitness of BCOR/L1 mutations themselves; instead, progression was associated with increased mutational burden, particularly in RUNX1. Prognostically, BCOR/L1 mutations were associated with inferior survival in MN, whereas in BMF they were not associated with prognosis and tended to correlate with a favorable response to immunosuppressive therapy. RNA-sequencing analyses showed reduced BCOR/L1 expression in BMF, and BCOR knockout was associated with reduced HLA class I expression. Our findings suggest that BCOR/L1 mutations are secondary events in MN and co-occurring mutations may influence disease progression and prognosis, whereas in BMF they appear to be ancestral events acquired independently of progression to MN, potentially through immune privilege-related mechanisms.

papers.title: Single-cell RNA sequencing reveals transcriptional remodeling of splenic lymphocytes following zearalenone exposure in mice.
papers.authors: Li X, Cai G, Zou H, Gu J, Yuan Y, Liu X, Liu Z, Bian J.
papers.abstract: Zearalenone (ZEA) is an estrogenic mycotoxin with documented immunotoxic effects, but its cell-type-resolved splenic responses remain incompletely characterized. In this study, C57BL/6 mice received 20 mg/kg·bw ZEA by oral gavage for 21 consecutive days. Conventional toxicological endpoints, TUNEL staining, cleaved caspase-3 immunofluorescence, and single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) were performed using samples derived from the same exposure experiment, with two pooled libraries sequenced per group, each constructed from the spleens of five mice. Under the tested conditions, no marked changes in spleen organ coefficient or overall histopathological architecture were observed, whereas the TUNEL-positive and cleaved caspase-3-positive cell ratios were significantly increased in ZEA-exposed mice. scRNA-seq resolved 44,759 high-quality splenic cells into 15 transcriptionally distinct populations. Differential expression analysis identified cell-type-associated transcriptional changes, including altered antigen-presentation and ribosomal programs in B and T cells and changes in apoptosis-, antioxidant-, and mitochondria-related gene sets in selected populations. CellChat predicted altered intercellular communication and SCENIC inferred altered NF-κB2, STAT1, and MYC regulon activities. These findings describe increased apoptosis-related positivity accompanied by cell-type-resolved transcriptional remodeling following ZEA exposure. This exploratory atlas provides a basis for further mechanistic and dose-response studies for mycotoxin risk assessment.
papers.venue: Toxicon : official journal of the International Society on Toxinology

papers.title: Integrated bioinformatic and molecular analyses reveal the IRF1-TGM2 axis in regulating oxidative stress and apoptosis in in vitro CD-like intestinal epithelial cell models.
papers.authors: Wang C, Zhang C, Wu C, Lin G, Shao Y, He M.
papers.abstract: Crohn's disease (CD) is a chronic recurrent inflammatory bowel disease (IBD). Transglutaminase 2 (TGM2) participates in CD progression, yet its regulatory mechanism remains elusive. Here, transcriptomic, single-cell transcriptomic, metabolomic, and apoptosis-related datasets from GEO, Metabolomics Workbench, and GeneCards were integrated, followed by bioinformatic analyses using R 4.5.1 and MetaboAnalyst 5.0. In vitro experiments included Western blot, cell transfection, TUNEL, ELISA, ROS detection, ChIP, dual-luciferase reporter assay, and RT-qPCR. Bioinformatic analyses identified distinct gene expression profiles, aberrant immune cell infiltration, and disrupted energy and lipid metabolism in CD, yielding 23 candidate targets. TGM2 was enriched in fibroblasts, enterocytes, and myeloid cells, modulating apoptosis, inflammation, and oxidative stress to aggravate CD phenotypes. Mechanistically, interferon regulatory factor 1 (IRF1) directly bound to the TGM2 promoter and enhanced its transcription. The IRF1-TGM2 axis regulated apoptosis, inflammation, and ROS levels, with TGM2 overexpression reversing the inhibitory effects of IRF1 knockdown. IRF1 transcriptionally upregulates TGM2 to promote apoptosis and oxidative stress, providing a plausible mechanistic framework for CD-associated epithelial injury.

papers.title: Pro-inflammatory Neutrophils in Kidney Injury: Emerging Mechanistic Insights.
papers.authors: Yin J, Kurts C.
papers.abstract: Background Neutrophils are traditionally viewed as short-lived antimicrobial effector immune cells, but recent evidence reveals substantial heterogeneity and broader roles in driving kidney disease. Summary This review highlights current insights into neutrophil diversity and their pathogenic roles in kidney disease. Recent advances, particularly single-cell analyses, have identified distinct neutrophil subsets. In inflammatory kidney diseases, pro-inflammatory neutrophils drive tissue injury through multiple mechanisms, including cytokine production, reactive oxygen species release, and formation of neutrophil extracellular traps. In addition, emerging evidence identifies specialized subsets with prolonged survival and enhanced inflammatory or pro-fibrotic activity, which contribute to disease progression. Interactions with adaptive immune cells, particularly T helper 17 cells, further amplify these responses, creating self-sustaining inflammatory circuits.

papers.title: Multi-omics indicating the risk of organochlorines to liver cancer.
papers.authors: Xie J, Bai H, Yang Z, Song L, Xie Y, Chao Y, Xie Y, Liang Q.
papers.abstract: The incidence and mortality rates of liver cancer remain consistently high worldwide, with China having the highest rates globally. The causes of liver cancer are multifactorial. This study focuses on identifying specific targets that continuously contribute to cellular damage after exposure to environmental organic chlorine compounds (OCCs), ultimately increasing the risk of liver cancer development. Liver cancer-related data were obtained from the GEO and TCGA databases. Differentially expressed genes (DEGs) were analyzed using the "limma" package in R. WGCNA was employed to identify co-expression modules of highly correlated genes in liver cancer. Targets for six representative OCCs-trichloromethane, carbon tetrachloride, PCB28, PCB52, TCDD, and DDT-were retrieved from the PharmGKB, STITCH 4.0, CTD, PharmMapper, and SuperPred databases. Liver cancer-related targets were extracted from the TTD, GeneCards, Digsee, DisGeNET, OMIM, and CTD databases. A "OCCs-key targets-liver cancer" network was constructed using Cytoscape 3.8.1. Core targets were selected through cancer risk prognostic models to further investigate their roles in cancer initiation and progression. GO, KEGG, and disease enrichment analyses were performed using the core targets. The correlation between core targets and 22 types of infiltrating immune cells was analyzed. Molecular docking and dynamics simulations were conducted to verify the binding affinities between OCCs and these core proteins. A total of 195 common targets between OCCs and liver cancer were identified. After performing PPI analysis, 85 key targets were selected to construct a "OCCs-key targets-liver cancer" network. TTK, KPNA2, CDKN3, EZH2, and CPEB3 were identified as core targets through the cancer risk prognostic model. GO enrichment analysis revealed that the core targets were primarily involved in the regulation of the mitotic cell cycle. KEGG enrichment analysis confirmed a strong association between these targets and chemical carcinogenesis, as well as cell cycle regulation. Disease enrichment analysis indicated that the core targets were significantly linked to neoplasms, particularly liver cancer. Immunoinfiltration analysis suggested that tumors may promote immune evasion by increasing the expression of immunosuppressive cells while decreasing the levels of activated immune cells. Molecular docking and dynamics simulations identified key binding interactions, amino acid residues, and binding energies, further confirming strong binding affinities between OCCs and the core targets. This study integrates network toxicology, machine learning, WGCNA, molecular docking, molecular dynamics simulations, and immunoinfiltration analysis, providing evidence that prolonged exposure to OCCs may increase the risk of liver cancer development.

papers.title: Unveiling the role of adipokine-related genes in biliary atresia through transcriptomic analysis and machine learning.
papers.authors: Wang Y, Liu X, Wang D, Hou P, Mu W, Zhang Y, Liu X, Sun Y, Zhang Q, Li A.
papers.abstract: Background Biliary atresia (BA) is a devastating neonatal cholestatic disease characterized by progressive fibro-obliteration of the extrahepatic bile ducts. Although adipokine signaling is implicated in liver pathology, its key mediators in BA remain unclear. Methods We analyzed BA transcriptomic data (GSE46960) to identify differentially expressed genes (DEGs) and derived an adipokine-associated gene set (AdipoBA-GeneSet). An ensemble of 101 machine learning algorithms was employed to prioritize key genes. The diagnostic value, associated biological pathways, and immune infiltration patterns of key genes were investigated. The role of Leucine-Rich Alpha-2-Glycoprotein 1 (LRG1) was validated in a biliatresone-induced BA mouse model by upregulating its expression. Results We identified 522 DEGs in BA livers, refined to a 30-gene AdipoBA-GeneSet. Machine learning prioritized seven key genes from this adipokine-related gene set (LEPR, SPP1, LRG1, IL32, FBN1, IGF1, and SAA1). These genes showed excellent performance in distinguishing BA patients from normal controls and were linked to extracellular matrix organization and immune pathways. Immune infiltration analysis revealed that key gene expression correlated with specific immune cell subsets. Notably, the adipokine LRG1 was downregulated in BA, and its overexpression alleviated the disease phenotype, as evidenced by improved body weight, decreased bile duct wall-to-lumen ratio, attenuated hepatic fibrosis, and ameliorated hepatic steatosis. Conclusion This study identifies a novel adipokine-related gene signature in BA and highlights LRG1 as a key protector. LRG1 overexpression mitigates cholestatic injury and fibrotic progression in vivo, positioning it as a promising therapeutic target.

papers.title: Integrative network toxicology and clinical validation identify CD4, PTGS2, and KDR as candidate targets of nicotine in infantile hemangioma.
papers.authors: Luo S, Chen Z, Liu D, Liao M, Hu J, Du F, Liu C, Lin B.
papers.abstract: Infantile hemangioma (IH) is the most common benign vascular tumor of infancy. Perinatal tobacco smoke exposure has been associated with pediatric benign tumors, but a specific molecular link between nicotine and IH has not been established. We aimed to identify and validate candidate targets of nicotine in IH. Age-stratified differentially expressed genes (6, 12, and 24 months) from GSE127487 were intersected with IH- and nicotine-related targets and prioritized by network analysis, followed by enrichment analysis, immune deconvolution, and molecular docking, with tissue validation and machine-learning screening of a clinical cohort (77 patients, 50 controls). CD4, PTGS2, and KDR were core targets shared across age groups, whereas EGFR, PPARG, TLR4, and ACE were stage-restricted; enrichment converged on PI3K-Akt, MAPK, HIF-1, and VEGF signaling. Nicotine showed computationally plausible docking to KDR (-6.91 kcal/mol) and PTGS2 (-6.39 kcal/mol). CD4 and PTGS2 proteins were markedly upregulated in IH lesions, with KDR showing a concordant upward trend (paired t-test: P < 0.001, P < 0.001, and P = 0.062, respectively). Single-cell re-analysis placed KDR in GLUT1-positive lesional endothelium and CD4 transcripts mainly in myeloid and mural cells. A four-indicator blood signature (globulin, mean platelet volume, platelet distribution width, and total protein; AUC 0.942, 95 % CI 0.859-1.000) reflected the associated immune-inflammation state. These hypothesis-generating results nominate a CD4-, PTGS2-, and KDR-centered network converging on angiogenic and inflammatory signaling as a candidate route through which nicotine may act in IH. These candidate targets and the blood signature require external-cohort and mechanistic validation.

papers.title: Semi-randomized zwitterionic peptides: a breakthrough in drug delivery.
papers.authors: Hernandez PA, Moore CJ, Overby CT, Benoit DSW.
papers.abstract: Introduction Nanoparticle drug delivery systems (NP DDS) have transformed therapeutic delivery by improving drug stability, extending circulation time, and enabling targeted biodistribution. However, clinical translation remains limited by protein corona formation, immune recognition, and accelerated blood clearance following repeated administration. Poly(ethylene glycol) (PEG) has been the gold-standard antifouling material for decades, but emerging anti-PEG immune responses have driven the search for alternative stealth technologies. Areas covered Zwitterionic peptides (ZIPs) have emerged as a promising class of antifouling materials because they combine the hydration-mediated stealth properties of zwitterionic polymers with the molecular precision and programmability of peptide synthesis. Here, ZIP applications in drug delivery were reviewed using the Web of Science database from 2014-2026, focusing on reducing and controlling the protein corona, recent advances in ZIP-based drug delivery, and the potential of high-throughput screening platforms and machine learning-guided ZIP design. Recent studies suggest that biological interactions of ZIP-functionalized NPs are governed primarily by charge motifs rather than precise sequences, creating new opportunities for material design. Expert opinion This observation motivates developing semi-randomized ZIPs (srZIPs) that preserve charge organization while introducing sequence diversity. By maintaining key physicochemical and biological properties while diversifying composition, srZIPs may reduce immune recognition without sacrificing antifouling function.

papers.title: Temporal dynamics of antigen-specific T cell expansion in primary SARS-CoV-2 infection.
papers.authors: Pyo AGT, Chan A, Rosenheim J, Thakker C, Bell L, Nageswaran G, Byrne S, Killingley B, Scobie D, Kalinova M, Boyers A, Catchpole A, Mann A, Lindeboom RGH, Nikolic MZ, Teichmann SA, Wagstaffe H, Noursadeghi M, Chiu C, Callan CG, Tiffeau-Mayer A, Wingreen NS, Chain B.
papers.abstract: Quantifying T cell response during primary infection in humans is crucial for understanding adaptive immunity. Leveraging a controlled human challenge to severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2, we characterized antigen-specific T cell responses within and across individuals. Notably, individual clones reached similar maximum frequencies despite differences in the timing of their peak expansion. Mathematical modeling within a coarse-grained framework suggested that variability in precursor frequency between different T cell clones could be one mechanism to explain this relationship. Single-cell profiling revealed distinct temporal programs for CD4 + and CD8 + T cells, with CD4 + cells expanding earlier but contracting to a lower frequency. Clones with similar receptors, likely recognizing the same antigen, expanded at similar times. Together, these findings highlight how clone-intrinsic properties such as precursor frequency and CD4/CD8 subset status shape T cell clonal kinetics. These insights provide a quantitative framework for understanding T cell response in humans, with implications for vaccine design.

figure.label: Fig. 1.
figure.caption: Characterization of T cell clonal dynamics in response to SARS-CoV-2. ( A ) Schematic overview of the study design and the approach used to characterize T cell clonal dynamics in peripheral blood mononuclear cells (PBMCs). ( B and C ) Abundance of expanding T cell clones inferred from CDR3 sequences of the α chain (B) and β chain (C) as a function of time relative to the peak time, estimated by fitting to Eq. 1 . The average fit is shown in red as a visual guide and does not correspond to any single clonal trajectory. ( D to G ) Inferred values of parameters characterizing T cell clonal dynamics. Expansion timescale (D), contraction timescale (E), peak day (F), and peak abundance (G) of expanding T cell clones from model fits for 10 individuals. Expanding T cell clones inferred from CDR3α sequences are shown in blue, and expanding clones inferred from CDR3β sequences are shown in green.

papers.title: Uncovering the immune microenvironmental atlas of breast cancer molecular subtypes based on single-cell transcriptomics.
papers.authors: Lin S, Zheng Y, Chen Z, Patrice MD, Wang L, Li X, Zhang Y, Zhang X.
papers.abstract: Breast cancer progression is closely linked to immune cells within the tumor microenvironment (TME), but the immune landscape differences across HER2-positive (HER2+), triple-negative (TNBC), and ER-positive (ER+) subtypes have yet to be systematically characterized. In this study, we characterized immune landscape differences across HER2-positive (HER2+), triple-negative (TNBC), and ER-positive (ER+) breast cancers using single-cell RNA sequencing data, focusing on T cells, macrophages, and B cells. Our analysis revealed that cytotoxic CD8 + T cells were more abundant in TNBC but showed signs of dysfunction. Macrophage subsets, including an NDUFB8 + population, exhibited divergent functional orientations across subtypes. B cells in TNBC exhibited functional alterations, characterized by a decreased proportion of plasmablasts and an increased proportion of memory B cells. Single-cell regulatory network inference and clustering (SCENIC) analysis predicted a set of subtype-specific candidate transcription factors (TFs), including E2F8 across all subtypes and ATF7 in HER2 + tumors, whose activity correlated with clinical outcomes. Finally, mapping multicellular communication networks revealed both conserved and subtype-specific signaling pathways. Together, these results present a detailed transcriptional landscape of immune heterogeneity in breast cancer and contribute novel insights that may inform the design of subtype-specific immunotherapies.

figure.label: Fig 1
figure.caption: Single-cell landscape of the tumor immune microenvironment in HER2 + , TNBC, and ER+ breast cancer subtypes. (A-C) Cell cluster distribution of the three breast cancer molecular subtypes visualized via UMAP dimensionality reduction: (A) HER2 + subtype, (B) TNBC subtype, (C) ER+ subtype; (D-F) Cell clusters of the three breast cancer subtypes were annotated and grouped using a panel of classical cell type markers, showing the distribution of major cell types in UMAP plots. These major cell types include 8 categories: B cells, T cells, myeloid cells, endothelial cells, epithelial cells, mesenchymal cells, plasma cells, and proliferating cells; (G-I) Bar charts showing the proportion of each cell type among patients for the three subtypes; (J-L) Pie charts representing the proportional analysis of cell types in the three subtypes.

papers.title: IGFBP7-targeting monoclonal antibodies attenuate the endothelial inflammatory niche in psoriasis-like inflammation.
papers.authors: Zhang X, Zhang T, Xu J, Li K, Li G, Miao H, Mao L, Shao S, Wang L, Dang E, Wang G, Li Q.
papers.abstract: Psoriasis is sustained by immune-endothelial interactions that support leukocyte recruitment into inflamed skin. We previously showed that endothelial IGFBP7 disrupts the glycocalyx and promotes T-cell extravasation. Here, we developed and compared monoclonal antibodies against human IGFBP7. Reanalysis of longitudinal single-cell RNA sequencing from risankizumab-treated psoriasis skin identified an IGFBP7-positive vascular endothelial state that was enriched in baseline lesions and reduced during treatment. Cutaneous IGFBP7 expression also correlated with Psoriasis Area and Severity Index in an independent cohort. Three mouse monoclonal antibodies were generated against recombinant human IGFBP7, and all three recognized recombinant murine IGFBP7. CMC0667 showed the strongest reference-antibody cross-competition (IC₅₀, 5.72 nM), while surface plasmon resonance confirmed direct nanomolar-range binding to IGFBP7 ( k a , 2.86 × 10 5 M -1 s -1 ; k d , 1.35 × 10 -2 s -1 ; kinetic K D , 47.4 nM). In cytokine-stimulated HMEC-1 cells, the antibodies increased hyaluronic acid and heparan sulfate signals, reduced endothelial activation, improved junction-associated gene expression, and decreased FITC-dextran permeability and CD3⁺CD4⁺ T-cell transendothelial migration. In imiquimod-treated mice, all three antibodies reduced epidermal hyperplasia, keratinocyte proliferation, inflammatory and chemotactic gene expression, and cutaneous T-cell accumulation. CMC0667 showed the most consistent overall activity. Together, these data identify CMC0667 as the lead anti-IGFBP7 antibody for further preclinical optimization.

papers.title: Comparing Gleason pattern 4 measurement approaches on prostate biopsy using machine learning: a proof-of-principle study.
papers.authors: Buzoianu MM, Yu R, Assel M, Bozkurt A, Aghdam H, Fine SW, Vickers AJ.
papers.abstract: Background and objective There is increasing evidence that length of Gleason Pattern (GP) 4 on biopsy is a stronger predictor of oncological outcomes than Grade Group (GG) or %GP4. However, there is no consensus regarding the optimal method for quantifying GP4 length. We propose that machine learning (ML) can be used to quantify GP4 on digitized biopsy slides using multiple measurement approaches, allowing direct comparison of their prognostic performance. In this study, we attempt to demonstrate proof-of-principle for this approach. Methods We assembled a convenience sample of 726 patients with GG2-4 prostate cancer on systematic biopsy who underwent radical prostatectomy between 2014 and 2023. ML algorithm (PAIGE-AI) quantified GP4 using different approaches, varying by how gaps between cancer foci were handled. GP4 extent was assessed using linear and pixel-based metrics. Discrimination of each quantification approach, along with GG, was assessed for adverse radical prostatectomy pathology and biochemical recurrence. Key findings and limitations We identified 15 different quantification approaches and observed differences between their discrimination. The highest discrimination was in the pixel-counting method (AUC 0.648). GP4 quantification outperformed GG for predicting adverse pathology (AUC 0.627 versus 0.608). The amount of GP3 was non-predictive once GP4 was known. These findings were consistent for BCR. Conclusions We were able to measure slides using 15 distinct measurement approaches and replicated prior findings using ML to quantify GP4. Our findings support the use of ML as a research tool to compare different GP4 quantification approaches. We intend to use our method on larger cohorts to determine which measurement approach best predicts oncological outcome.

papers.title: Cytokine and chemokine circuits in non-small cell lung cancer: spatial biomarkers and an evidence-guided framework for combination immunotherapy.
papers.authors: Xu Y, Yang M, Ma Y, Wang Y, Liu J, Liang T, Guo L.
papers.abstract: Immune checkpoint inhibitors have improved outcomes in non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC), yet durable benefit remains uneven because tumor immunity is organized by cytokine and chemokine circuits that vary across anatomic niches and treatment states. This narrative review integrates single-cell, spatial, mechanistic and clinically annotated evidence around source-ligand-receptor-target relationships to assess how cytokine and chemokine circuits relate to ICI response and resistance in NSCLC, and what these findings imply for spatial biomarkers and combination strategies. Representative activating circuits reviewed here include XCL1/2-XCR1- and CCL5-dependent cDC1 recruitment, IL-12/IL-18-supported NK-cell activation, CXCL9/10-CXCR3-guided effector trafficking and CXCL13-CXCR5-dependent tertiary lymphoid structure organization. These programs may support antitumor immunity relevant to ICI response, whereas suppressive programs involving TGF-β, IL-10, CSF1, CCL2, IL-17, together with interacting pathways such as adenosine-mediated metabolic suppression, may contribute to immune exclusion and resistance in NSCLC. Clinical translation remains uneven: spatial biomarkers and pathway-directed combinations are supported mainly by cross-sectional cohorts, mechanistic studies and early clinical trials, with several negative or context-specific results. We therefore synthesize these findings and outline a conceptual, evidence-tiered framework that considers cellular source, receptor-bearing target, spatial niche, treatment history and pharmacodynamic evidence. By linking spatial immune organization to mechanisms of response and resistance, this framework provides a foundation for biomarker-informed combinations tailored to distinct immune dysfunctions, with the potential to overcome resistance and extend durable immunotherapy benefit to more patients with NSCLC.

papers.title: Dupilumab modulates type II IL-4/IL-13 receptor-expressing immune cells in eosinophilic chronic rhinosinusitis.
papers.authors: Sonobe Y, Iinuma T, Kokubo K, Kiuchi M, Iwamura C, Nemoto M, Hishiya T, Sasaki A, Tsuji K, Ohishi K, Kusakari K, Sekino S, Hiramoto T, Shinmi R, Koya T, Onodera A, Kimura MY, Motohashi S, Yonekura S, Nakayama T, Hanazawa T, Hirahara K.
papers.abstract: Background Eosinophilic chronic rhinosinusitis (eCRS) is a refractory type 2 inflammatory disease characterized by nasal polyp formation and eosinophilic infiltration. Although dupilumab, an IL-4Rα-blocking antibody, demonstrates clinical efficacy, its cellular mechanisms within nasal polyps remain unclear. Objective To define the cell type-specific effects of dupilumab in eCRS, we examined IL-4/IL-13 receptor-dependent transcriptional responses in tissue-resident immune cells. Methods Nasal polyp and peripheral blood samples were collected from five patients with eCRS before and after dupilumab treatment. Single-cell RNA sequencing on four paired cases, spatial transcriptomics, and immunostaining were performed. In vitro stimulation of human conventional dendritic cells (cDCs) validated IL-4/IL-13-regulated pathways. Results Dupilumab improved symptoms and attenuated eosinophilic inflammation. Across annotated populations, the number of differentially expressed genes correlated positively with pre-treatment IL13RA1 expression. Accordingly, myeloid cells, particularly cDCs, which predominantly express type II IL-4/IL-13 receptors, showed the broadest transcriptional changes, including downregulation of ALOX15; ALOX15 inhibition abrogated IL-4/IL-13-induced CCL13 and CCL22 expression in cDCs. After treatment, pathogenic Th2 cell subset expressed lower IL1RL1 and AREG. IGHE and IL4R expression in CD23-positive B cells declined, as did PRDM1 and ELL2 in plasma cells. In one paired case, spatial analysis identified fewer TLS-like aggregates and lower detection of ALOX15 and IGHE transcripts after treatment. Conclusion Dupilumab preferentially remodels type II IL-4/IL-13 receptor-expressing immune cells, particularly polyp cDCs, while selectively reprogramming Th2, B, and plasma cells. Identification of ALOX15 as a candidate mediator in cDCs provides mechanistic insight that may inform optimization of type 2-targeted therapy in eCRS.
papers.venue: The Journal of allergy and clinical immunology

papers.title: Senescent T cells within the tumor microenvironment are a potent driver for tumor growth, stemness, and chemotherapy resistance.
papers.authors: Zhang Y, Liu X, Xie Y, Zhao L, Jeon MS, Ai L, Luo J, Ford DA, Abusalamah H, Harbison RA, Huffman C, Guo J, He I, Mulvehill A, Buchman CA, Puram SV, Garcia BA, Varvares MA, Colonna M, Peng G.
papers.abstract: T cell senescence is an important dysfunctional state associated with tumor progression, but whether senescent T (Tsen) cells directly reprogram tumor cell behavior remains unknown. Here, single-cell transcriptomic analyses identify abundant Tsen cells across breast, colorectal, and lung cancers. Tsen cells actively promote tumor growth, metastasis, stemness, and chemotherapy resistance by reprogramming tumor cells in vitro and in vivo. Mechanistically, lipid-enriched senescence-associated secretory phenotypes (SASPs) from Tsen cells drive metabolic remodeling and activate STAT1/STAT3 signaling in tumor cells, establishing a pro-tumorigenic state. Therapeutically, depletion of Tsen cells or disruption of tumor lipid metabolic reprogramming suppresses Tsen-mediated tumor progression and metastasis in vivo. Our findings establish Tsen cells as active orchestrators of tumor cell biological functions through lipid-rich SASP-dependent intercellular communication and reveal a previously unrecognized mechanism linking immune senescence to cancer progression. Targeting Tsen cells or their metabolic crosstalk with tumor cells can enhance anti-tumor immunity and improve therapeutic responses.

papers.title: Deep Phenotyping Reveals Evolution in T cell Phenotype after Hexaviral-specific T cell Infusion Post Hematopoietic Stem Cell Transplant.
papers.authors: Chansky P, Maghzian N, Adhikari N, Harris K, Hanisch B, Trampetti F, Ayala-Gomez D, Datar A, Lazarski C, Paul G, Joy E, Fulton K, McCann C, Dioverti-Prono V, Bhatia M, Hanley PJ, Hoq F, Jacobsohn D, Vatsayan A, Saldana BD, Zhang A, Tanna J, Parekh C, Li W, Abraham AA, Bollard CM, Keller MD, Kinoshita H.
papers.abstract: Viral infections are common following hematopoietic stem cell transplant (HCT) and multivirus-specific T cell therapies have been utilized to treat or prevent several viral infections and reactivation. In this study, we evaluated a novel donor-derived hexaviral specific T cell (hVST) product targeting cytomegalovirus (CMV), adenovirus (AdV), Epstein-Barr Virus (EBV), human polyomavirus (BKV), human parainfluenza virus 3 (HPIV3), and human herpes virus 6 (HHV6). This hVST product was tolerated in 5 adult and 9 pediatric patients with toxicities limited to grade I-II cytokine release syndrome (n=2), immune effector cell-associated neurotoxicity syndrome (n=1) and chronic GVHD (n=1). Three months post-treatment, 8/8 evaluable patients with active viral infections achieved a partial or complete response to at least one target virus. Single cell gene expression of hVST products showed CD4+ and CD8+ T cells with effector memory and activation markers (n=4). In evaluable recipients (n=4) following hVST infusion, there was a shift from a naïve and indistinct T cell profile pre infusion to predominantly memory T cell populations in the peripheral blood after hVST infusion (median 70 days). These data suggest that hexaviral specific T cells have potential for preventing and treating multiple viruses in patients post-HCT.
papers.venue: Molecular therapy : the journal of the American Society of Gene Therapy

papers.title: In situ CAR engineering and nanoparticle-mediated TREM2 degradation for macrophage reprogramming in malignant ascites.
papers.authors: Li Y, Yang T, Zhang X, Peng R, Gong J, Zhang Z, Ma B, Hou Y, Liu Y, Chen K, Bai Q, Fang Y, Cao C, Hao J, Sun Z, Jiang Z, Dong M, Wei C, Li Z, Zhang Q, Shen L, Wang X, Deng M, Qi C, Miao L.
papers.abstract: Peritoneal metastasis (PM) and the resulting malignant tumour ascites characterize advanced gastrointestinal cancers, often leading to poor prognosis and limited response to current therapies. Single-cell analysis of patient-derived PM and malignant tumour ascites reveals an approximately 90% enrichment of TREM2 + -tumour-associated macrophages, which drive CD8 + T cell dysfunction and tumour growth. Here we develop lipid nanoparticles encapsulating mRNA to reprogram these tumour-associated macrophages into chimeric antigen receptor macrophages targeting Claudin18.2-positive tumour ascites. The lipid nanoparticles incorporate a TREM2 + ligand to enhance the targeting of TREM2 macrophages. The piperazine-containing phosphoramide ionizable lipid synergizes with the TREM2 ligand to inhibit ligand dissociation, promoting TREM2 internalization and degradation via lysosomal and autophagosomal pathways. This inhibits AKT signalling and reprograms tumour-associated macrophages towards an antitumour phenotype, enhancing progenitor exhausted and effector memory CD8 + T cell responses, altering the PM transcriptome, and reducing immunosuppression in both malignant tumour ascites and tumours. Combined with PD-1 blockade, this therapy suppresses tumour growth and extends survival in mice, and with matching immunological effects in clinical samples, demonstrates its translational potential for PM immunotherapy.

papers.title: Parental obesity is associated with altered hematopoiesis and impaired viral immunity in offspring.
papers.authors: Allene EC, Sundarraj SP, Alibolandi Z, Khojandi N, Piening E, Piening A, Pritchett M, Shornick LP, Teague RM.
papers.abstract: The prevalence of obesity among adults of childbearing age has tripled worldwide since 1975. Obesity during pregnancy has been linked to impaired neonatal immunity and a higher risk of infections in childhood but the causal mechanisms have not been defined. Using a mouse model of diet-induced obesity, we documented impaired antiviral immunity in the offspring of obese mice, corresponding with reduced cell-mediated immune responses. This included lower frequencies of Tbet+ CD4+ T helper 1 cells and a decrease in cytotoxic CD8+ T cells in the lungs of mice infected with respiratory Sendai virus, and confirmed in spleens from mice infected with LCMV. Consistent with impaired cellular immunity, single-cell transcriptomic analysis of bone marrow revealed altered hematopoiesis in these offspring, with evidence of interferon-induced skewing toward myelopoiesis at the expense of lymphocyte development. Our studies provide an in-depth transcriptomic profile of immune cell progenitors in the bone marrow paired with mature innate and adaptive immune cell populations in lymph nodes at single-cell resolution. Results suggest that compromised immune protection from viral infections in the offspring of obese mice stems from altered lymphocyte development that is influenced by inflammatory interferon signaling in bone marrow.

papers.title: Cholesterol transporters and immune-metabolic features in patients with metastatic renal cell carcinoma receiving immunotherapy combinations.
papers.authors: Giudice GC, Abushukair HM, Mazzaschi G, Tuttobene P, Maffezzoli M, Gnetti L, Campanini N, Iovane G, Perrone F, Pluchino M, Rapacchi E, Pinterpe G, Travaglini S, Marchitelli R, Oh TG, Naqash AR, Santoni M, Araldi E, Pili R, Perrone R, Potì F, Berardi R, Pecci F, Buti S.
papers.abstract: Background Despite improved outcomes with immune checkpoint inhibitor (ICI) combinations in metastatic renal cell carcinoma (mRCC), reliable biologically-driven prognostic markers remain needed. The CHOMET study evaluated tumor ABCA1/ABCG1 expression and their association with systemic lipid parameters, nutritional status, nephrectomy status and survival outcomes. Methods CHOMET was a retrospective observational biomarker study including mRCC patients undergoing first-line ICI-combinations. Tumor ABCA1 and ABCG1 expressions were assessed by immunohistochemistry (IHC). Serum total cholesterol (TC), triglycerides (TG), and the Controlling Nutritional Status score (CONUT) were collected. Publicly available transcriptomic datasets were used for exploratory bulk RNA-seq, immune deconvolution, and single-cell analyses. Results Among 86 patients (46 with IHC), high ABCA1 and ABCG1 expression was associated with shorter overall survival (OS, p = 0.003 and p = 0.01) and progression-free survival (PFS, p = 0.05 and p = 0.08). A composite nephrectomy-cholesterol score and a lower CONUT score were both significantly associated with improved PFS and OS. Exploratory bulk RNA-seq analyses suggested that high ABCA1 expression correlated with features of an immunosuppressive microenvironment enriched in M2 macrophages and depleted of CD8+ T cells, whereas high ABCG1 expression correlated with increased regulatory T cells. Exploratory single-cell analyses from four patients showed ABCA1 and ABCG1 expression across tumor-associated macrophages and tumor cells, with donor-specific pathway enrichment patterns involving immune signaling and cholesterol metabolism-related transcriptional programs. Conclusions ABCA1 and ABCG1 expression levels were associated with poorer outcomes in mRCC treated with ICI combinations and support a link between cholesterol transport programs and an immunosuppressive, metabolically reprogrammed tumor microenvironment.

papers.title: Resolving melanoma heterogeneity at single-cell resolution: implications for target discovery and therapy resistance.
papers.authors: Jin M, Song J, Xin Y, Tan Q, Qin Z, Wang Z, Zhang L.
papers.abstract: Melanoma is characterized by profound intra-tumoural heterogeneity and a complex tumour microenvironment (TME), which are primary drivers of therapy resistance. Conventional bulk sequencing lacks the resolution to capture these cellular nuances. Single-cell technologies, particularly single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) and spatial multiomics, have fundamentally advanced our understanding of melanoma by enabling high-resolution characterization of malignant cell states, immune ecosystems and tumour microenvironment interactions. In this review, we summarize recent advances in single-cell multiomics studies of melanoma heterogeneity and therapy resistance, focusing on the identification of drug-tolerant persister states, immune escape mechanisms and resistance-associated cellular transitions. We further discuss how single-cell approaches facilitate target discovery, biomarker development and the rational design of combination therapies. By integrating multiomics profiling, computational modelling and pharmacological validation, these technologies provide a framework for translating cellular-level insights into precision therapeutic strategies. Finally, we highlight current challenges and future opportunities for clinical implementation of single-cell-guided approaches in refractory melanoma.

papers.title: Single-Cell RNA Sequencing-Integrated Fibroblast Markers and Candidate Drug-Target Associations in Pancreatic Ductal Adenocarcinoma.
papers.authors: Ji T, Wu H, Zheng Z, Ma K.
papers.abstract: Background Pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) has dismal outcomes and is shaped by a fibroblast-rich tumor microenvironment (TME). A cell type-resolved, module-level understanding of cancer-associated fibroblasts (CAFs) and their therapeutic relevance remains incompletely characterized. Methods We integrated single-cell RNA-seq data from six treatment-naïve PDAC resection specimens in GSE212966; individual tumor-stage information was not available in the public metadata. Standardized preprocessing, clustering, and major-cell-type annotation were performed. Contact-mediated intercellular signaling toward fibroblasts was profiled. High-dimensional weighted gene co-expression network analysis (hdWGCNA) was applied to fibroblasts to identify co-expression modules and hub genes. Associations with overall survival were assessed by univariate Cox models and Kaplan-Meier analysis; immune infiltration was evaluated with CIBERSORT and ESTIMATE; pathway associations were examined by gene set enrichment analysis (GSEA). Candidate compounds were screened via Enrichr/DSigDB and docked to target proteins using a PyMOL-Chem3D-AutoDockTools workflow. SEMA3C was further examined in PDAC cell lines by siRNA-mediated knockdown followed by qRT-PCR, CCK-8, wound-healing, and Transwell invasion assays. Results We resolved 10 cell subpopulations and observed broad contact signals to fibroblasts, including the CD99-CD99 axis. hdWGCNA delineated fibroblast modules, from which four key modules were prioritized. Five genes-SEMA3C, PMP22, CPE, SNX9, and UACA-were significantly associated with overall survival. These biomarkers showed both positive and negative associations with specific immune-cell fractions but were positively correlated with the StromalScore, ImmuneScore, and ESTIMATEScore. High-expression groups were enriched for cancer-relevant programs such as epithelial-mesenchymal transition, inflammatory response, and TNF α -NF- κ B signaling, whereas several proliferative and metabolic pathways were enriched in the CPE-low group. In vitro, siRNA-mediated SEMA3C knockdown in PANC-1 and Capan-2 cells reduced cell viability, wound closure, and invasion, supporting a cell-intrinsic protumorigenic role of SEMA3C in PDAC cells. Coumestrol emerged as a computationally prioritized compound, and molecular docking predicted a potentially favorable interaction with SNX9 (predicted binding energy -7.5 kcal/mol); this association requires experimental validation. Conclusion An integrative single-cell and network framework identified fibroblast-related co-expression modules and five survival-associated genes in PDAC. The prognostic relevance of these genes and the predicted coumestrol-SNX9 association require further independent and experimental validation.

papers.title: The tumour microenvironment in mycosis fungoides - decoupling biological and clinical responses.
papers.authors: de Masson A, Battistella M, Guenova E, Papadavid E, Vermeer MH, Moins-Teisserenc H.
papers.abstract: The tumour microenvironment (TME) plays a pivotal role in the progression of mycosis fungoides (MF), characterised by a shift in the immune response from a T helper (Th) 1 cell (Th1) to a Th2 cell profile. While this framework captures key features of disease progression, recent single-cell and spatial transcriptomic studies have further illuminated diverse malignant T-cell states, immune trajectories and spatial niches that extend beyond cytokine polarity alone. Skin-directed and systemic therapies for MF affect both malignant T-cells and the surrounding TME. The therapeutic response begins with biological changes in the TME, including tumour T-cell elimination via tumour cell killing and apoptosis, along with modification of the inflammatory milieu. Because these biological changes take time, early signs of clinical improvement may be subtle. Skin-related treatment-related adverse events, including inflammation, may occur and can be difficult to distinguish from ongoing disease. Given this overlap, careful clinical evaluation is warranted before changes to therapy are considered. It is therefore important to distinguish biological responses in the skin TME from clinical responses on the skin. In this article, we review data on biological and clinical responses to treatment in patients with MF and highlight the lack of biomarkers correlating with skin responses. Finally, we explore emerging tools and consider their potential to improve clinical decision-making when differentiating between biological and clinical responses.

papers.title: Integrated Network Toxicology and Multi-Omics Reveal Budesonide-Induced Immunotoxicity Mechanisms in Zebrafish Embryos.
papers.authors: Liu S, He Z, Zhang J, Yang H, Han C, Li Q, Gong J, Cui M.
papers.abstract: Budesonide (BDN), a widely used synthetic glucocorticoid and emerging aquatic contaminant, is increasingly detected in surface waters; however, its system-level immunotoxicity mechanisms remain poorly understood. This study integrated network toxicology, molecular dynamics, transcriptomics, and metabolomics to elucidate BDN-induced immunotoxicity in zebrafish embryos. In silico toxicity profiling consistently identified immunotoxicity as the dominant hazard endpoint of BDN. Network toxicology analysis predicted 14 immunotoxicity-associated protein targets, among which MAPK1 emerged as a previously unrecognized moderate-affinity target in addition to the canonical glucocorticoid receptor (GR). Molecular docking and 100-ns molecular dynamics simulations indicated stable and specific binding between BDN and MAPK1. This computational prediction was experimentally validated by microscale thermophoresis, which confirmed direct interaction with a dissociation constant of 55.5 μM and supported a non-canonical mechanism of action. Transcriptomic and metabolomic profiling of embryos exposed to 100 and 1000 ng/L BDN revealed dose-dependent alterations in the expression of immune regulatory networks. Integrated pathway analysis across computational predictions and multi-omics datasets consistently converged on arachidonic acid metabolism as the central perturbed pathway. RT-qPCR validation of eight immune-related genes (il1b, fkbp5) confirmed significant dysregulation at concentrations as low as 1 ng/L, within the range reported for surface waters. BDN has been proposed to induce immunotoxicity primarily through GR-dependent transcriptional reprogramming, with secondary or non-canonical contributions from direct interference with MAPK signaling; these mechanisms may converge on lipid mediator-driven inflammatory pathways. This study not only provides novel mechanistic insights into the immunotoxicity of BDN but also establishes a scalable, integrative strategy for elucidating the mechanisms of action of emerging aquatic micropollutants.

papers.title: Antibody-drug conjugates: unpacking toxicity profiles and optimized designs for enhanced safety and antitumor efficacy.
papers.authors: Yin Y, Fan L, Wan R, Sun B, Xiong B, Zhuang W, He D, Bai H, Wang J.
papers.abstract: Antibody-drug conjugates (ADCs) have expanded treatment options across multiple malignancies, but their clinical benefit remains constrained by heterogeneous and sometimes serious toxicities. These toxicities rarely arise from a single component; instead, they reflect the association between target biology, molecular architecture, systemic exposure, and tissue susceptibility. We first examine the structural basis of ADC toxicity by discussing the distinct contributions of the antibody-target axis, linker, payload, drug loading, and conjugation strategy to systemic exposure and tissue toxicity. We distinguish organ-selective "on-target, off-tumor" injury from target-independent toxicity and further characterize two major off-target routes: context-dependent uptake of intact ADCs through Fcγ receptor-mediated or pinocytosis-dominant pathways, and spatially distinct exposure to released payload arising from premature systemic release or localized bystander diffusion. Furthermore, we summarize a multidisciplinary management framework, ranging from prophylactic measures to graded interventions across complex scenarios such as treatment rechallenge and combination therapy. Finally, we discuss strategies to widen the therapeutic window through exposure-response-guided dosing, next-generation molecular engineering, and emerging conjugate platforms. Artificial intelligence and computational approaches may further extend safety optimization from drug design to patient stratification and real-world surveillance. By linking molecular design, spatial exposure, and clinical management, this review provides an integrated framework to improve ADC safety while preserving antitumor efficacy.

papers.title: A Biologically Optimized PEG-IFN-α2 Variant Exhibits Potent Anti-HBV and Immunomodulatory Efficacy.
papers.authors: Ashuo A, Ye J, Jia R, Li Y, Chen Y, Fang Z, Wang MZ, Chen J, Yuan Z.
papers.abstract: Human interferon-alpha (IFN-α) includes 13 subtypes, but only IFN-α2 (a/b) is clinically approved for chronic hepatitis B (CHB) therapy, limited by adverse effects and suboptimal response rates. Previously, we identified IFN-α14 as a superior anti-HBV subtype compared to IFN-α2, leading to the engineering of the IFN-α2-EIFK variant, which mimics IFN-α14's enhanced antiviral activity through targeted mutations at receptor-binding sites. However, the in vivo anti-HBV effects of IFN-α2-EIFK remained unexplored due to its short plasma half-life and lack of immunocompetent murine systems suitable for evaluating human IFN-α activity. Using an immunocompetent IFNAR-hEC mouse model and HBV-infected human-liver chimeric mice etc, we demonstrated that N-terminally PEGylated IFN-α2-EIFK (PEG-IFN-α2-EIFK) suppressed HBV replication and antigen expression approximately 10-fold more effectively than PEG-IFN-α2 at equivalent mass doses, while concurrently activating IFN-γ-like signaling pathways in both hepatocytes and immune cells. Subsequent single-cell analysis of intrahepatic immune cells from IFNAR-hEC mice showed that PEG-IFN-α2-EIFK was associated with enhanced antigen-presenting capacity of macrophages, dendritic cells (DCs), and B cells. In addition, PEG-IFN-α2-EIFK was found to preferentially promote M1-like macrophage polarization, and modulate PD-L1/PD-1 interactions between macrophages and CD8 + T cells, accompanied by attenuation of an exhaustion-associated CD8 + T cell state. In conclusion, this study demonstrates that PEG-IFN-α2-EIFK exhibits greater anti-HBV activity and immunomodulatory potency than PEG-IFN-α2 under equivalent mass dosing, supporting its potential as an enhanced therapeutic candidate for CHB.

papers.title: A transcriptional and cellular exploration of obesity and type II diabetes in human adipose tissues.
papers.authors: Trim WV, Petrova K, Healy K, Stevens BM, Scanlan JG, Faust HJ, Svensson Akusjärvi S, O'Brien KL, O'Shea D, Brenner MB, Heneghan H, Lynch L.
papers.abstract: Obesity is tightly linked to metabolic disorders such as type II diabetes mellitus (T2D), although a subpopulation of individuals with obesity do not present with these morbidities. The biological factors conferring T2D vulnerability remain incompletely understood. We recruited 58 individuals with obesity with or without a clinical diagnosis of T2D (Ob + T2D and Ob). We profiled paired samples of omental and subcutaneous adipose by single-cell RNA sequencing ( n = 10), flow cytometry under basal and stimulated conditions ( n = 42), and histology ( n = 17). Flow cytometry and chemokine quantification were also performed in paired whole blood. We identified reprogramming of the omental stromal compartment, centered on mesothelial and endothelial cells, alongside contrasting innate T cell and macrophage phenotypes across depots. Mesothelial and IGFBP2 + cells exhibited a fibrotic, epithelial-mesenchymal transition-like phenotype, while omental endothelial cells exhibited a lipid-overload, inflammatory, antigen presentation profile in T2D. Omental and subcutaneous adipose innate T cells exhibited divergent inflammatory profiles between tissues. These findings reveal previously unidentified insights into the pathophysiology of T2D in adipose tissue and identify compensatory networks within the tissues that could be exploited by targeted therapeutics.

papers.title: Predicting key viral mutations from within-host deep sequencing data.
papers.authors: Su S, Tang YS, Li Q, Cao L, Zhang Y, Lou J, Zheng H, Liu C, Sun Y, Li J, Zhang Z, Zee BC, Cheung PPH, Chen Z, Chan RWY, Wu WKK, Yu J, Yen HL, Gu H, Man Poon LL, Hui DS, Hiscox JA, Mok CKP, Wang MH.
papers.abstract: Rapid SARS-CoV-2 evolution drives continuous epidemic waves, harming vaccine protection and exerting heavy burden to population health. Predicting virus evolution holds the key for current and future medical countermeasures against infectious diseases by allowing well-matching vaccines and timely epidemic response. However, due to its high genetic diversity, fast transmissibility and evolutionary rate, accurate and timely prediction of SARS-CoV-2 evolution remains a challenge. To address this, we developed a computational framework, Beth-2, to predict key mutations of SARS-CoV-2 through analyzing within-host viral genome deep sequencing data. We leveraged the early fitness signals of variants exhibited within-host and their fitness pattern between-host to infer the emerging mutations with fitness potential. In retrospective data validation, 98.6% of the key SARS-CoV-2 mutations on receptor binding domain could be detected by our model with a median lead time of 9 mo before they reached predominance at population level. Among the 26 prospectively predicted mutations, 69% of them exhibited significantly enhanced transmissibility and five showed significant immune escape from plasma of subjects who received COVID-19 mRNA vaccine collected 6 mo after the prediction time. The mutations predicted by Beth-2 that are functionally enhanced include F456L, the defining mutation of multiple current circulating lineages, including KP.3, NB.1.8.1, and XFG. The model captures mutations of high fitness potential under the natural immune environment of host and is applicable to other pathogens. The framework can be implemented along with the existing genome surveillance network and offers an efficient and effective instrument for vaccine preparation and epidemic response.
papers.venue: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America

papers.title: An information-theoretic framework for inferring T cell dynamics from single-cell RNA and T cell receptor sequencing.
papers.authors: Ceglia N, Salehi S, Sethna ZM, Elhanati Y, Freeman SS, Lyudovyk O, Burman B, Chow A, Zamarin D, DeWolf S, Shahid S, Bojilova V, Rusk N, Balachandran VP, McPherson A, Shah SP, Greenbaum BD.
papers.abstract: Single-cell T cell receptor (TCR) repertoire sequencing enables simultaneous profiling of gene expression and TCR sequences, providing a coregistered measure of T cell phenotypic diversity and clonal dynamics. However, principled probabilistic frameworks for joint modeling of clonotype and phenotype have remained limited. Here we introduce TCRi, a hierarchical Bayesian information-theoretic framework that infers the joint probability distribution between genetic clonotype and transcriptional phenotype from paired single-cell transcriptomic and TCR sequencing data. TCRi treats phenotype assignment as a probabilistic inference problem: a variational autoencoder embeds single-cell expression into a structured latent space, and a hierarchical Bayesian model learns clonotype-specific phenotype distributions through principled information-sharing across clonotypes, patients and covariates. From these distributions, TCRi computes information-theoretic quantities: clonotypic entropy, phenotypic entropy, phenotypic flux and mutual information between clonotype and phenotype. When TCRi was applied to four real-world datasets comprising 167,118 CD8 T cells from patients with cancer treated with anti-PD-(L)1 immune checkpoint blockade, mutual information emerged as a robust discriminator of therapeutic response.

papers.title: Dysregulated CSF T-cell responses and their evolution after intravenous immunoglobulin in Guillain-Barré syndrome.
papers.authors: Morrison AH, Yao T, Isfort MC, Morena J, Liu T, Roell J, Akkaya B, Kolb SJ, Bell EH, Saligrama N, Segal BM.
papers.abstract: Guillain-Barré syndrome (GBS) is an acute immune-mediated neuropathy that frequently results in long-term disability. The cellular mechanisms underlying GBS and the immunomodulatory effects of intravenous immunoglobulin (IVIg) remain incompletely understood. In this prospective observational cohort study, we performed single-cell RNA sequencing with paired T cell receptor (TCR) sequencing on peripheral blood and cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) collected before and after IVIg treatment from treatment-naïve patients with GBS. Pre-treatment blood and CSF were obtained from nine and eight patients, respectively; post-treatment samples were available from six patients for blood and three patients for CSF. Previously published healthy control (HC) blood and CSF single-cell datasets were analyzed for comparison. We characterized immune cell composition, transcriptional states, TCR clonality, and clonal dynamics across peripheral and CSF compartments as well as following treatment. Individuals with GBS exhibited enrichment of T helper 1 (Th1)-polarized CD4+ T cells, activated and resident-memory CD8+ T cells, and macrophages in CSF relative to paired peripheral blood. This CSF-to-blood enrichment was greater than in healthy controls (HCs) for Th1 cells, activated effector-memory CD8+ T cells, and inflammatory macrophages, although the overall degree of T-cell clonal expansion was similar between groups. In both GBS and HCs, expanded CSF CD4+ clonotypes were predominantly Th1-polarized and largely absent from blood, whereas expanded CD8+ clonotypes showed greater overlap between compartments. Among clonotypes detected in both blood and CSF, CD4+ and CD8+ T cells exhibited more activated transcriptional states in the CSF, a shift that was particularly pronounced in GBS. Following IVIg treatment, peripheral blood showed minimal changes, whereas CSF T-cell populations exhibited more substantial alterations, including reductions in Th1-associated and activated effector-memory states, increases in T helper 2 (Th2) and regulatory T cell populations, and changes in the clonal repertoire. Expanded T cell clonotypes with sequence-based predicted specificity for pathogens associated with GBS were identified in six patients, and convergent clonotype groups were detected both within and across patients. Demyelinating GBS is characterized by compartmentalized enrichment and activation of pro-inflammatory T-cell populations within the CSF rather than an overall increase in T-cell clonal expansion. Exploratory longitudinal findings further suggest that CSF T-cell populations are altered following IVIg treatment. Integrated single-cell transcriptomic and TCR analyses provide insight into the early immune response in GBS and identify candidate cellular pathways for biomarker development and therapeutic investigation.

papers.title: Antigen-driven CD8+ T cell activation drives the immunopathogenesis of myasthenia gravis-associated myocarditis.
papers.authors: Chen H, Zhang N, Shi Z, Zhang Y, Du Q, Wang R, Wang X, Zhou H.
papers.abstract: Purpose Myasthenia gravis-associated myocarditis (MG-myocarditis) is a life-threatening condition. However, the immune dysregulation underlying its pathogenesis remains poorly defined. This study aimed to delineate the immunological pathways driving myocarditis development in patients with MG. Methods We performed integrated single-cell RNA sequencing and paired T cell receptor (TCR) repertoire profiling on peripheral blood mononuclear cells (PBMCs) from 3 patients with MG-myocarditis and 4 patients with MG-only. Analyses were conducted to characterize transcriptional states, differentiation trajectories, clonal expansions, and antigen-specific signatures associated with MG-myocarditis. Results Although the overall proportions of major PBMC lineages did not differ significantly between groups, transcriptomic profiling revealed substantial numbers of significantly differentially expressed genes across multiple immune cell subsets. Classical CD14+ monocytes displayed a marked skewing toward a pro-inflammatory differentiation trajectory, accompanied by downregulation of the Activator Protein-1-high intermediate state associated with anti-inflammatory programming. Within the T cell compartment, MG-myocarditis was characterized by robust expansion of TCR clonotypes concurrently enriched in CD8+ effector memory with high EOMES expression and CD8+ effector subsets, indicative of recent or ongoing antigen-driven activation.TCR-peptide binding prediction analysis showed preferential reactivity of these expanded clonotypes toward cardiac proteins-including Titin, MYO10, and MYH6-implicating antigen-specific cytotoxicity in myocardial injury. In parallel, non-classical CD16+ monocytes and conventional dendritic cells (cDCs) exhibited enhanced antigen-presenting signatures, marked respectively by S100A8 upregulation and LY6E downregulation. Conclusion Our findings identify non-classical CD16+ monocytes and cDCs as potential cardiac antigen-presenting populations capable of priming pathogenic CD8+ T cell responses, thereby contributing to the immunopathogenesis of MG-associated myocarditis.

papers.title: A Spatial Multiomics Atlas and Resource for Immune-Fibrotic Niches in Chronic Kidney Allograft Dysfunction.
papers.authors: Gao Q, Ke Z, Xu W, Zheng M, Wang B, Ding R, Liu J, Hang Z, Yu Z, Ni K, Su H, Du M, Jiang M, Ye D, Tan R, Gu M, Wang Z, Gui Z.
papers.abstract: Chronic allograft dysfunction (CAD) is a major cause of late kidney-allograft failure, yet its spatially organized cellular and metabolic mechanisms remain poorly resolved because human biopsies are scarce and experimental models are imperfect. Here, we established a tacrolimus-modulated accelerated mouse model of CAD and constructed a cross-species multiomics atlas by integrating mouse single-cell RNA sequencing, flow cytometry, and multiplex imaging with human single-nucleus RNA sequencing, Visium HD spatial transcriptomics, and spatial metabolomics. Cross-species analysis revealed conserved immune, stromal, epithelial, and myeloid programs and delineated 2 anatomically distinct fibrotic niches. Cortical fibrosis was associated with endothelial/pericyte remodeling, altered cholesterol-biosynthesis transcriptional programs, and reduced regional cholesterol-related signals. Medullary fibrosis was enriched for proximal-tubule S3 [PT(S3)] cells with glycolysis-associated remodeling, increased regional lactate-related signals, and adjacent tissue-resident memory T-cell domains displaying an atypical exhaustion-like program. Glutamine/glutamate metabolism-associated programs accompanied inferred monocyte-to-macrophage state remodeling. In renal tubular epithelial cells, 2-deoxy-D-glucose partially attenuated transforming growth factor-β1-induced E-cadherin loss and α-smooth muscle actin induction, providing focused functional support for glycolysis-associated tubular remodeling. We additionally provide an exploratory kidney-transplant multiomics resource for data visualization, auxiliary summarization of platform-derived results, and gene/pathway querying. Together, this study provides a spatially resolved, cross-species framework for identifying candidate immune-metabolic mechanisms and prioritizing experimentally testable targets in CAD.
