papers.title: Cross-lineage mesenchymal transition in mesothelioma.
papers.authors: Wu L, de Perrot M.
papers.abstract: Mesothelioma is characterized by extreme cellular plasticity, profound stromal remodeling, and near-universal resistance to therapy. While epithelial-mesenchymal transition (EMT) has long been implicated in disease progression, mesothelioma arises within a uniquely heterogeneous cellular ecosystem in which multiple non-epithelial lineages contribute to mesenchymal states. Here, we introduce cross-lineage mesenchymal transition (XMT) as a unifying framework describing the convergence of epithelial, mesothelial, endothelial, immune, hematopoietic, adipocytic, neural, and stem-like cells toward fibroblast-like, extracellular-matrix-producing phenotypes. Mesothelioma is presented as a conceptual framework for studying convergent mesenchymal programming and XMT-related processes, rather than as a definitively proven example of XMT. XMT is driven by shared signaling axes, including TGF-β, Wnt/β-catenin, Notch, hypoxia, and mechanotransduction pathways that erase lineage identity and reinforce mesenchymal programs. Recurrent mesothelioma-associated genomic alterations, particularly loss of BAP1 and CDKN2A, further potentiate XMT by reshaping chromatin accessibility, cell cycle control, metabolic state, and inflammatory signaling, thereby lowering barriers to lineage plasticity. Integrative bulk and single-cell transcriptomic analyses reveal that XMT-associated gene signatures correlate with stromal enrichment, immunosuppressive myeloid and regulatory T cell infiltration, and poor survival in patients with pleural mesothelioma. XMT underlies mesothelioma desmoplasia, immune evasion, and therapy resistance, and represents a tractable vulnerability for stromal, immune, and plasticity-directed therapeutic strategies. Framing mesothelioma through the lens of XMT provides a unifying biological rationale for stromal evolution and identifies actionable pathways-genetic, epigenetic, and microenvironmental mechanisms that may be targeted to overcome plasticity-driven disease progression. This review highlights specific therapeutic strategies, including stromal-targeted approaches aimed at TGF-β signaling and extracellular matrix remodeling, immune-targeted approaches that address myeloid-driven immunosuppression and inflammatory signaling, and plasticity-directed strategies targeting EMT/stemness programs and cellular state transitions.

papers.title: A triptolide-associated prognostic model for personalized treatment stratification in pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma.
papers.authors: Xie H, Deng M, He H, Liang J, Li J.
papers.abstract: Pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) lacks effective stratification tools to guide therapy. This study explores the potential of triptolide-associated biology in developing a prognostic model for risk stratification and treatment guidance. By integrating computational target predictions with TCGA and ICGC transcriptomic cohorts, we identified differentially expressed triptolide-associated genes. A gene prognostic signature was developed using Cox regression and SHAP-based feature ranking, followed by comprehensive immune landscape and in silico drug-sensitivity profiling. We identified a core six-gene prognostic signature comprising AADAC, BTNL9, ADGRF1, AQP2, F5, and H2AC6. This model demonstrated exceptional predictive accuracy, with 1-, 3-, and 5-year AUC values of 0.759, 0.748, and 0.741 in the training set, and consistent performance in the validation cohort (0.626, 0.677, and 0.703). High-risk patients were characterized by a classic "immune-cold" microenvironment, showing enrichment of M0 macrophages and upregulated immune checkpoints (BTLA, PDCD1, TIGIT). TIDE analysis further revealed that high-risk patients exhibited an "immune-excluded" phenotype characterized by elevated Exclusion and MDSC scores. Furthermore, high-risk patients showed higher sensitivity to paclitaxel and erlotinib, while low-risk patients were more responsive to axitinib and metformin. Molecular docking confirmed stable, high-affinity binding between triptolide and all six target proteins, providing a biophysical basis for the model. Single-cell analysis revealed that the six genes are primarily expressed in endothelia, ductal cells and acinar cells. IHC staining confirmed an enhancement in AADAC, AQP2, ADGRF1, and H2AC6 protein levels in PDAC lesions. This six-gene signature serves as a prognostic model for PDAC risk stratification, with its constituent genes computationally predicted to interact with triptolide, provideing a testable hypothesis for future mechanistic exploration.

papers.title: Integrative molecular profiling of TAM receptors and STAT-SOCS signaling in thymic epithelial tumors.
papers.authors: Oner DA.
papers.abstract: Thymic epithelial tumors (TETs) are rare, molecularly heterogeneous tumors with a complex immune microenvironment. How TAM receptor signaling interacts with STAT-SOCS-mediated immune regulation in TETs remains incompletely understood. The TAM receptor family and STAT-SOCS signaling were examined in relation to genomic alterations, gene expression, survival, and the immune microenvironment, using TCGA-THYM genomic, transcriptomic, and clinical data integrated with GTEx normal thymus expression profiles. Expression of TAM receptors (AXL, MERTK, TYRO3), their ligands (GAS6, PROS1), and the STAT1-SOCS1/SOCS3 axis was assessed using GEPIA2; survival associations were evaluated using GEPIA2 and patient-level TCGA-THYM data, and immune infiltration using TIMER2.0. Cell-type expression of TAM pathway genes was assessed using TET single-cell RNA-seq data, and protein-protein interactions using STRING. Genomic alterations affecting the TAM-STAT-SOCS axis were infrequent, comprising missense variants and copy-number amplifications. AXL, MERTK, PROS1, GAS6, STAT1, and SOCS1 showed higher expression in tumor tissues than in normal thymus. Higher MERTK expression was associated with poorer overall survival in the GEPIA2 analysis, although not significant in WHO-stratified and multivariable analyses. AXL, MERTK, and TYRO3 expression were inversely correlated with CD4 + and CD8 + T-cell infiltration, whereas GAS6, PROS1, STAT1, and SOCS3 were positively associated with neutrophil infiltration. MERTK expression was positively correlated with CD274, and single-cell analysis showed MERTK was most frequent in macrophage/monocyte populations. TAM-STAT-SOCS expression was associated with the TET immune landscape, with MERTK showing an initial association with overall survival and further associations with T-cell infiltration, CD274 expression, and cell-type-specific expression patterns.

papers.title: Spatial architecture of the synovium identifies clinically relevant phenotypes of osteoarthritis.
papers.authors: Tsubaki T, Miyahara J, Arino Y, Naoi Y, Kawaguchi K, Kono K, Yamagami R, Taketomi S, Ishikura H, Kasai T, Ennishi D, Tanaka S, Saito T, Chijimatsu R.
papers.abstract: Objectives Osteoarthritis (OA) is a heterogeneous joint disease characterized by marked variability in etiology and clinical symptoms. We aimed to determine whether spatial organization of synovial tissue underlies clinically relevant heterogeneity in knee OA. Methods We developed a deep learning-based semantic segmentation framework to analyze hematoxylin and eosin-stained whole-slide images of human synovium. Spatial entropy and inter-tissue connectivity metrics were incorporated to evaluate local pathology. We further applied graph neural network-based community modeling to classify tissue structures based on their microenvironment. Results The model identified key OA-associated histological features, including synovial lining hyperplasia, immune cell infiltration, angiogenesis, and fibrotic remodeling. Quantitative analysis of tissue composition revealed that enrichment of dense fibrous tissue was associated with poorer postoperative outcomes. However, tissue proportion alone did not adequately capture baseline disease status. Inter-tissue connectivity-based analysis showed that enrichment of Lining-Micro vessel interactions was associated with lower preoperative KOOS Symptom scores, indicating more severe symptoms, and elevated synovitis scores. Using features derived from graph neural network-based modeling, Micro vessels segregated into two distinct communities, one enriched in adjacent lining structures and another associated with immune-rich regions, and their relative abundances varied among knee OA patients. Integration with matched synovial single-cell RNA sequencing data showed increased predicted interactions between lining fibroblasts and endothelial cells in the Lining-Micro vessel-rich phenotype. These interactions were enriched for angiogenesis-related VEGF and ANGPTL signaling, providing supportive evidence for a distinct fibroblast-endothelial signaling state. Conclusions These findings indicate that the spatial organization of synovial architecture, beyond simple tissue composition, captures clinically relevant heterogeneity in knee OA and links histological microenvironments to cell-cell communication networks.

papers.title: Migraine-driven causal genes in ischemic stroke.
papers.authors: Zhang Z, Lin P, Ni H, Li Y, Wei J, Zhang J, Dai Z, Liu Y, Han L, Lin J.
papers.abstract: Migraine, most notably migraine with aura, elevates the risk of ischaemic stroke, though the underlying causal molecular connections have not been fully elucidated. This study sought to uncover migraine-associated causal genes that confer susceptibility to ischaemic stroke and to dissect their cell-type-specific functional mechanisms operating within the neurovascular unit. We combined publicly available human transcriptomic resources, genetics-driven causal inference, machine-learning-assisted biomarker screening, mouse-derived single-cell and spatial transcriptomic atlases, immune-cell deconvolution, and in-silico molecular docking. Twenty migraine-related genes were detected with causal associations to ischaemic-stroke risk. We prioritised three consensus hub genes: CD79A, PKN2, and PRKDC. In stroke patients, CD79A was significantly downregulated, while PKN2 and PRKDC exhibited elevated expression; their reliable diagnostic capacity was further confirmed in an independent external cohort. Single-cell and spatial transcriptomic profiling mapped these hub genes to endothelial, myeloid and glial cell populations residing within a dynamic inflammatory-vascular pathological niche in mouse ischaemic brain lesions. Mechanistic analyses pointed to perturbed mitochondrial energy homeostasis and dysregulated adaptive immune responses as downstream consequences modulated by these hub genes. Molecular-docking simulations demonstrated high-affinity interactions between Tamibarotene, Dirithromycin and the three encoded hub proteins, highlighting these compounds as promising candidates for drug repurposing. Collectively, our multi-omics analysis pinpoints CD79A, PKN2 and PRKDC as migraine-derived causal targets for ischaemic stroke, delivers cell- and spatial-resolved mechanistic perspectives on neurovascular-unit injury, and puts forward lead compounds awaiting further pre-clinical validation.
papers.venue: Neurotherapeutics : the journal of the American Society for Experimental NeuroTherapeutics

papers.title: Stromal APOL4 defines a cancer-associated fibroblast state that organizes a chemosensitive niche in ovarian cancer.
papers.authors: Lim SO, Park J, Lee K, Kim M, Lee J, Lee JW, Lee DW, Kang HJ, Lee JK.
papers.abstract: Despite initial high response rates to platinum-based chemotherapy in high-grade serous ovarian carcinoma, most patients eventually develop resistance, and the contribution of the tumor microenvironment to treatment outcomes has remained underexplored relative to tumor cell-intrinsic mechanisms. Combining patient-derived ex vivo carboplatin screening with bulk and single-cell transcriptomics, functional perturbation in cancer-associated fibroblasts (CAFs), and high-resolution spatial transcriptomics, we identified stromal apolipoprotein L4 (APOL4) as a biomarker of platinum sensitivity. The ex vivo classification showed directional concordance with clinical platinum response, and stromal APOL4 expression predicted favorable outcomes across multiple validation cohorts. APOL4 specifically marked a transcriptionally distinct CAF subtype (CAF-1) that extended beyond canonical CAF states and exhibited high matrix metalloproteinase and immune-activating cytokine expression. APOL4 knockdown attenuated the CAF-1 transcriptional program, and in 3D tumor-CAF co-cultures conferred carboplatin resistance to 12 of 14 ovarian cancer cell lines, providing causal evidence that stromal APOL4 supports platinum sensitivity in a tumor cell-extrinsic manner. NicheNet analysis revealed bidirectionally asymmetric communication: CAF-1 engaged non-stressed cancer cells through epithelial integrity-supporting axes, whereas other CAFs preferentially reinforced stressed, drug-tolerant cancer cells through canonical chemoresistance circuits. High-resolution Xenium spatial transcriptomics revealed a contact-restricted spatial association between CAF-1 proximity and reduced cancer-cell stress, defining a low-stress, immune-infiltrated niche that is spatially and compositionally distinct from the stress-enriched, immune-poor niche associated with CAF-2, with CAF-3 sharing features of both compartments. These findings identify stromal APOL4-CAF-1 as a prognostic biomarker and a functional contributor linking stromal matrix remodeling to platinum sensitivity and associated with an immune-infiltrated microenvironment, highlighting CAF-1-targeted strategies to enhance chemotherapy efficacy.

papers.title: In vivo CAR-T double knockout screen maps synergistic antitumour gene pairs.
papers.authors: Zhou L, Renauer PA, Tang K, Li S, Luo Z, Feng Y, Lin SH, Zhang F, Park D, Fang SY, Vest G, Zhao Z, Dorst W, Yang L, Dong C, Pan X, Klemm L, Yi SS, Sahni N, Peng L, Müschen M, Zhou X, Chen S.
papers.abstract: Chimeric antigen receptor (CAR)-T cell therapy has transformed the treatment of haematological malignancies, but its efficacy remains limited by multiple negative regulatory mechanisms intrinsic to T cells 1-4 . Here we perform a high-throughput in vivo CAR-T double-knockout (DKO) CRISPR screen, and identify multiple DKO gene pairs that are both effective and synergistic. The top pair, NR4A1-SOCS3 DKO, has multiple favourable immunological features. Whole-transcriptome profiling and in vivo single-cell RNA sequencing reveal that NR4A1-SOCS3 DKO specifically upregulates metabolic pathways in CAR-T cells, which show significantly higher metabolic fitness and mitochondrial activity. NR4A1-SOCS3 DKO CAR-T cells and T cells exhibit exceptionally potent antitumour efficacy and long-term tumour control across different tumour models without compromising safety features. NR4A1-SOCS3 DKO outperforms several benchmark single-gene and dual-gene modifications in T cells and CAR-T cells 5-9 . These data demonstrate high-throughput in vivo CAR-T DKO screening for rapid discovery of combination targets, and establish NR4A1-SOCS3 as a promising pair of intracellular checkpoints to engineer high-performance CAR-T therapies against cancer.

papers.title: Venousization enables angiogenesis in the absence of VEGFR signalling.
papers.authors: Garcia-Gonzalez I, Rocha SF, Oliveira FV, Sanchez-Muñoz MS, Lytvyn M, Garcia-Cabero A, Ipe U, Graupera M, Mäkinen T, Benedito R.
papers.abstract: The vascular endothelial growth factor (VEGF) ligand and its main receptor VEGFR2 are considered to be essential for endothelial differentiation, proliferation, sprouting and survival 1 . Blood vessels cannot form in growing embryos or tissues when VEGF-VEGFR2 signalling is compromised in all cells 2,3 . The anti-VEGF antibody, which can block angiogenesis in cancer, wound healing or ischaemic diseases, is among the most widely used antibodies in the clinic. However, vascular resistance to anti-VEGF therapy has been reported 4,5 . Here we used iFlpMosaics and iSuRe-HadCre to induce and track genetic mosaics of endothelial cells (ECs) lacking VEGFR2 during the entire embryonic and postnatal development. These Vegfr2-knockout (Vegfr2 KO ) ECs adapted, proliferated normally and competed with wild-type cells over time, eventually forming a substantial portion of the vascular network in most organs. Vegfr2 KO ECs could not sprout during the first wave of angiogenesis in most tissues, because this process is highly VEGF-dependent and favours growth and mobilization of wild-type ECs. However, owing to their inability to respond to VEGF, Vegfr2 KO ECs became dominant in veins, which represented a long-term and continuous source of ECs for subsequent waves of VEGF-independent angiogenesis. Comparative single-cell RNA sequencing analysis of ECs with acute and long-term loss of VEGFR2 identified both common and organ-specific molecular mechanisms of adaptation and resistance to VEGF signalling loss. These included significant endothelial venousization and upregulation of ligands for VEGFR1 and VEGFR3. VEGFR1 only partially compensated for VEGFR2 loss in capillary ECs, whereas VEGFR3 compensated only in arterial ECs. Loss of the three VEGF receptors did not compromise venous growth. Notably, loss of the master regulator of venous development, NR2F2 (also known as COUP-TFII), significantly compromised expansion of Vegfr2 KO ECs. This work has implications for our understanding of the role of VEGF receptors in angiogenesis and demonstrates venousization as a mechanism of adaptation and resistance to VEGF signalling loss during angiogenesis.

papers.title: TWEAK signaling drives the transition from psoriasis to atopic dermatitis-like inflammation in paradoxical eczema.
papers.authors: Marella S, Bogle R, Zhang H, Fox J, Kirma J, Xing X, Klein B, van Drongelen V, Feister Z, Zagairy F, Hamed M, Liaks M, Ziv M, Jiang R, Dey P, Kahlenberg JM, Billi AC, Tsoi LC, Gudjonsson JE, Barak EC.
papers.abstract: Targeted biologics have transformed the treatment of inflammatory skin diseases such as plaque psoriasis. However, some patients with psoriasis paradoxically develop eczematous skin reactions after therapy targeting tumor necrosis factor (TNF), interleukin-17 (IL-17), or IL-23. Although paradoxical eczema (PE) resembles atopic dermatitis (AD) clinically and histologically, the molecular mechanisms that drive its development remain poorly understood. Here, we generated high-resolution cellular and spatial maps of human skin using single-cell RNA sequencing, spatial transcriptomics, immunohistochemistry, and in vitro assays, profiling lesional biopsies from patients with PE ( n = 8 donors), alongside healthy control, psoriasis, and AD skin ( n = 4 donors per group). In PE, we identified distinct transcriptional changes characterized by myeloid and T cell expansion and an altered keratinocyte phenotype shaped by TNF-like weak inducer of apoptosis (TWEAK; encoded by TNFSF12 ) signaling through its receptor TNFRSF12A , confirmed at the protein level by immunohistochemistry. To define the underlying mechanism, we stimulated immortalized (N-TERT) and primary human keratinocytes and found that TWEAK acted together with IL-13 to drive a T helper 2- and type I interferon-polarized epithelial program that partially recapitulated the keratinocyte signature of PE lesions. We validated key target genes by quantitative polymerase chain reaction in primary keratinocytes. In THP-1 cells and primary human CD14 + monocytes, anti-TNF treatment induced TWEAK expression, suggesting a compensatory inflammatory circuit. Together, these findings identify the TWEAK-IL-13 axis as a key driver of PE and suggest how cytokine blockade may reshape cutaneous immune responses.

papers.title: Synthetic nanobodies for drug discovery-Design, construction, optimization, and applications.
papers.authors: Xie Y, Tian Z, Wen Y, Zheng F.
papers.abstract: Nanobodies (Nbs) are single-domain antibody fragments derived from camelid heavy-chain-only antibodies (HCAbs). Nbs can be readily produced in microbial expression systems and are widely used as research tools while also being actively explored for diagnostic and therapeutic applications. Nbs are traditionally isolated from either immune libraries generated through camelid immunization or naïve libraries constructed from nonimmunized donors. The development of synthetic Nb libraries has transformed this paradigm by eliminating the need for animal immunization and accelerating every stage of Nb discovery-including library design, construction, selection, and optimization-through integrated in vitro and computational approaches. Compared with conventional immune libraries, synthetic libraries provide greater experimental control, broader target coverage, and increased flexibility for generating binders against challenging or predefined targets. This review summarizes current strategies for the design, construction, optimization, and application of synthetic Nbs, with particular emphasis on advances in library engineering, computational design, and their emerging roles in biomedical research and drug discovery.

papers.title: Protein nanocages: Programmable biomaterial platforms for therapeutics, bioimaging, and diagnostics.
papers.authors: Shin J, Jung S, Lee AS, Kim CS.
papers.abstract: Protein nanocages are monodisperse, hollow structures formed through the symmetric self-assembly of protein subunits. Their genetically encoded architectures combine the geometric precision of nanoscale assemblies with the intrinsic biocompatibility and functional versatility of naturally evolved proteins. Well-defined internal cavities and engineerable interior and exterior surfaces enable the spatial organization of therapeutic cargoes, molecular recognition elements, and bioactive components within a single nanoscale platform. In this Review, we examine the structural organization, self-assembly mechanisms, physicochemical properties, and functional diversity of representative protein nanocages, including ferritin, the pyruvate dehydrogenase E2 core, DNA-binding proteins from starved cells (Dps), small heat shock proteins (sHSPs), encapsulins, and lumazine synthase. We discuss how their structural features and assembly behavior govern biological performance and support biomedical applications in targeted drug delivery, cancer immunotherapy, vaccine development, and in vivo and in vitro diagnostics. Beyond describing individual platforms, we establish a unifying framework that positions protein nanocages as programmable molecular organizers and highlights five transferable design principles: multivalent ligand display, spatial compartmentalization, receptor-guided targeting, reporter organization and signal enhancement, and stimulus-responsive cargo release and functional activation. We also examine persistent challenges in structural stability, immunogenicity, scalable manufacturing, and clinical translation, alongside emerging opportunities in protein engineering, synthetic biology, and computational protein design. Collectively, these principles establish protein nanocages as versatile biomaterial platforms for integrating sensing, targeting, imaging, and therapy within a single molecular architecture, providing a foundation for next-generation precision nanomedicine. STATEMENT OF SIGNIFICANCE: Reviews typically treat protein nanocages individually, obscuring shared structural features and the extent to which design strategies transfer across systems. This Review addresses this gap by establishing a comparative framework spanning structurally diverse nanocages and distilling their similarities into a concise set of generalizable design principles. It reframes protein nanocages not merely as passive delivery vehicles but as programmable molecular scaffolds that organize cargo with controlled spatial arrangement and stoichiometry. This framework provides biomaterials researchers with a transferable basis for engineering protein assemblies for precision nanomedicine while identifying key challenges in structural stability, immunogenicity, and scalable manufacturing that must be addressed to facilitate clinical translation.

papers.title: Single-cell profiling reveals monocyte mitochondrial dysfunction in patients with cirrhosis progressing to acute-on-chronic liver failure.
papers.authors: Wirtz TH, Palomino-Echeverria S, Pollmanns MR, Huergo E, Schreibing F, Reißing J, Sánchez-Garrido C, López-Vicario C, Aransay AM, Baldassare M, Zaccherini G, Pompili E, McCoy MS, Uschner FE, Klein S, Gu W, Schierwagen R, Valainathan S, Verbeeck A, Campion D, Giovo I, Schneider KM, Koch A, Kramann R, Bruns T, Kiani N, Stiles L, Caraceni P, Alessandria C, Moreau R, Trebicka J, Clària J, Planell N, Rautou PE, Trautwein C, Gomez-Cabrero D.
papers.abstract: Background & aims Patients with acute decompensation (AD) of cirrhosis are at a high risk of developing acute-on-chronic liver failure (ACLF), a syndrome characterized by multi-organ failure and high short-term mortality. Prospective studies addressing the cellular mechanisms that drive the transition from AD to ACLF are lacking. In this study, we aimed to determine whether peripheral immune cell subsets at hospital admission predict the progression from AD to ACLF and to delineate underlying molecular mechanisms. Methods We prospectively enrolled 63 patients with AD and 15 healthy donors across five European centres, with a 90-day follow-up. Single-cell RNA sequencing was performed on peripheral blood mononuclear cells (PBMCs) from 16 patients with distinct trajectories and 4 controls. Results Progression to ACLF was associated with expansion of classical monocytes, particularly subcluster "C2", which specifically displayed impaired energy metabolism with reduced oxidative phosphorylation (p Conclusions We identified and validated a distinct monocyte subpopulation with defective energy metabolism in patients with AD with poor outcomes, supporting a link between monocyte bioenergetic dysfunction and ACLF development. Impact and Implications:The cellular mechanisms that drive progression from acute decompensation (AD) to acute-on-chronic liver failure (ACLF) remain poorly understood, limiting the development of effective strategies for therapeutic intervention. By integrating prospective single-cell transcriptomics, functional bioenergetic analyses, and validation in independent multicentre cohorts, we identified a distinct monocyte subset characterized by impaired oxidative phosphorylation that is associated with subsequent ACLF development. These findings are relevant to clinicians and researchers because they suggest that immune-metabolic dysfunction emerges before overt ACLF and may contribute to disease progression. While further mechanistic and prospective validation studies are required, our results provide a framework for the investigation of monocyte bioenergetics as a potential therapeutic target in patients with decompensated cirrhosis.

papers.title: Cancer-induced changes in systemic intravascular monocyte dynamics revealed by MRI single cell tracking in a murine breast cancer model.
papers.authors: Havlas A, Fredrich IR, Wilken E, Wachsmuth L, Kuhlmann M, Geyer C, Hoffmann E, Jürgens R, Vogl T, Faber C, Helfen A, Masthoff M.
papers.abstract: Objectives In cancer, monocytes with patrolling-like behavior have been associated with antitumoral effects, but their intravascular motion is currently concealed to noninvasive imaging techniques. This study aimed to evaluate systemic monocyte intravascular patrolling-like behavior during tumor growth, immunotherapy, and splenectomy, using single-cell tracking with preclinical time-lapse brain magnetic resonance imaging (MRI). Materials and methods In a murine syngeneic breast cancer model (4T1, 67NR), time-lapse MRI (repetitive T2*-weighted gradient-echo sequence after in vivo labeling with iron oxide nanoparticles for monocyte detection) of the brain was conducted using a 9.4 T small animal MRI. Control mice were either naive or received sham injections. Additionally, time-lapse MRI was conducted during immunotherapy or following splenectomy in tumor-bearing and tumor-free mice. Individual cells were identified as hypointensities. Tumors were harvested for ex vivo analysis. Results The number of detected cells within the brain, distant from the tumor, changed during cancer growth. The cell count was significantly lower for tumor-bearing mice compared to controls. In mice bearing 4T1 tumors, the cell count was significantly lower on day 1 and 9 compared to mice bearing 67NR tumors. During immunotherapy, the monocyte count was significantly lower compared to control, but only in the presence of a tumor. Splenectomy reduced the tumor-associated effect on monocyte dynamics in both low- and highly malignant tumors. Conclusion Based on an exemplary murine breast cancer model, both cancer and immunotherapy change systemic intravascular monocyte patrolling-like behavior early during tumor growth distant from the tumor, an observation that is dependent on the grade of malignancy and the presence of splenic reservoirs. Key points Question Do tumors alter systemic intravascular monocyte dynamics during tumor growth, immunotherapy, and splenectomy at distant sites, and can such changes be detected noninvasively? Findings In murine breast cancer, time-lapse MRI revealed reduced monocyte patrolling-like behavior during tumor growth and immunotherapy, influenced by malignancy grade and splenic reservoirs. Critical Relevance Noninvasive single-cell MRI tracking provides novel insights into systemic immune dynamics in cancer, potentially enabling future monitoring of tumor-immune interactions, therapeutic responses, and immune modulation beyond conventional assessment of tumor burden or tumor microenvironment composition.

papers.title: Autophagy-Active Immune Cell Cluster and Crucial Gene Expression in Nonunion Via Single-Cell Sequencing and Functional Enrichment Analysis.
papers.authors: Zhao G, Sun L, Li D, Wang Q, Li Z, Zhang K, Duan N, Lu Y.
papers.abstract: Fracture nonunion represents a great challenge for orthopedic clinicians. This study aimed to identify autophagy-active immune cell clusters and key genes associated with nonunion progression using single-cell profiles and RNA-seq data. scRNA-seq profiles related to femoral nonunion were derived from the GEO database, and cell cluster annotation was subsequently performed. The AUCell package was utilized to calculate active cells based on autophagy gene expression, and cell communication was analyzed using CellChat. Twenty-one distinct cell clusters were identified from the nonunion tissues, which were annotated into 14 major cell types, and macrophages exhibited the highest AUCell score. Intercellular communication analysis revealed that the total number and intensity of overall cell interactions in the nonunion were notably increased compared with normal tissue. Furthermore, three ligand-receptor pathways (SPP1, MIF, and FN1) were notably altered between M1 macrophages and multiple other cell types, including endothelial cells, fibroblasts, pericytes, and NK cells. By combining the scRNA-seq and transcriptomic analyses, 21 key genes were identified, of which 12 genes, including CCL8, CDO1, and CEBPD, showed potential discriminatory ability for nonunion (AUC > 0.9). Moreover, the PPI network, ceRNA network, and mRNA-TF network were established to predict co-expression molecules. The results highlight the pivotal role of autophagy-active macrophages in nonunion and identify altered ligand-receptor pathways and 21 key DEGs associated with disease progression.

papers.title: 18 F-FGln PET/CT Imaging of Glutamine Uptake Has Potential for Predicting Immunotherapy Response in Hepatocellular Carcinoma.
papers.authors: Liu Y, Li J, Pan X, Xu X, Huang X, He S, Zhang J, Liu F, Song S.
papers.abstract: We investigated whether glutamine (Gln) uptake, imaged by 18 F-(2S,4R)-4-fluoroglutamine ( 18 F-FGln) PET/CT, could predict and modulate immunotherapy response in hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC). Analysis of the Cancer Genome Atlas (TCGA)-Liver Hepatocellular Carcinoma (LIHC) dataset revealed that SLC1A5 expression-which encodes a primary Gln uptake channel in HCC cells-was significantly associated with poor prognosis, higher tumor grade, and an immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment. In murine HCC models, tumors with high 18 F-FGln uptake exhibited elevated Slc1a5 expression and poor response to anti-PD-1 therapy, whereas low-uptake tumors were more sensitive to immunotherapy. Genetic knockdown of Slc1a5 reduced 18 F-FGln uptake, enhanced anti-PD-1 efficacy, increased cytotoxic T lymphocyte infiltration, and decreased regulatory T cell abundance. Transcriptomic and single-cell analyses revealed activation of antitumor immune pathways and reprogramming toward an immune-inflamed phenotype after Slc1a5 suppression. V-9302 decreased tumor Gln uptake, as measured by 18 F-FGln PET/CT, and sensitized HCC to PD-1 blockade. In patient-derived organoid-T cell co-culture systems, low-SLC1A5 organoids were susceptible to PD-1 blockade, whereas high-SLC1A5 organoids were resistant, consistent with 18 F-FGln PET/CT findings. These results identify Gln uptake as a checkpoint of immune evasion in HCC and support that 18 F-FGln PET/CT has the potential to predict and monitor immunotherapy response.

papers.title: An integrated MRI-pathology model for predicting response to TACE combined with targeted therapy and immunotherapy in hepatocellular carcinoma.
papers.authors: Ding W, Hua HJ, Shen X, Yan HT, Dong ZN, Zu QQ, Fan WL, Zhou CG, Liu S, Feng ZL, Wang WD, Shi HB, Zhang JX.
papers.abstract: Objectives The efficacy of transarterial chemoembolization (TACE) plus targeted therapy and immunotherapy in unresectable hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) is limited by variable responses. We aimed to develop and validate an integrated magnetic resonance imaging (MRI)-pathology model for response prediction and survival stratification (IMPRESS), which combines pretreatment MRI habitat radiomics and paired biopsy whole-slide images (WSIs) pathomics. Materials and methods This multicenter, retrospective study enrolled patients with unresectable HCC receiving TACE plus targeted therapy and immunotherapy from January 2019 to December 2024. Eligibility required pretreatment MRI and paired biopsy WSIs within 1 month before therapy, Child-Pugh class A/B, Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) performance status ≤ 1, and at least one measurable intrahepatic lesion ≥ 1 cm. Patients with missing or poor-quality MRI or WSIs, prior locoregional or systemic HCC therapy, second malignancy, ECOG ≥ 2, or incomplete data were excluded. Habitat MRI radiomics, WSI pathomics, and clinical features were integrated into IMPRESS. Model performance was evaluated using the area under the curve (AUC) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs). Single-cell analysis was performed to explore the biological basis of the IMPRESS predictions. Results Among 231 patients, 94 (40.7%) achieved a treatment response. IMPRESS achieved AUCs of 0.957 (95% CI: 0.931-1.0), 0.878 (95% CI: 0.789-0.966), and 0.875 (95% CI: 0.782-0.966) in the training, validation, and test cohorts, respectively. Predicted responders and non-responders showed significantly different overall survival in all cohorts (all p Conclusion IMPRESS model may provide a promising tool for pretreatment response prediction and survival risk stratification in unresectable HCC undergoing TACE-based combination therapy. Key points Question Reliable pretreatment tools are needed to identify unresectable HCC patients likely to benefit from TACE plus targeted therapy and immunotherapy. Findings An integrated MRI-pathology model combining habitat radiomics and deep-learning pathomics predicted treatment response, with validation and testing areas under the curve of 0.878 and 0.875. Clinical relevance The integrated model may support pretreatment response stratification for TACE-based triple therapy and help inform surveillance intensity or alternative treatment considerations, pending prospective validation.

papers.title: Senescent CD8 T effector memory cells are functionally impaired, enriched in aging and disease, and a barrier to immunotherapy.
papers.authors: Turano PS, Akbulut E, Aquino NM, Garza-Martínez L, Singh S, Aviv A, Toupance S, Yap GS, Fitzgerald-Bocarsly P, Martínez-Zamudio RI, Herbig U.
papers.abstract: Senescent cells play important roles in various biological processes that promote fitness and health; however, their timely elimination by immune cells is critical to maintain tissue homeostasis and prevent disease. Despite this, senescent cells accumulate systemically with age, suggesting that certain immune cells also become senescent and dysfunctional during aging. In support of this, we previously demonstrated that CD8 T cells, immune cells capable of targeting senescent cells, increasingly develop characteristics of senescence with advancing age in humans. Here, we characterized the senescence state of human SA-βGal-expressing (SA-βGal high ) CD8 T effector memory (EM) cells, their functional capabilities, and their enrichment in aging and disease. Single-cell RNA sequencing revealed that SA-βGal high CD8 T cells with unique transcriptional signatures develop in all stages of T cell differentiation, including in CD8 T EM cells, which increased in abundance with human aging. SA-βGal high CD8 T EM cells expressed various classical markers of senescence and were significantly impaired in their ability to proliferate, produce cytokines, and eliminate senescent human stromal cells. Gene signatures of senescent SA-βGal high CD8 T EM cells were enriched in CD8 T cells from older human donors, patients with age-related disorders, cancer, and in smokers. Furthermore, we show that T cell senescence is distinct from and dominant over T cell exhaustion, limiting the response of CD8 T EM cells to immune checkpoint blockade. Collectively, our study demonstrates that senescence impairs CD8 T EM cell function and reveals the involvement of senescent and dysfunctional CD8 T EM cells in aging, disease, smoking, and responses to immunotherapy.

papers.title: Making sense of TILs: recommendations for morphological assessment of tumour-infiltrating lymphocytes in colorectal carcinoma: a report on behalf of the International Immuno-Oncology Biomarker Working Group.
papers.authors: Sur D, Lang-Schwarz C, van Herpe F, Rasschaert G, Weeda YA, Littlefield N, Gu Q, Li N, Alexandros H, Hida AI, Bhalla A, Khramtsov AI, Ehinger A, Tanaka A, Acs B, Steen S, Ercan C, Focke CM, Ehinger D, Huang D, Sheng W, Khramtsova GF, Nishida H, Sevim S, Ichihara S, Morikawa S, Michiels S, Papathomas T, Haga T, Kervadec H, Horlings HM, Sanchez-Vega F, Janjigian JY, Chalabi M, van Laarhoven HW, Kodach LL, Meijer SL, Williams DS, Gill AJ, Loi S, Salgado R, Vieth M.
papers.abstract: Tumour-infiltrating lymphocytes (TILs) are recognized as critical components of the colorectal cancer (CRC) immune microenvironment, demonstrating significant prognostic and predictive implications. However, a clear and widely accepted definition of colorectal TILs has not yet been established, and TILs are not systematically used as biomarkers in current oncology practice. This highlights the need for standardized assessment methods and a deeper understanding of the complex role of TILs in CRC, necessitating collaborative work to achieve clinical importance. This report, on behalf of the International Immuno-Oncology Biomarker Working Group (ITWG), provides a comprehensive overview of TILs in CRC, including a TILs-assessment method. It details their multifaceted role of TILs within the tumour microenvironment, details current and emerging methods for their assessment and reviews their prognostic and predictive importance. The report also explores the relationship of TILs to other established and emerging biomarkers in CRC. Emerging trends, including AI-driven analysis for automated TIL quantification, and single-cell and spatial technologies for in-depth characterization of the tumour microenvironment (TME), are also highlighted. The report concludes with a discussion of future directions and the ongoing efforts of the ITWG to address the challenges and standardize and advance the clinical application of TIL assessment in CRC.

papers.title: CDH3-directed immunotherapy targets basal-like hormone receptor negative prostate cancer and breast cancer.
papers.authors: Liu G, Wang S, Zeng Z, Duong L, Yang J, Barupala N, Zhao Y, Rahmy S, Feng S, Chi X, Arce A, Jia L, Wan J, Cheng L, Lu X, Lu X.
papers.abstract: Basal-like double-negative prostate cancer (DNPC) and triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC) are aggressive tumors with few targeted treatment options, raising the question of whether a shared, druggable cell-surface antigen can be leveraged for effective immunotherapy. Here, we integrated analyses of independent bulk and single-cell transcriptomic datasets with mechanistic and preclinical therapeutic studies to evaluate CDH3 (P-cadherin) as a candidate target in basal-like disease. CDH3 expression was consistently enriched in basal-like subtypes across prostate and breast cancer cohorts and was preferentially expressed in basal epithelial tumor compartments. Mechanistically, CDH3 expression was governed by a YAP1-WNT5A/ROR2 signaling axis, linking basal subtype gene expression to non-canonical Wnt signaling. To exploit this target, we evaluated both a CDH3-directed antibody-drug conjugate (ADC) and CDH3-specific chimeric antigen receptor (CAR)-T cells. The ADC exhibited antigen-dependent internalization and cytotoxicity in vitro and reduced metastatic tumor burden in vivo. CDH3 CAR-T cells showed antigen-specific activation and tumor cell killing in vitro and improved tumor control and survival in metastatic prostate and breast cancer xenograft models, with additional benefit when combined with PD-1 blockade (nivolumab). Together, these findings establish CDH3 as a clinically relevant and therapeutically actionable target and support CDH3-directed ADC and CAR-T strategies for aggressive, basal-like DNPC and TNBC.

papers.title: Cellular and spatial continuum of TAM functional states governs immune exclusion and dictates immune checkpoint resistance in melanoma.
papers.authors: Chakraborty S, Corrales E, Godbole I, Madkhali N, Das T, Krolla C, Nystrom A, Meiss F, Rafei D, Bengsch B, Andrieux G, Boerries M.
papers.abstract: Background Immune checkpoint inhibitor (ICI) therapy has transformed melanoma treatment, yet many patients either fail to respond or develop resistance after an initial response. The cellular and spatial determinants within the tumor microenvironment (TME) that underlie these divergent ICI therapy outcomes remain poorly defined. Here, we aimed to characterize the immune composition and spatial organization of the TME associated with ICI response and resistance. Methods We integrated public scRNA-seq data (N = 32) with in-house spatial transcriptomics and imaging mass cytometry from an independent melanoma cohort (N = 6) to achieve high-resolution spatial profiling of the TME. This multimodal approach allowed us to map cellular heterogeneity within discrete spatial neighborhoods. To validate our findings, we constructed a scRNA-seq derived signature-matrix and deconvoluted a bulk RNA-seq cohort (N = 334). Clinical associations were assessed using Kaplan-Meier survival analysis, Cox hazard models, and a machine-learning classifier. Results We identified a distinct tumor-associated macrophage (TAM) state, termed lipid-associated TAMs (LA-TAMs), characterized by conserved lipid metabolic programs and tumor-specific adaptations in glycolysis under hypoxic conditions. Deep spatial multi-omics profiling revealed divergent immune architectures associated with treatment outcomes. In non-responder patients, LA-TAMs colocalized with sparsely distributed TIM3⁺ exhausted CD8⁺ T cells within an immune-excluded TME. In contrast, responder patients harbored interferon-primed CCL4 + TAMs (IFN-TAMs) spatially associated with Granzyme B⁺ activated CD8⁺ T cells, reflecting an immune-active microenvironment. These findings define contrasting macrophage-centered immune neighborhoods linked to ICI response. Interestingly, patients with LA-TAM-enriched neighborhoods were consistently non-responders or progressed during follow-up, irrespective of the presence of IFN-TAM neighborhoods. Lastly, we constructed a single-cell-derived signature matrix that estimates TAM fractions from bulk RNA-seq data and revealed LA-TAM abundance as a robust, independent predictor of poor ICI response and survival in a validation cohort. Conclusions Our study defines the spatial landscapes of TAM-heterogeneity in melanoma and identifies LA-TAM neighborhoods as an important feature of ICI resistance. Although patients span a continuum of TAM-centered immune states, the presence of LA-TAM is likely to diminish the beneficial effects of IFN-TAM-associated immune activation. Finally, our proposed Melanoma-TME-derived signature-matrix provides a translatable framework to robustly predict ICI response and resistance.

papers.title: eNAMPT is a plasma biomarker of COVID-19 severity and ARDS progression linked to increased immune effector cell expression.
papers.authors: Canizales Galaviz J, Khan A, Tourki B, Patarroyo-White S, Johnson NH, Arjona A, Bime C, Knox KS, Mirsaeidi MS, Juan Guardela B, Herazo-Maya JD, Casanova NG, Garcia JGN.
papers.abstract: Background The COVID-19 pandemic highlighted the critical unmet need for novel targets, biomarkers, and effective pharmacotherapies to reduce the severity/mortality of COVID pneumonia and progression to acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS). Extracellular NAMPT (eNAMPT) is a druggable DAMP and TLR4 ligand centrally involved in ARDS pathobiology. We explored the utility of plasma eNAMPT measurements as a potential COVID-19 biomarker linked to ARDS progression and disease severity and investigated the potential cellular source for eNAMPT release/secretion in COVID-19 subjects. Methods A plasma biomarker panel of inflammatory cytokines (IL-1β, IL-6, IL-8, IL-1RA, TNF-α), DAMPs (eNAMPT, MIF) and vascular proteins (ANG-2, PSGL-1) were evaluated in three distinct COVID-19-positive cohorts (Miami, Arizona, Tampa) (n = 277) and healthy control subjects (n = 214). Single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) publicly available on peripheral blood mononuclear cells (PBMCs) in a subset of Tampa COVID-19 survivors (n = 18) and an autopsied COVID lung tissue database was separately analyzed for biomarker gene expression. Results Plasma biomarkers, including eNAMPT were significantly elevated in COVID-19 subjects compared to healthy controls (p Conclusion Our study corroborated the utility of this biomarker panel for diagnostic and severity assessment in COVID-19- associated ARDS and as a strategy for subject stratification in therapeutic trials of eNAMPT-neutralizing therapies. We further identified NAMPT expression in immune effector cells that correlates with COVID-19 severity and lethality. Together, these findings suggest NAMPT plays a key role in sustaining inflammatory activation and impairing lung regeneration in fatal COVID-19.

papers.title: Investigating the Expression and Function of PPP2R1A in Hepatocellular Carcinoma: A Multi-Omics Analysis with in vitro Validation.
papers.authors: Tan J, Zeng Y, Wu H, Liang Y, Qiu Y, Mo Q, Luo Y, He J, Wang Y, Yin H, Chen P, Li M, Lin H.
papers.abstract: Background Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) remains difficult to diagnose early and to treat effectively. Protein Phosphatase 2A Regulatory Subunit Aα ( PPP2R1A ), the scaffolding (Aα) subunit of the PP2A holoenzyme, is altered in several cancer types, but its expression pattern, functional significance, and translational relevance in HCC are incompletely understood. Methods Public transcriptomic, single-cell, and spatial transcriptomic datasets (TCGA-LIHC, GTEx, GEO, ICGC-LIHC, HPA, TISCH2) and drug-sensitivity databases were integrated to characterize PPP2R1A expression and its associations with survival, biological pathways, and tumor immune infiltration in HCC. Functional effects of PPP2R1A knockdown were assessed in Huh7 cells by RT-qPCR, CCK-8, Transwell, flow-cytometric cell-cycle, and β-galactosidase assays. Results PPP2R1A was significantly overexpressed in HCC tissues relative to normal liver and was also elevated across several other cancer types. High PPP2R1A expression was associated with shorter overall and disease-specific survival in Kaplan-Meier analysis, although it was not an independent prognostic factor after multivariate adjustment (hazard ratio [HR] = 1.051, p = 0.789). PPP2R1A expression correlated positively with transcriptional programs related to cell cycle, MYC, EGFR, MAPK, and WNT signaling, and negatively with p53 pathway activity. At single-cell and spatial resolution, PPP2R1A was enriched in malignant cells and in tumor regions, and its expression correlated with the abundance of several computationally inferred immune cell populations. PPP2R1A knockdown in Huh7 cells reduced proliferation and invasion, induced G2-phase arrest, and decreased MYC, CDK1, and CCNB1 mRNA expression without inducing senescence. Drug-sensitivity screens suggested candidate agents, such as AT-7519, that warrant further investigation in PPP2R1A -high HCC. Conclusion PPP2R1A is consistently overexpressed in HCC and contributes to the malignant phenotype at least partly through cell-cycle regulation. These findings are hypothesis-generating, and the potential diagnostic, prognostic, or therapeutic value of PPP2R1A in HCC requires dedicated prospective and functional validation.

papers.title: Identification and Validation of Autophagy- and Inflammatory-Related Genes in Childhood Asthma via Integrated Bioinformatics and Clinical Samples.
papers.authors: Huang M, Wu J, Xu D.
papers.abstract: Childhood asthma (CA) is a prevalent chronic airway disease, yet the roles of autophagy and inflammation in its pathogenesis remain poorly understood. Transcriptomic datasets were retrieved from the Gene Expression Omnibus (GEO). Inflammation- and autophagy-related genes were identified using weighted gene co-expression network analysis and consensus clustering and intersected with differentially expressed genes (DEGs) to identify candidate genes. Subsequently, 101 machine learning algorithm combinations were evaluated to select key genes for diagnostic model construction. Functional characterization involved immune infiltration analysis, gene set enrichment analysis, and transcription factor network construction. Mendelian randomization (MR) was used to assess potential causal relationships between key genes and CA, and gene expression was validated by quantitative polymerase chain reaction (qPCR) in clinical blood samples. The analysis identified 39 candidate genes associated with autophagy and inflammation. Machine learning identified 10 key genes, and the resulting diagnostic model achieved areas under the curve of 0.768, 0.751, and 0.710 in the training, test, and validation sets, respectively. Pathway and immune infiltration analyses revealed enrichment in signaling, metabolic, and immune-regulatory functions and significant correlations with immune cell infiltration. MR analysis suggested a potential causal association between genetically predicted STYXL1 expression and CA risk. qPCR analysis in five CA patients and five healthy controls showed expression patterns consistent with the transcriptomic findings. However, the small clinical validation cohort limits the generalizability of these results. This study identifies a 10-gene peripheral blood diagnostic signature associated with CA and highlights STYXL1 as a potential causal risk gene supported by genetic evidence. Larger clinical cohorts and functional studies are required to validate these findings.

papers.title: RAPGEFL1 as a Novel Prognostic Biomarker Correlated with Immune Infiltration and Drug Sensitivity in Kidney Renal Clear Cell Carcinoma.
papers.authors: Wan L, Zheng Z, Zhong H, Zhu H, Lao M, Peng W, Chen Y.
papers.abstract: The aim of the study was to examine the clinical expression, prognostic value, and clinical treatment of Rap Guanine Nucleotide Exchange Factor Like 1 (RAPGEFL1) in kidney renal clear cell carcinoma (KIRC). Three GEO datasets, together with RNA-seq and clinical data from TCGA (541 KIRC and 72 normal tissues), were analyzed. Bioinformatics techniques included differential expression, survival (Kaplan-Meier, Cox regression), pathway enrichment (GSEA), immune infiltration (ssGSEA), stemness index (mRNAsi), and drug sensitivity analysis. Quantitative reverse transcription polymerase chain reaction (qRT-PCR) was used to validate RAPGEFL1 expression in KIRC cell lines (OSRC-2 and A-498) compared with normal HK-2 cells. RAPGEFL1 was significantly upregulated in KIRC (p < 0.001) and showed high diagnostic value (AUC = 0.904). High expression independently predicted worse overall (HR = 2.05, p < 0.001), progression-free (HR = 1.50, p = 0.011), and disease-specific survival (HR = 2.30, p < 0.001). Multivariate Cox regression further identified RAPGEFL1 as an independent prognostic factor for overall survival (HR = 2.21, p < 0.001). It was associated with metabolite pathways, including oxidative phosphorylation and PPAR signaling, and decreased immune infiltration (T cells, macrophages), high immune checkpoints (CTLA4, LAG3), diminished stemness, and altered drug sensitivity (e.g., increased response to docetaxel). qRT-PCR revealed that it is overexpressed in KIRC cells. RAPGEFL1 overexpression identifies an aggressive KIRC subclass and may inform future personalized treatment strategies, including targeted therapy and immunotherapy, pending further validation. This study is the first to comprehensively characterize RAPGEFL1 as a prognostic biomarker in KIRC through integrative bioinformatics and experimental validation, revealing its dual role in immune modulation and drug response prediction.

papers.title: Cell-specific responses to copper stress and cuproptosis in renal fibrosis.
papers.authors: Wang X, Sun X, Yao X, Jiang Y, Liu W, Geng D, Xia P, Wei M.
papers.abstract: Renal fibrosis is a common pathological feature of progressive chronic kidney disease (CKD). Its development involves persistent injury to resident renal cells, inflammation, myofibroblast activation, and excessive accumulation of extracellular matrix (ECM). Renal fibrosis is not driven by a single cell type but results from sustained interactions among resident renal cells, infiltrating immune cells, matrix-producing fibroblasts, and other cell populations. Within this multicellular context, cuproptosis, a recently described form of copper-dependent cell death, may contribute to the onset and progression of renal fibrosis by amplifying inflammation, fostering a profibrotic microenvironment, and promoting ECM deposition during kidney injury. Elevated intracellular copper alone, however, is insufficient to trigger cuproptosis. Cellular susceptibility also depends on metabolic state, mitochondrial function, and mitochondrial protein lipoylation. Because renal cell types differ substantially in these biological features, the effects of cuproptosis-related stress are likely to vary across cell populations. This review aims to systematically elucidate the essential prerequisites underlying cuproptosis and its role in renal fibrosis from the perspective of cell type specificity. In particular, we highlight the heterogeneity of renal tubular epithelial cells, podocytes, endothelial cells, immune cells, and fibroblasts in terms of energy metabolism, reliance on mitochondrial function, copper-handling capacity, and protein lipoylation to discuss how these differences may give rise to distinct injury patterns and pathological consequences of cuproptosis-related stress. Finally, this review summarizes potential therapeutic strategies targeting copper homeostasis and cuproptosis-related stress to attenuate renal fibrosis, offering new directions for understanding the mechanisms of renal fibrosis and developing more cell-specific interventions.

papers.title: A novel preclinical platform to study FGFR2 fusion-driven cholangiocarcinoma ☆ .
papers.authors: Wolf A, Facciuto M, Damiecki M, Bramel ER, Park E, Young SE, Torres M, Nath S, Mazzaferro V, Schwartz M, Lujambio A, Hopkins BD, Tsankov AM, Tocheva A, Sia D.
papers.abstract: Background & aims FGFR2 fusions represent the most frequent genetic alteration in intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma (iCCA). However, clinical responses to FGFR inhibitors are suboptimal. A major limitation is that preclinical models do not mimic the immunobiology of human FGFR2-driven iCCA. We developed an autochthonous and immunocompetent FGFR2 fusion-driven mouse model. Methods Using the hydrodynamic tail-vein injection method, we generated a mouse model harboring the FGFR2-PPHLN1 fusion (with or without the V565F resistance mutation) in combination with activated YAP1, and established 2D lines and 3D organoids. We characterized tumors using bulk and single cell RNA-sequencing (n=3), spectral cytometry (n=3-7/group), and performed cross-species analysis using 411 human samples. Tumor-associated neutrophils (TAN) were depleted in vivo using an anti-murine Ly6G antibody. In vitro and in vivo drug treatment with FGFR inhibitors and anti-PD-L1 was performed. Results FGFR2-driven murine tumors were molecularly and immunologically similar to human iCCA, with selective accumulation of TAN and impaired T cell infiltration. scRNA-seq identified pro-tumorigenic and immunomodulatory TAN subsets while In vivo TAN depletion significantly prolonged survival (log-rank p=0.009) and led to increased CD8 + T cells infiltration (p=0.007). 3D organoids reproduced clinical responses to irreversible FGFR inhibitors, while showing a sustained response to the reversible inhibitor derazantinib in presence of the V565F mutation (IC50=5.190uM). In vivo derazantinib reduced tumor number (unadj. p=0.03) and marginally prolonged survival (unadj. p=0.052) whereas no statistically significant benefit of anti-PD-L1 was detected, either alone or in combination. Conclusions Our mouse model faithfully recapitulates the immunobiology and therapeutic sensitivities of the human disease. Inter-species and cross-species analyses suggest a critical role of FGFR2 fusions in shaping a cold tumor microenvironment with selective accumulation of TAN in both humans and mice. Impact and implications This study develops a clinically-relevant mouse model of FGFR2-driven iCCA for future translational studies. Accumulation of pro-tumorigenic and immunomodulatory TAN along with poor sensitivity to immune checkpoint inhibitors suggests the need of designing alternative strategies harnessing the unique immunosuppressive nature of these tumors.

papers.title: Toxicological effects of acetyl tributyl citrate exposure on the progression of uterine fibroids and cervical cancer.
papers.authors: Wei Z, Wu Y, Li M, Sa S, Liu J, Wei K.
papers.abstract: Background Uterine fibroids (UFs) and cervical cancer (CC) are two common gynecological tumors, the pathogenesis of which has not yet been fully elucidated, with environmental factors playing a significant role. Acetyl tributyl citrate (ATBC), a widely used plasticizer, has been proven to pose a threat to human health. Although studies have indicated that ATBC exposure may be associated with tumorigenesis, the specific roles and molecular mechanisms of ATBC in UFs and CC remain unclear. Objective This study aims to investigate the molecular mechanisms of ATBC-related UFs and CC using network toxicology, machine learning, and multidimensional bioinformatics approaches. Methods Network toxicology methods were used to identify the relevant targets of ATBC, UFs, and CC. Gene Ontology and Kyoto Encyclopedia of Genes and Genomes enrichment analysis were employed to explore the potential target gene pathways of ATBC-related UFs and CC. Transcriptomics analysis, Least Absolute Shrinkage and Selection Operator, and Support Vector Machine - Recursive Feature Elimination algorithms were used to determine the core targets of ATBC-related UFs and CC, and the discrimination of core genes among them was evaluated by receiver operating characteristic curve. Immune infiltration analysis was used to analyze the relationship between the expression of core target genes and the infiltration levels of various immune cells, while molecular docking and in vitro cell experiments were used to validate the above results. Results We identified 12 targets related to UFs and 153 targets related to CC, of which 11 were common targets for UFs and CC, significantly enriched in the ERBB signaling pathway and oxidative stress response pathway. F10, ABCB1, MMP9, CDK2, PIK3CA, and GABRA2 were identified as the core targets of ATBC-related UFs, while CDK2 and DHFR were identified as the core targets of ATBC-related CC. Among them, CDK2 is a cross-disease hub target for UFs and CC. In UFs tissues (MMP9, GABRA2, and CDK2) and CC tissues (CDK2 and DHFR), the expression of these genes was significantly higher than that in normal tissues. These genes were significantly associated with immune cell infiltration. Molecular docking and in vitro cell experiments results confirmed the stable interactions between ATBC and these targets. Conclusion This study reveals that some key targets play important roles in the relationship between ATBC and UFs and CC, providing new insights into the mechanisms of ATBC in gynecological tumors and offering potential targets for future prevention and treatment strategies.

papers.title: Next-Generation Cancer Nanovaccines: Reprogramming the Tumor Microenvironment from Rational Design Toward Clinical Translation.
papers.authors: Tabibzadeh S, Meng F, Asghariazar V, Safarzadeh E, Esmaeili A, Ten Hagen TLM, Farhoudi L, Cai Y.
papers.abstract: Cancer vaccines have emerged as a promising immunotherapeutic strategy for inducing durable and tumour-specific immune responses; however, their clinical efficacy remains limited by poor antigen immunogenicity, inefficient delivery, tumor heterogeneity, and the highly immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment (TME). Recent advances in nanotechnology have expanded opportunities for the rational engineering of multifunctional nanoparticle (NP) platforms that can protect therapeutic cargo, enhance antigen presentation and lymphatic transport, co-deliver immunostimulatory adjuvants, and potentially improve immune modulation while reducing systemic exposure. This narrative review provides an overview of next-generation cancer nanovaccines, including lipid-, polymer-, peptide-, inorganic-, biomimetic-, theranostic, in situ-, and stimuli-responsive platforms, with emphasis on their physicochemical design principles, mechanisms of immune activation, and interactions with the TME. Particular attention is given to strategies targeting tumor -associated macrophages, myeloid-derived suppressor cells, regulatory T cells, cancer-associated fibroblasts, and tumor cells to support dendritic-cell maturation, cytotoxic T-cell activation, and anti-tumor immunity. Emerging personalized approaches, including neoantigen- and autologous cell-based nanovaccines, mRNA vaccine platforms, and combinations with immune checkpoint inhibitors, are also discussed. In addition, we examine the growing role of artificial intelligence, machine learning, and computational immunology in neoantigen prioritization, nanoparticle formulation optimization, immunogenicity prediction, and patient-specific vaccine design. Despite encouraging preclinical findings, most cancer nanovaccine platforms remain at the preclinical or early clinical stage, and translation is limited by tumor heterogeneity, variable immune responses, long-term safety and biodistribution concerns, manufacturing reproducibility, scale-up, and regulatory requirements. Overall, the integration of nanotechnology, immunology, precision medicine, and AI offers considerable potential to advance personalized cancer vaccination, but broader clinical validation and standardized manufacturing and evaluation frameworks are required before these platforms can achieve routine clinical application.

figure.label: Figure 1
figure.caption: Evolution of cancer nanomedicine and nanovaccine platforms. The timeline highlights major advances in nanotechnology relevant to cancer therapy, progressing from early nanoparticle-based drug delivery systems, including Doxil and Abraxane, to more advanced targeted, stimuli-responsive, and mRNA-based nanovaccine platforms. The lower panel summarizes key functional advantages of nanovaccines, including enhanced antigen stability and presentation, targeted delivery, co-delivery of antigens and adjuvants, and controlled modulation of anti-tumor immune responses.

papers.title: Identification and validation of circadian rhythm-related diagnostic biomarkers for endometriosis through integrating machine learning and single-cell analysis.
papers.authors: Chen D, Xu L, Cheng L, Su A.
papers.abstract: Background Endometriosis (EMs) is a chronic inflammatory disease, and the lack of candidate molecular biomarkers remain a major clinical challenge. Circadian rhythm disruption plays a non-negligible role in EMs. However, the diagnostic potential of circadian rhythm-related biomarkers remains insufficiently validated. Methods We performed weighted gene co-expression network analysis to screen for endometriosis-related hub modules. Four machine learning algorithms were used for feature selection in the training cohort, and the resulting diagnostic model was evaluated in three independent GEO validation cohorts. To evaluate the immune microenvironment, we applied MCPcounter, CIBERSORT, and single-sample gene set enrichment analysis. Single‑cell RNA‑seq data were processed with Seurat for cell clustering and annotation, cell‑cell communication networks were constructed using CellChat, and pseudotime trajectory analysis was performed with Monocle. Results SMC2, SUV39H2, and TIMELESS were identified as candidate molecular biomarkers, demonstrating favorable diagnostic performance across three independent validation sets. Computational immune infiltration analysis suggested higher enrichment scores for B cells and CD8 + T cells, along with lower scores for Tregs and NK cells in EMs samples. Single-cell analysis revealed an increased proportion of mesenchymal cells in EMs samples and altered cell-cell communication involving BMP, CHEMERIN, and GRN signaling pathways. Pseudotime analysis further suggested transcriptional relationships among distinct stromal cell populations. Conclusion This study identified SMC2, SUV39H2, and TIMELESS as candidate tissue-based molecular biomarkers for EMs and revealed alterations in stromal cell populations and immune-related features associated with the disease.
papers.venue: European journal of obstetrics, gynecology, and reproductive biology

papers.title: Tumor Immune Microenvironment Heterogeneity and Key Immunoregulatory Gene Expression in Lung Cancer.
papers.authors: Mao J, Zhang X, Yang R, Wang X.
papers.abstract: Background The aim of this study is to characterize the cellular heterogeneity and key immunoregulatory gene expression patterns of the tumor immune microenvironment (TIME) in lung cancer using single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq). Methods The scRNA-seq dataset GSM4453577 was retrieved from NCBI GEO. Unsupervised clustering, cell-cell communication analysis, pseudotime trajectory reconstruction, and GO/KEGG enrichment analyses were performed. Results Seven immune cell types were annotated from 223 single cells after quality control. Macrophages demonstrated the strongest outgoing intercellular interaction intensity and showed relatively high SPP1-associated expression-based interaction scores, with macrophages and monocytes identified as the dominant SPP1 signal sources. ISG15 showed the broadest expression across all seven immune cell types (highest z-scores in stem-like/mast cells and neutrophils), whereas TNFRSF18 and TNFRSF4 exhibited similar descriptive expression trends during intermediate pseudotime stages (scaled 0-1), with TNFRSF18 enriched in stem-like/mast cells ( z = 1.93) and TNFRSF4 in mast cells ( z = 2.22). T cell, NK cell, and Treg markers (CD3E, NKG7, and FOXP3) were below the detection threshold, consistent with the predominantly myeloid/B-lineage immune infiltrate in this sample. Conclusion ScRNA-seq analysis of a single GEO sample (GSM4453577; 223 cells; PC1 explaining 5.3% of variance) suggested myeloid/B-lineage immune cell heterogeneity in the lung cancer microenvironment and identified ISG15, TNFRSF18, and TNFRSF4 as candidates of potential immunoregulatory interest; external multisample validation is required before generalizing these findings.
