papers.title: Dynamic CD4⁺ T-Cell eQTLs Reveal Gene Regulatory Networks Associated with Atopic Dermatitis.
papers.authors: Chen J, Bai B.
papers.abstract: Background and objective Atopic dermatitis (AD) is a complex immune-mediated disorder in which aberrant activation of CD4⁺ T cells plays a critical pathogenic role. We integrated dynamic CD4⁺ T cell expression quantitative trait loci (eQTL) data with Mendelian randomization (MR) to dissect the causal effect of transcriptional changes on AD risk. Methods This study integrated dynamic CD4⁺ T-cell eQTL analysis, two-sample MR, colocalization analysis, single-cell transcriptomic, pseudotime, cell-cell communication and protein-protein interaction (PPI) analyses, with virtual single-cell knockout further used to evaluate gene regulatory effects in AD. We systematically analyzed gene expression and genetic variation in CD4⁺ T cells from 119 individuals of European ancestry across multiple activation time points (0 h, 16 h, 40 h, and 5 days). Results We performed two-sample Mendelian randomization (MR) integrating dynamic CD4⁺ T-cell eQTL, OneK1K, eQTLGen, and FinnGen R12 AD cohort data. The analysis identified 298 genes significantly associated with AD (FDR Conclusion We demonstrate that understanding the dynamic characteristics of CD4⁺ T cells is crucial for AD, and prioritize genes for future research into its pathogenesis.

papers.title: A time-resolved single-nucleus atlas of cochlear aging reveals biphasic inflammaging and Tbx2-dependent inner hair cell maintenance.
papers.authors: Zhao H, Wang Y, Wang Q, Ma X, Zhao K, Zhai X, Wang R, Han M, Cui L, Sun Y.
papers.abstract: Background Age-related hearing loss (ARHL) is the most prevalent sensory deficit in older adults, yet its molecular progression remains poorly resolved. Few cochlear single-cell studies have integrated cell-cell communication, gene regulatory network (GRN) reconstruction, and cross-cohort bulk validation into one temporal framework. Methods We reanalyzed publicly available single-nucleus RNA sequencing data from C57BL/6 J mouse cochleae at 3, 12, and 24 months and cross-validated against two independent bulk microarray cohorts. Ligand-receptor interactions were inferred and validated at the ligand-expression level. GRNs were reconstructed and perturbed in silico; and feature selection extracted cross-scale inflammatory features. Results ARHL did not follow a linear decline. A cochlea-wide type I interferon response peaked at 12 months and resolved by 24. Apolipoprotein E followed a three-phase trajectory, baseline, compensatory upregulation, collapse, across spiral ganglion neurons, inner hair cells (IHCs), macrophages, and fibrocytes. SLIT-ROBO axon-guidance signaling shut down in these cells, alongside neurotrophic and Notch withdrawal. In silico perturbation identified T-box transcription factor 2 (Tbx2) as a protective GRN node: knockout drove 81.2% of IHCs toward aging and overexpression 74.6% toward youth. A 13-gene inflammatory panel showed midlife activation and end-stage exhaustion in macrophages, mirroring the interferon peak. Conclusion These findings support a two-stage ARHL model, midlife immune activation followed by end-stage synaptic, lipid, and axon-guidance collapse, positioning the midlife window and Tbx2-dependent IHC maintenance as candidate intervention targets, pending in vivo validation.

papers.title: Evaluation of cross-cohort generalizability of machine learning-derived blood transcriptomic biomarkers for Parkinson's disease.
papers.authors: Kumar S.
papers.abstract: Parkinson's disease (PD) lacks reliable, minimally invasive diagnostic biomarkers, and blood transcriptomic machine learning (ML) has emerged as a potential discovery strategy, although cross-cohort reproducibility remains uncertain. We performed a leakage-free analysis of four publicly available transcriptomic datasets (GSE99039, GSE6613, GSE7621, and GSE54536) using a nested ML framework in which data-dependent preprocessing and model development were restricted to training data. Eleven classifiers were evaluated using a training-fold-derived 100-gene panel with repeated 5-fold cross-validation, independent validation, and exploratory cross-tissue comparison, complemented by WGCNA and functional enrichment analysis. The ensemble achieved a mean discovery AUC of 0.682 ± 0.049 in GSE99039, whereas independent validation in GSE6613 yielded an AUC of 0.618 (95% CI, 0.470-0.767). Cross-tissue evaluation in substantia nigra GSE7621 produced an AUC of 0.549 with 51% direction-of-change concordance. WGCNA showed only weak module-trait associations, while the ML panel was predominantly enriched for immune processes, including natural killer cell immunity, myeloid leukocyte activation, and antigen presentation. These findings indicate limited generalizability of blood transcriptomic ML signatures and support further validation in larger, harmonized multicenter cohorts.

papers.title: Single-cell profiling of cross-tissue features of fetal pig macrophages and their remodeling in fetal growth restriction.
papers.authors: Lai CL, Chen XY, Cai LP.
papers.abstract: Macrophages are highly heterogeneous immune cells with context-dependent functions, yet their diversity across prenatal tissues of the whole body, sexes, and stages remains elusive. During fetal development, macrophages play essential roles in tissue formation and maintaining maternal-fetal immune balance, but their specific phenotypic and functional changes in the context of fetal growth restriction remain relatively underexplored. Herein, we constructed a cross-tissue macrophage atlas of 85 473 cells from 54 tissues of late-gestation fetal pigs. We identified 15 macrophage subtypes, among which two Hofbauer cell (HBC) subtypes were distinguished by their distinct transcriptional and functional characteristics between the amniotic and chorioallantoic membranes: HBC GPNMB+ cells upregulated glycolytic enzymes and extracellular matrix regulators such as LDHA and GPNMB , while HBC PEG10+ cells expressed immunomodulators and developmental regulators, including A2M and PEG10 . Two dichotomous subtypes, LYVE1 high MHCII low and LYVE1 low MHCII high , were delineated across 27 tissues, with a conserved transcriptional signature in pigs and humans. Transcriptional profiling of metabolic pathways revealed oxidative phosphorylation and the tricarboxylic acid cycle as core pathways across tissues, alongside tissue-specific adaptations such as enhanced glycolysis in amniotic macrophages. Cross-stage comparisons showed fetal macrophages mainly maintained developmental programs, whereas adult macrophages globally exhibited heightened immune activity. Cross-sex and cross-species analyses revealed high transcriptomic similarity in fetal macrophages. In growth-restricted fetuses, chorioallantoic HBCs showed profound remodeling, including increased inflammation, hypoxia response, and vascular dysfunction signaling, with altered intercellular communication. Collectively, this work provides a comprehensive resource for understanding fetal macrophage heterogeneity and offers insights into the potential mechanisms underlying fetal growth restriction.

papers.title: Single-cell transcriptomics revealed immunological and molecular profiling of pangolin viruses at the viral interface.
papers.authors: Yang XN, Chen PY, He YL, Li XR, Zhou YJ, Cao JY, Pan XY, Qiu H, Zhang ZN, He MH, Li YJ, Qin J, Liu LL, He YX, Zhou JP, He XN, Hassan NMA, Que TC, Hu YL.
papers.abstract: Pangolins have been identified as potential intermediate hosts for various viruses, including coronaviruses related to SARS-CoV-2 and MERS-CoV, yet the cellular mechanisms underlying their viral susceptibility remain poorly understood. Here, we establish the first comprehensive single-cell transcriptomic atlas for two pangolin species Manis pentadactyla and Manis javanica , generated through single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) of 245 618 high-quality cells from 12 major tissues, combined with 123 bulk transcriptome datasets. This resource is integrated with cross-species data from Homo sapiens, Eptesicus fuscus, Sus scrofa, Mus musculus, and Panthera tigris . Our analysis reveals a myeloid-biased hematopoiesis in pangolin bone marrow, dominated by monocytes and T cells, which contrasts sharply with the lymphoid-skewed composition observed in H. sapiens and M. musculus . We also identify species-specific features, including thyroid-specific expression of FKBP5 in M. pentadactyla , and MIF-signaling-mediated cellular interactions in intestinal lymph. Furthermore, key viral receptors ( AXL, NRP1, DPP4, ACE2, SCARB1, and UVRAG ) are broadly expressed in immune cells (e.g., B cells, T cells, and macrophages), fibroblasts, and endothelial cells across tissues, as confirmed by single-cell and bulk transcriptomic analyses. Cross-species comparisons reveal fundamental differences in splenic immune architecture, hematopoietic lineage distribution, and viral receptor expression. Together, these findings based on single-cell transcriptomic profiling establish a molecular and cellular framework for understanding pangolins as potential mixing vessels for viruses and provide a foundation for the targeted surveillance of emerging zoonotic pathogens.

papers.title: Proof-of-Concept of an Intravital Murine Model to Observe the Spatiotemporal Distribution of Immune Cells Constituting the Foreign Body Response and Biomaterial Associated Infections.
papers.authors: Boonstra EC, Jutte PC, van der Mei HC, Satapathy AS, Wolters AHG, van Kooten TG, Sjollema J.
papers.abstract: Biomaterials are used more and more for permanent implantation in humans to replace body parts. Biomaterial implantation is frequently complicated by chronic immune activation, the foreign body response (FBR), and biomaterial-associated infections (BAI). While biomaterial design increasingly focuses on immune modulation, predicting complex biological outcomes remains challenging. Existing models typically address single cell types or molecular parameters, overlooking the dynamic spatial and temporal interactions that define the FBR. Here, an intravital "FBR-through-a-window" model was established, with the internal surface of a murine abdominal imaging window either uncoated or biomaterial-coated, which enables longitudinal microscopy of the underlying tissue in the same mouse. Using transgenic mice with fluorescent probes, macrophages or neutrophils, myofibroblasts, and collagen were simultaneously visualized. Distinct spatiotemporal patterns of the different cell types were observed in the absence and presence of BAI: macrophages and neutrophils localized near the window, followed in depth by myofibroblasts and collagen, with depth and quantities changing longitudinally. This model enables integrated investigation of FBR and BAI, advancing understanding of host-biomaterial interactions in vivo.
papers.venue: Journal of biomedical materials research. Part B, Applied biomaterials

papers.title: Pan-Adrenergic Inhibition Alleviates Post-Hemorrhagic Hydrocephalus by Attenuating Neutrophil Extracellular Traps-Mediated Glymphatic Dysfunction.
papers.authors: Yang Y, Zhou Y, Ouyang Q, Nuerlanbieke H, Yuan Y, Wang J, Wang K, Long P, Chen Y, Liu Z, Huang J, Zhang Z, Su Z, Wang X, Xiao G.
papers.abstract: Aims Post-hemorrhagic hydrocephalus (PHH) is a devastating complication. This study aims to elucidate how the acute post-hemorrhagic adrenergic storm drives neutrophil extracellular traps (NETs) formation, blocks the glymphatic system (GS), and causes an imbalance in intracranial fluid homeostasis, leading to PHH. It is necessary to explore whether pan-adrenergic inhibition as non-surgical intervention strategies can rescue this neuro-immune dysregulation. Methods Single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) was used to draw the immune infiltration map. Utilizing a rat PHH model, ventricular volumes and glymphatic fluid dynamics were assessed via MRI and fluorescent tracer tracking. Multiple behavioral analyses were used to observe the neurological dysfunction. The structural integrity of the GS was assessed using IF staining and TEM. The formation of NETs was detected using ELISA, WB, and IF. In vitro, flow cytometry and molecular assays were used to explore the changes in molecular pathways in epinephrine-stimulated primary neutrophils, and NETs were used to treat astrocytes to study the interaction between them. A pharmacological intervention using pan-adrenergic inhibitor cocktail PPA (prazosin, propranolol, atipamezole), NETs agonist, NETs inhibitor, and AKT activator was conducted to explore the mechanism. Results scRNA-seq identified a pathogenic neutrophil subset presented as a transcriptional phenotype consistent with NETs, which dominated hemorrhagic stroke. Structurally, adrenergic storm-driven NETs extrusion occluded perivascular spaces and stripped aquaporin-4 (AQP4) polarization at astrocytic endfeet, precipitating glymphatic stasis and severe ventricular dilation. Molecular analysis revealed that epinephrine might promote the formation of NETs by activating the PI3K/AKT/mTOR cascade. PPA blocked this pathological axis, inhibited NETs, polarized AQP4 distribution, restored the fluid dynamics of the GS, and relieved cognitive deficits after intraventricular hemorrhage and alleviated hydrocephalus. Conclusion After PHH, targeted pan-adrenergic inhibition can block the adrenergic storm and inhibit NET formation, protect the clearance function and structural integrity of the GS, stabilize the intracranial fluid homeostasis, and alleviate hydrocephalus in the acute phase. The molecular mechanism may involve the PI3K/AKT/mTOR cascade. This mechanism provides a potential therapeutic strategy for neuro-immune-based drug protection.

papers.title: Antigen-Experience Imprints Integrin Expression in Human B Cells.
papers.authors: Cinicola BL, Laffranchi M, Sugoni C, Volpe G, Albano C, Pulvirenti F, Zaffina S, Vinci MR, Di Prinzio RR, Zicari AM, Quinti I, Sozzani S, Carsetti R, Piano Mortari E.
papers.abstract: Integrins are critical regulators of lymphocyte adhesion and migration, shaping immune responses by directing cells to specific tissues. In B cells, integrin expression is dynamically regulated during differentiation and activation, yet it is incompletely understood whether immunization and infection influence these pathways. Here, we investigated the expression and regulation of the α4β1 and α4β7 integrins across circulating human B-cell subsets in adults and children following SARS-CoV-2 vaccination and/or infection. By combining flow cytometry, bulk and paired single-cell RNA and VDJ sequencing, and antigen-specific analyses, we show that naïve and early memory B cells predominantly express β7, while antigen experience drives the emergence of two integrin-imprinted memory lineages characterized by β7 or β1 expression. The highest integrin levels were observed in activated memory B cells (actMBCs) and plasmablasts, indicating enhanced migratory potential. Integrin expression was linked both to the maturation stage and to the immunoglobulin isotype. Importantly, SARS-CoV-2 infection-either before or after vaccination-significantly increased the frequency of β1-expressing memory B cells in both adults and children, particularly among spike-specific actMBCs. Single-cell analyses further identified distinct actMBC subsets with divergent integrin profiles and activation dynamics. Together, our findings demonstrate that respiratory viral infection imprints durable migratory programs on antigen-specific B cells, favoring α4β1 expression, with implications for tissue targeting and the design of next-generation mucosal vaccines.

papers.title: Integrative transcriptomic profiling of the phosphatome identifies DUSP15 as a chromophobe renal cell carcinoma-selective epithelial biomarker associated with an immune-metabolic tumour state.
papers.authors: Sarhan AR.
papers.abstract: Chromophobe renal cell carcinoma (chRCC) lacks robust molecular markers and well-defined therapeutic vulnerabilities. Here, 265 protein-coding phosphatases were systematically interrogated using pan-cancer transcriptomic profiles from The Cancer Genome Atlas (TCGA), cross-cohort evaluation in seven subtype-annotated Gene Expression Omnibus datasets drawn from a ten-dataset compilation, pathway and immune analyses, and two independent single-cell RNA-sequencing datasets. DUSP15 emerged as the most chRCC-selective phosphatase (Tau = 0.977) and showed high retrospective discriminative performance both between chRCC and clear-cell and papillary RCC (AUC = 0.976) and between chRCC tumours and adjacent normal kidney tissue (AUC = 0.973) in TCGA. Subtype discrimination was independently reproduced across the GEO cohorts (AUC = 0.837). Transcriptome-wide analyses showed that DUSP15-high tumours were characterised by coordinated enrichment of oxidative phosphorylation, MYC target and DNA repair programmes, together with reduced interferon and inflammatory signalling. Immune deconvolution revealed lower regulatory T-cell, dendritic-cell and overall immune enrichment scores, consistent with a relatively immune-poor transcriptional state. Single-cell analyses localised the bulk-tumour DUSP15 signal predominantly to tumour-associated epithelial populations in two independent datasets, with DUSP15 detected in 72.2-83.7% of tumour epithelial cells and pseudobulk abundance ranging from 144.9 to 204.3 counts per million. Expression was substantially lower in immune, stromal, normal renal epithelial and non-chRCC tumour populations. Collectively, these findings identify DUSP15 as a highly selective tumour-epithelial biomarker candidate for chRCC and establish the cellular context of a DUSP15-associated immune-metabolic state with potential diagnostic and biological relevance.

papers.title: Single-cell and spatial analysis of inflammation-associated resistance in intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma.
papers.authors: Tang X, Huang H, Shen X, Kong G, Zhang W, Yu J, Wu C, Wu J.
papers.abstract: Intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma (ICC) is frequently associated with chronic inflammation and a complex stromal microenvironment, yet the cellular and molecular features underlying heterogeneous responses to neoadjuvant chemo-immunotherapy remain unclear. Here, using Flex-based single-cell transcriptomic profiling of post-treatment ICC specimens from responders and non-responders, together with multiplex immunohistochemistry and animal model validation, we delineate a coordinated, inflammation-associated multicellular state linked to treatment non-response. Non-response tumors showed enrichment of SPINK1⁺ epithelial cells, inflammatory cancer-associated fibroblasts, SPP1⁺ and inflammatory macrophage states, and immunosuppressive or inflammation-associated CD4⁺ T-cell programs. Across epithelial, stromal, and immune compartments, IL6-JAK-STAT3-related inflammatory signaling emerged as a recurrent feature of resistance. Computational cell-cell communication analysis predicted increased communication probabilities between iCAFs and SPINK1⁺ epithelial cells and between InfMp and CD4Tem cells in non-response tumors, nominating TNF-TLR2, HMGB1-TLR2, AGT-CYBB, and TNF-ICAM1 as candidate ligand-receptor associations. Tissue-level validation confirmed increased SPINK1 expression, inflammatory macrophage features, and elevated p-STAT3 signals in non-response tumors. Combined PD-1 blockade and JAK1/2 inhibition showed enhanced antitumor activity in both a hydrodynamic injection-based cholangiocarcinoma-like mouse model and a humanized huPBMC-NOG-dKO mouse model bearing ICC-X1 xenografts. In the hydrodynamic model, the combination was also accompanied by reduced p-STAT3 activity and enhanced T-cell infiltration and granzyme B expression. Together, these findings identify a coordinated, multicellular inflammatory state associated with non-response to neoadjuvant chemo-immunotherapy in ICC and nominate JAK-STAT signaling as a convergent, therapeutically actionable vulnerability. The antitumor activity observed with combined JAK1/2 inhibition and PD-1 blockade further supports evaluating this inflammatory signaling axis as a therapeutic target to improve immunotherapy responsiveness in ICC.
papers.venue: Drug resistance updates : reviews and commentaries in antimicrobial and anticancer chemotherapy

papers.title: B cell/adipocyte crosstalk amplifies MCP-1 secretion, M2-like macrophage accumulation, and polarization in gut-associated, inflamed adipose tissue.
papers.authors: Goess MC, Heinze JM, Hofmann J, Buck A, Gadjalova I, Weber MC, Ring S, Buescher JM, Villa M, Neumann PA, Ruland J, Keppler SJ.
papers.abstract: Background and aims During Crohn's disease (CD), hyperplasia of the mesenteric white adipose tissue (WAT), called creeping fat (CrF), is associated with the accumulation of immune cells. Here we investigated the impact of B cell/adipocyte crosstalk on immune cell recruitment and inflammation within inflammatory bowel disease-related adipose tissue. Methods We used flow cytometry and in vitro 3D culture systems of biopsies from CrF of CD patients as well as a mouse model of intestinal inflammation, in vitro co-cultures, mass spectrometry, and single-cell RNA sequencing to evaluate the impact of B cell/adipocyte interplay on monocyte chemoattractant protein-1 (MCP-1) production and macrophage polarization. Results Employing primary human and mouse 3D adipocyte cultures, we observed that adipocytes from CD patients displayed a persistent inflammatory phenotype even after prolonged time in culture, a cytokine secretion profile also recapitulated via lipopolysaccharide stimulation. Analyzing CrF of CD patients as well as WAT of a mouse model of intestinal inflammation, we found an accumulation of B cells. B cell/adipocyte co-cultures led to elevated secretion of MCP-1 by primary adipocytes, facilitating macrophage migration. Consequently, co-transfer of B cells with T cells increased T cell activation and M2-like macrophage accumulation in inflamed mouse WAT. Mass spectrometry and single-cell RNA sequencing analyses suggested that the B cell/adipocyte crosstalk establishes a microenvironment that may promote M2-like macrophage polarization. Conclusion B cell/adipocyte interactions in CD-associated inflamed adipose tissue increase MCP-1 and lactate, promoting recruitment and M2-like polarization of macrophages, likely amplifying local WAT inflammation.

papers.title: Integrative Analysis of Nucleotide Metabolism-Related Genes Reveals a Diagnostic Signature and In Silico Functional Disruption in Hypertrophic Scarring.
papers.authors: Luo Q, Yang X, Shen J, Yan M, Wang X, Liang Y, Guan L.
papers.abstract: Hypertrophic scar (HTS) is a fibrotic skin disease characterized by excessive extracellular matrix accumulation and chronic inflammation. This study aimed to investigate cellular heterogeneity, immune alterations, and nucleotide metabolism-related biomarkers in HTS and to explore their potential mechanisms. Single-cell RNA sequencing data were analyzed using Seurat for cell clustering and annotation. Nucleotide metabolism activity was evaluated to identify key cell populations and candidate genes. Bulk transcriptomic datasets from the Gene Expression Omnibus (GEO) were used for differential expression analysis, and machine learning algorithms were applied to develop a diagnostic model. Sixteen cell clusters were identified, with macrophages showing prominent activation of nucleotide metabolism pathways and immune-related signaling. The optimal Enet + svmLinear model achieved strong predictive performance (area under the curve = 0.934), and Shapley Additive exPlanations analysis identified NCF1 and GPR34 as key predictive genes. These genes were also associated with immune cell infiltration. In vitro validation using THP-1-derived M2 macrophages showed that NCF1 and GPR34 promoted transforming growth factor-β1 secretion and enhanced fibroblast activation, while their knockdown reduced α-smooth muscle actin and collagen I expression. Collectively, this study reveals the important role of macrophage-associated nucleotide metabolism in HTS and identifies NCF1 and GPR34 as potential biomarkers and therapeutic targets.

papers.title: Identification of potential active ingredients from Chuanxiong Rhizoma in the treatment of vascular dementia: CHI3L1 and TLR2 are potential key targets.
papers.authors: Liao H, Zeng Q, Zhang J, Chen T, Li J, He Q, Sun L, Wang J, He B, Xiang Q.
papers.abstract: Vascular dementia (VaD) is a cognitive impairment resulting from cerebrovascular disease, which causes functional decline. Its rising prevalence and the absence of effective therapeutic interventions highlight an urgent need for novel therapeutic strategies. The research aimed to identify crucial target genes and bioactive compounds responsible for the therapeutic effects of Chuanxiong Rhizoma in VaD through a comprehensive bioinformatics strategy. Network pharmacology identified 240 shared target genes between Chuanxiong Rhizoma and VaD. Weighted gene co-expression network analysis identified 114 genes significantly associated with VaD. Venn analysis identified CHI3L1, TAC1, toll-like receptor 2 (TLR2), and CCL2 as candidate target genes. Differential expression analysis confirmed dysregulation of CHI3L1, TAC1, TLR2, and CCL2 in VaD. Single-cell RNA analysis showed CHI3L1 predominantly in fibrous astrocytes, TAC1 in Parvalbumin inhibitory neurons, and TLR2 in microglia. Receiver operating characteristic analysis showed CHI3L1 (area under the curve [AUC] = 0.6597, P = .0144), TAC1 (AUC = 0.7797, P < .0001), and TLR2 (AUC = 0.7468, P = .0002) had significant AUC values, indicating potential diagnostic value for VaD. Gene set enrichment analysis showed CHI3L1, TAC1, and TLR2 enriched in chemokine signaling, allograft rejection, and JAK/STAT pathways. Immune cell infiltration analysis indicated that the correlation of CHI3L1 with Macrophages M2 was significantly positive, whereas it was significantly negative with activated natural killer cells (NK cells). The correlation of TAC1 with Macrophages M2 was significantly negative, whereas it was significantly positive with both activated NK cells and follicular helper T cells. The correlation of TLR2 with Macrophages M2 was significantly positive, whereas it was significantly negative with activated NK cells and follicular helper T cells. Molecular docking followed by 100-nanosecond molecular dynamics simulations indicated that palmitic acid binds stably to both CHI3L1 and TLR2, and that perillyl alcohol binds stably to TLR2, whereas the CHI3L1-perillyl alcohol complex showed persistent instability during the molecular dynamics trajectory and was therefore not considered a supported interaction. The findings indicated Chuanxiong Rhizoma might exert its anti-VaD effects through palmitic acid and perillyl alcohol by targeting CHI3L1 and TLR2. The study generated a multi-component, multi-target hypothesis for VaD that warrants further experimental validation.

papers.title: MultiMHC: a multiscale learning framework integrating sequence and residue contact topology for peptide-MHC binding prediction.
papers.authors: Chen W, Chi Y, Wang Y, Wu J, Wei M, Zhao W, Kang Y, Bai X, Chen S, Zhou Z, Zhou R.
papers.abstract: Accurate prediction of peptide-major histocompatibility complex (pMHC) binding is central to understanding antigen presentation and identifying T-cell epitopes in cancer immunotherapy. Although recent methods have achieved notable progress, most approaches rely predominantly on sequence-based features and only partially capture structural determinants of pMHC recognition. In this study, we present MultiMHC, a multiscale deep learning framework that integrates complementary sequential and biologically-informed residue contact topology for pMHC binding prediction. MultiMHC combines a recurrent neural network to model global sequence context with a graph-based representation to encode residue contact patterns derived from known pMHC binding interfaces. Features from these two pathways are subsequently fused to generate binding predictions across peptides of varying lengths. Benchmark evaluations show that MultiMHC achieves performance comparable to existing state-of-the-art methods, with particularly strong performance in ranking-based assessments. Moreover, evaluation on the Tumor Neoantigen Selection Alliance dataset showed that MultiMHC binding scores can enrich experimentally validated T-cell epitopes among top-ranked candidates, supporting its potential utility as an upstream binding-based filtering step in neoantigen discovery workflows. Together, these results highlight the value of incorporating residue interaction patterns and lightweight structural information into pMHC modeling and establish MultiMHC as a robust and extensive framework for antigen presentation analysis.

papers.title: Analysis and Identification of Candidate Genes Associated with M1 Macrophage Infiltration and Glycolysis in Breast Cancer.
papers.authors: Zhang L, Wu L, Xu C, Fang C, Tian X, Zhu K.
papers.abstract: Macrophage polarization and glycolytic reprogramming contribute to the breast cancer microenvironment. However, the genes associated with these features and their clinical relevance remain poorly defined. Breast cancer transcriptomic datasets were analyzed using immune deconvolution, single-sample gene set enrichment analysis, and weighted gene coexpression network analysis. We identified 101 genes shared by the M1 macrophage-associated, glycolysis-related, and differentially expressed gene sets. Eight genes showed suggestive genetically predicted associations with BC risk. Machine learning selected seven consensus genes. In TCGA-BRCA, six genes differed significantly between tumor and normal tissue, but only five changed in the same direction as in GSE65194. In the 56 paired clinical tissues, ADAM15, PPP1R14B, and XPO5 were upregulated in tumors, whereas FAM172A and PPM1M were downregulated. ADAM15, PPP1R14B, and XPO5 were preferentially expressed in M1-like TAMs, whereas FAM172A and PPM1M showed higher expression in M2-like TAMs. In BMDMs, overexpression of ADAM15, XPO5, or PPP1R14B, as well as knockdown of PPM1M or FAM172A, increased the proportion of CD80-positive cells and ATP, glucose uptake, and lactate production. Five genes showed significant associations with overall survival. Functional enrichment analyses implicated immune regulation, extracellular matrix organization, and metabolic pathways.

(B) A heatmap illustrates the pairwise Spearman correlation coefficients among the infiltrating immune cell populations across all samples. papers.title: ROS-Responsive Hydrogel Delivery of miR-665 for Alopecia Areata: Mechanistic Insights and Translational Perspectives.
papers.authors: Cheng W, Ren X, Chen G, Ni S, Ni H, Wu M.
papers.abstract: Alopecia areata (AA) is a common autoimmune hair-loss disorder driven by cytotoxic T cells, interferon-γ (IFN-γ) signaling, and dysregulated JAK-STAT activation. Current systemic treatments, including JAK inhibitors, are limited by safety considerations and frequent relapse after treatment discontinuation. Local nucleic acid delivery is promising but faces challenges in stability, tissue retention, and controlled release. Luo et al. recently developed a reactive oxygen species (ROS)-responsive injectable hydrogel based on polyvinyl alcohol crosslinked with N 1 ,N 3 -bis(4-boronobenzyl)-N 1 ,N 1 ,N 3 ,N 3 -tetramethylpropane-1,3-diaminium bromide (PVA-TSPBA) for delivery of miR-665, a microRNA targeting STAT3. This Commentary evaluates the mechanistic rationale of the miR-665/STAT3 axis, the advantages of ROS-responsive hydrogels for lesion-specific release, and key translational barriers. Specific testable mechanisms are proposed for the dissociation between reduced STAT3 mRNA and stable total protein, including upstream kinases (JAK2/SRC), phosphatases (SHP-1/PTEN), and indirect pathways. Although the system shows prolonged local retention, attenuated inflammation, and enhanced hair follicle regeneration in preclinical models, critical issues remain unresolved, including the cellular targeting spectrum of miR-665, in vivo ROS-dependent release kinetics, miRNA stability under oxidative conditions, and potential systemic immune effects. Single-cell omics, spatial imaging, in vivo imaging, humanized models, and toxicological evaluation will be key to clinical translation.

papers.title: DNA damage response and repair signaling: Emerging biomarkers and therapeutic targets in human cancers.
papers.authors: Dasgupta A, Sarkar K.
papers.abstract: Maintenance of genomic integrity is essential for proper cellular function and for protecting against malignant transformation. Prolonged exposure to endogenous and exogenous genotoxic environments results in multiple forms of DNA damage, including single-strand breaks, double-strand breaks, oxidative lesions, base mismatches, and replication-associated abnormalities. Cells possess a meticulously regulated DDR network of specialized sensor proteins, checkpoint regulators, signal mediators, and repair pathways to address various damages. Key repair mechanisms, such as BER, NER, MMR, HRR, NHEJ, and Alt-EJ, collectively maintain genomic stability and regulate cellular viability in response to genotoxic stress. Aberrant expression of DDR-associated molecular partners significantly contributes to genomic instability, tumorigenesis, progression, metastasis, and therapy resistance in specific malignancies. Recent advancements in molecular oncology have underscored the translational significance of DDR signaling in cancer diagnosis, prognosis, and targeted therapy. Synthetic lethality methods, particularly PARP inhibition in malignancies that impair HR, have transformed precision oncology. Moreover, recent data indicate significant interactions between DDR mechanisms and various cancer hallmarks, including epigenetic regulation, metabolic reprogramming, immune modulation, adaptation to replication stress, and TME signaling. This review focuses on the diagnostic and translational significance of DDR alterations in human cancers, with particular emphasis on biomarker interpretation and clinical efficacy. Current approaches for HRD and MMR/MSI assessment, including genomic, functional and liquid-biopsy strategies, are considered together with their pre-analytical and analytical limitations. The review further examines how DDR biomarkers inform targeted treatment selection, resistance monitoring, and emerging approaches, while highlighting unresolved challenges in assay validation, tumor heterogeneity, dynamic biomarker evolution, and clinical implementation. PLAIN LANGUAGE SUMMARY: DNA in our cells is constantly being damaged by normal cellular processes and environmental factors such as radiation and harmful chemicals. Cells contain protective systems called the DNA damage response (DDR) and DNA repair pathways that are capable of detecting and repairing this damage. When these systems become defective, DNA modifications can accumulate and contribute to cancer development, progression, and resistance to treatment. This review explains how major DNA repair pathways maintain genomic stability and how alterations in these pathways might generate vulnerabilities that can be used to treat cancer. It also addresses the established and emerging therapies targeting DNA repair vulnerabilities such as PARP, ATR, ATM, CHK1, WEE1, DNA-PK, and POLQ inhibitors. It also discusses why certain tumors do not respond or develop resistance to these therapies and why biomarkers do not always accurately predict treatment effectiveness. The review also covers the interactions between DNA damage and the immune system, such as context-dependent functions of cGAS-STING signaling. Finally, emerging methods such as functional DNA-repair tests, circulating tumor DNA (ctDNA), single-cell and spatial analysis, and multi-omics may improve patient selection and assist in leading more personalized and effective cancer treatment.

papers.title: Extracellular Vesicle Associated MicroRNAs in Vitiligo: A Systematic Review of Mechanisms and Translational Potential.
papers.authors: Husan N, Trifitriana M, Thaha MA, Purwoko MIH, Aryani IA, Diba S.
papers.abstract: Background Extracellular vesicle (EV)-associated microRNAs may contribute to vitiligo-related melanocyte and immune-cell changes. This review evaluates their mechanistic and translational evidence while distinguishing biological compartments and experimental models. Methods Searches covered six information sources from database inception up to 30 April 2026. Three authors screened reports and three extracted data, with disagreements referred to designated adjudicators. Bias was appraised using an adapted Cochrane domain-based framework. No registration identifier was reported. Evidence was synthesized by design and EV source; heterogeneity precluded meta-analysis. Results Seven studies examined keratinocyte EVs, circulating EV-enriched fractions, human umbilical cord mesenchymal stem cell (hUMSC) EVs, or computational datasets. Cellular experiments linked miR-200c and miR-21-5p to melanogenesis and miR-493-3p to keratinocyte dopamine handling in segmental vitiligo. miR-1469 was associated with non-segmental vitiligo activity and natural killer (NK)-cell regulation. A small longitudinal miR-487b-3p study reported an exploratory area under the receiver operating characteristic curve of 0.840 for pretreatment versus post-treatment samples. hUMSC-EV experiments distinguished miR-125b-5p/BAK1-mediated melanocyte protection from miR-132-3p/SIRT1-mediated regulatory T-cell differentiation. Computational associations provided hypothesis-generating evidence. Conclusion Evidence supports selected experimental mechanisms and exploratory biomarker candidates. Small samples, heterogeneous methods, incomplete retrieval accounting, and lack of established external clinical validation limit inference. EV-based microRNA therapies remain preclinical.

papers.title: Identification and Validation of Hub Genes Associated With Periodontitis and Systemic Lupus Erythematosus.
papers.authors: Li Y, Xu X, Wu Z, Li F, Zhang J.
papers.abstract: Background Accumulating evidence suggests a close relationship between periodontitis and systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE); however, the shared molecular mechanisms underlying this association remain unclear. This study aimed to identify candidate genes and molecular features shared between periodontitis and SLE through integrative bioinformatics analysis and clinical validation. Methods Gene expression profiles were obtained from the Gene Expression Omnibus (GEO) database, and differentially expressed genes (DEGs) shared between periodontitis and SLE were identified. Gene Ontology (GO) and Kyoto Encyclopedia of Genes and Genomes (KEGG) enrichment analyses were performed, followed by protein-protein interaction (PPI) network construction and hub gene screening. The expression patterns of the hub genes were evaluated in independent validation datasets, and their discriminatory performance was assessed by receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve analysis. Immune cell infiltration and its correlations with hub gene expression were further investigated. Transcription factor-microRNA regulatory networks and candidate compounds were computationally predicted. Finally, quantitative real-time PCR (qPCR) was performed to validate hub gene expression in clinical samples. Results A total of 124 overlapping DEGs were identified, from which five hub genes-CCL3, LY96, FOS, MMP9, and PTGS2-were selected. GO and KEGG enrichment analyses indicated that the overlapping DEGs were predominantly associated with inflammatory and immune-related biological processes and signaling pathways. All five hub genes showed consistent expression patterns in the independent periodontitis validation dataset, whereas FOS, LY96, and PTGS2, but not CCL3 and MMP9, showed consistent differential expression in the independent SLE validation dataset. ROC analyses demonstrated varying discriminatory performance across the analyzed datasets. Immune infiltration analysis revealed differences in estimated immune cell profiles in both disease datasets, and computational prediction identified candidate regulatory interactions and compounds for further investigation. qPCR validation in clinical samples (n = 15 per group) showed significantly increased expression of all five hub genes in gingival tissues from patients with periodontitis and PBMCs from patients with SLE compared with their respective healthy controls. Conclusion This study identified CCL3, LY96, FOS, MMP9, and PTGS2 as candidate genes associated with periodontitis and SLE. FOS, LY96, and PTGS2 showed consistent expression patterns across datasets, whereas CCL3 and MMP9 exhibited dataset-dependent variation in SLE. Clinical qPCR validation showed increased expression of all five genes in both disease cohorts. These findings provide insight into the shared molecular features of periodontitis and SLE and warrant further validation in larger, independent, and clinically well-characterized cohorts.

papers.title: MYH11-LMOD1 Axis Promotes Ferroptosis and Inhibits Migration and Invasion in Non-Small-Cell Lung Cancer.
papers.authors: Lin B, Xu Y, Liu S, Wang M, Shi L, Chen C.
papers.abstract: Background Ferroptosis has emerged as a critical mechanism influencing the development of non-small-cell lung cancer (NSCLC). Emerging evidence implicates the dysregulation of leiomodin 1 (LMOD1) in tumorigenesis. This work explored in detail the function of LMOD1 in NSCLC ferroptosis and malignant progression. Methods The expression pattern of LMOD1 in NSCLC was analyzed using GSE238161, GSE229301, and the GEPIA platform. Analysis of correlation between LMOD1 and immune cell infiltration was performed using the TIMER algorithm. LMOD1-associated genes were identified using LinkedOmics platform and subjected to KEGG pathway enrichment analysis. The effects of LMOD1 were evaluated by detecting cell colony formation, migration, and invasion. The impact on ferroptosis was assessed by measuring ROS levels and related protein expression. The myosin heavy chain 11 (MYH11)-LMOD1 relationship was confirmed by chromatin immunoprecipitation (ChIP) and luciferase assays. Results LMOD1 expression was downregulated in NSCLC and correlated with tumor TNM stage and lymph node metastasis. Bioinformatics analysis suggested a potential correlation between LMOD1 expression and immune cell infiltration in NSCLC. LMOD1 might intersect with multiple signaling pathways, including PI3K-Akt, MAPK, calcium, cGMP-PKG, Th1/Th2 differentiation, and chemokine signaling. Functionally, increase of LMOD1 suppressed cell growth, migration, and invasion while enhancing ferroptosis. Mechanistically, MYH11 acted as a transcriptional activator of LMOD1 by binding to the LMOD1 promoter region. Conclusion Our study shows that LMOD1, transcriptionally activated by MYH11, functions as a tumor suppressor in NSCLC by enhancing ferroptosis, uncovering a previously unrecognized therapeutic strategy for NSCLC intervention.

papers.title: Endothelial Cell Secretome Alterations Induced by Inflammatory Stress.
papers.authors: Tang VT, Baid S, Castellanos A, Basrur V, Kretz CA, Nesvizhskii AI, Gao X, Dong Q, Weiss MJ, Abbineni PS.
papers.abstract: Endothelial cells detect pathogens through pattern recognition receptors, such as Toll-like receptor 4 (TLR4), which triggers the synthesis and secretion of molecules that initiate the innate immune response. Proteins bearing signal peptides are secreted through the classical endoplasmic reticulum (ER)-Golgi-dependent route, whereas select signal-peptide-lacking proteins are secreted via less well-characterized ER-Golgi-independent mechanisms, collectively termed unconventional protein secretion (UcPS). To systematically characterize the secretome of human umbilical vein-derived endothelial cells (HUVECs) and delineate the contribution of UcPS, we performed deep quantitative proteomics on HUVEC lysates and conditioned medium before and after TLR4 stimulation with lipopolysaccharide (LPS). Of 5205 proteins detected in either fraction, 381 were enriched in the conditioned medium and therefore classified as secreted. Of these, 302 proteins (79.3%) were secreted via the conventional pathway, and 79 (20.7%) lacked a signal peptide and were classified as candidate UcPS cargos. Predicted functions of UcPS-secreted proteins include redox regulation, proteostasis, cytoskeletal remodeling, and innate immune signaling. We confirmed that α-globin (HBA1), which functions as a redox sensor and regulator of nitric oxide in endothelial cells, is secreted constitutively by UcPS and at higher levels following inflammatory activation. Notably, candidate UcPS cargo identity showed poor concordance with current computational predictors, underscoring the need for empirical datasets. Overall, our findings suggest that the HUVEC secretome includes both conventionally and unconventionally secreted proteins that regulate coagulation, angiogenesis, and immune function. Our findings establish a high-quality secretome dataset for HUVECs, providing a novel resource for future efforts to define the molecular determinants governing UcPS cargo selection and trafficking related to endothelial cell function.

papers.title: Nucleotide metabolism and cervical cancer: A comprehensive study of molecular subtypes and therapeutic targets.
papers.authors: Li F, Bao C, Liu Y, Liu B, Zhai F.
papers.abstract: Cervical cancer (CC) is among the most prevalent malignancies in women worldwide. Tumor progression involves profound metabolic reprogramming, in which nucleotide metabolism sustains deoxyribonucleic acid/ribonucleic acid synthesis and proliferation; however, its role in CC remains unclear. Transcriptomic and clinical data of CC patients were obtained from The Cancer Genome Atlas. Nonnegative matrix factorization classified patients into molecular subtypes based on nucleotide metabolism-related genes and compared their survival, immune infiltration, somatic mutations, and drug sensitivity. Mfuzz soft clustering identified subtype-associated expression patterns. Gene set variation analysis scoring, differential expression analysis, and Gene Ontology/Kyoto Encyclopedia of Genes and Genomes enrichment of differentially expressed genes were then performed. Prognostic models were constructed using multiple machine learning algorithms, and the model with the highest concordance index (C-index) was selected. Patients were stratified into high- and low-risk groups and assessed using multivariate Cox regression, Kaplan-Meier, and time-dependent receiver operating characteristic analyses. Immune checkpoint inhibitor response was predicted using the tumor immune dysfunction and exclusion algorithm, and molecular docking was performed between core genes and candidate compounds. Nonnegative matrix factorization revealed 5 subtypes with distinct outcomes: cluster 2 showed the worst prognosis, whereas clusters 3 and 4 had favorable survival. TTN, KMT2C, HUWE1, and PIK3CA were frequently mutated across subtypes. B cells, regulatory T cells, CD8+ T cells, and M2 macrophages were enriched in clusters 3 and 4. VX-680, CIL70, and BRD-K01737880 exhibited significantly lower IC50 values in the poor-prognosis group. Seven key genes (SERPINE1, CAV1, SOD2, SLC16A1, XDH, CYP27B1, and NAGS) were identified by Mfuzz clustering. Forty-two differentially expressed genes between the high- and low-score groups were predominantly enriched in xenobiotic response, nutrient sensing, small-molecule catabolism, inflammatory response, tumor necrosis factor signaling, apoptosis, and hypoxia. The generalized boosted regression model achieved the highest C-index, with 1-, 3-, and 5-year area under the curves of 0.62, 0.67, and 0.61, indicating modest discrimination. Tumor immune dysfunction and exclusion analysis indicated reduced immune checkpoint inhibitor responsiveness in the high-risk group. Molecular docking predicted favorable binding between core genes and candidate compounds, providing hypotheses for experimental validation. This study delineates the associations of nucleotide metabolism-related genes with molecular classification and prognosis in CC and identifies potential biomarkers, candidate therapeutic agents, and a prognostic model providing complementary assessment value.

papers.title: Integrated NeutroDrop-enabled single-cell ROS-NE droplet biosensing for sepsis auxiliary diagnosis and survival prediction.
papers.authors: Yao Y, Wang F, Pu X, Shao M, Hua C, Cui J, Zhang Y, Wang Q, Deng G, Liu Y, Zhu L, Liu N, Yang X, Yang K.
papers.abstract: Sepsis assessment relies largely on organ-dysfunction scores and systemic biomarkers, which provide limited information on immune-effector function. We developed NeutroDrop, an integrated droplet microfluidic platform for single-cell profiling of neutrophil reactive oxygen species (ROS)-related oxidative activity and neutrophil elastase (NE)-associated proteolytic activity. Under standardized fMLP stimulation, individual neutrophils were co-encapsulated with fluorescent probes in monodisperse droplets, while membrane-integrity screening and software-assisted image analysis excluded multicell and membrane-compromised droplets. The study included 1012 neutrophils from 10 healthy controls and 2353 neutrophils from 20 patients with sepsis. Analysis of patient-level median signals showed reduced NE activity in sepsis (group means, 28.91 vs. 72.32), whereas ROS showed a nonsignificant decrease (72.14 vs. 92.26). Healthy-reference single-cell analysis revealed marked depletion of high ROS/high NE neutrophils in sepsis (2.89% vs. 16.86%), leading to the Per HighHigh index for healthy/sepsis classification. Local abundance analysis identified a data-derived low-amplitude ROS-NE region associated with non-survival; its patient-level abundance, P i (R), stratified 12-day outcome with 83.33% sensitivity and 92.85% specificity in the discovery cohort. These locked rules were implemented in NeutroDrop-Plus, which correctly classified all 10 operator-blinded samples and matched 12-day outcomes in 5 of 6 sepsis cases. NeutroDrop converts neutrophil single-cell functional heterogeneity into quantitative biosensing indicators for adjunctive sepsis classification and exploratory short-term outcome stratification.

papers.title: Multimodal profiling of repair-associated immune cells in a mouse model of menstruation.
papers.authors: Ainslie RJ, Kirkwood PM, Li H, Gerasimou S, Saunders PTK, Simitsidellis I, Gibson DA.
papers.abstract: Despite the importance of inflammation to menstruation, we lack detailed understanding of how immune dynamics contribute to endometrial repair. We performed detailed phenotypic characterisation of uterine immune cells using single cell RNA sequencing, flow cytometry and multiplex immunohistochemistry in a mouse model of simulated menstruation. Uterine tissues were collected from age-matched controls or from key phases of menstruation; tissue breakdown, repair and remodelling. Our findings reveal distinct compositional and transcriptional changes in uterine immune cells across different phases of menstruation. Flow cytometry and immunohistochemistry analysis demonstrated that monocytes and neutrophils were predominant in tissue repair, while macrophages and neutrophils were abundant during tissue remodelling. Distinct tissue repair-associated genes were detected in monocytes (Fn1, Pdpn, Thbd), macrophages (Apoe, Axl, C3), and neutrophils (Lrg1, Plaur, S100a9), with thrombospondin 1 and secreted phosphoprotein 1 identified as key signalling pathways in endometrial repair. Unexpectedly, neutrophils were predominant throughout menstruation, and were the most abundant uterine immune cell in endometrial breakdown, repair and remodelling. Transcriptome profiling highlighted expression of anti-inflammatory markers such as Dusp1 and Acod1 consistent with a pro-resolution phenotype in this context. These data significantly advance our understanding of the immunology of menstruation, highlighting myeloid-specific mediators as future translational targets for menstrual disorders.

papers.title: Drug resistance mechanisms and sensitization strategies in central nervous system tumors.
papers.authors: Xiong F, Li G, Chan YT, Xin Y, Hong R, Xie K, Zhou W, Zhang C, Zhang B, Feng Y, Wang N, Chen ZS, Huang Q.
papers.abstract: Central nervous system tumors remain challenging owing to their location, heterogeneity, and relapse, with persistently high mortality to incidence ratios. Current standard therapy (surgery plus temozolomide based chemoradiotherapy) remains first line, yet nearly all patients eventually develop acquired resistance, the major hurdle to survival benefit. Resistance is not driven by single gene mutations but by a multidimensional adaptive network from nucleus to intercellular communication. In the nucleus, backup DNA repair pathways activate with epigenetic regulation, allowing cells to escape via lineage reprogramming or senescence. In the cytoplasm, metabolic reprogramming affects epigenetic enzymes and reshapes antioxidant/repair networks. At the membrane, the blood brain and blood tumor barriers not only physically block drugs but also actively remodel to promote resistance. In intercellular communication, immunosuppressive cells (Tregs, M2 macrophages) and neuron glioma synapses provide signals and metabolic support. Emerging sensitizing strategies include targeting repair, blocking plasticity, eliminating senescent cells, computational combination therapy, epigenetic metabolic interventions, biomimetic delivery, immune microenvironment remodeling, and disrupting neuro tumor crosstalk-but are limited by BBB penetration, preclinical model fidelity, and target selectivity. This review organizes current evidence by spatial mechanisms and proposes a multi modal personalized sensitization framework centered on overcoming barriers, aiming to provide a theoretical reference for precision therapy.
papers.venue: Drug resistance updates : reviews and commentaries in antimicrobial and anticancer chemotherapy

papers.title: Single-Cell Immune Cis-eQTL Mendelian Randomization Prioritizes Cell-Type-Resolved Candidate Causal Genes for Endometriosis.
papers.authors: Wang X, Yao G, Ding W.
papers.abstract: Background Endometriosis has a substantial immune component, but the cellular contexts of genetically regulated disease susceptibility remain incompletely resolved. Methods We tested single-cell cis-eQTL instruments from 20 OneK1K peripheral-blood cell types against FinnGen R12 endometriosis (20,190 cases; 130,160 controls) using single-variant Mendelian randomization (MR), colocalization and sensitivity analyses. Benjamini-Yekutieli (BY) correction distinguished conservative findings from an exploratory Benjamini-Hochberg (BH) screen. Directional consistency, bulk-blood MR and lesion expression provided contextual comparisons. Results Across 9157 unique gene-cell-type tests, 135 associations in 61 genes reached BH-FDR Conclusion The analysis prioritizes immune-context candidate genes for functional study. IGF1R remains an exploratory, mechanistically unresolved nomination. Genetic support and protein tractability do not establish therapeutic benefit or reproductive safety; experimental validation is required.

figure.label: Figure 1
figure.caption: Study design. Single-cell immune cis-eQTL instruments (OneK1K via the eQTL Catalogue, 20 cell types) are tested against endometriosis (FinnGen R12) by Wald-ratio Mendelian randomization, followed by colocalization on complete ±500 kb windows, robustness and power assessment, dependence-aware significance tiers, directional consistency, cross-disease comparison and tractability annotation. BH, Benjamini–Hochberg; by, Benjamini–Yekutieli; FDR, false discovery rate; MHC, major histocompatibility complex; PIP, posterior inclusion probability; PP4, posterior probability of a shared causal variant.

papers.title: Temporal Dynamics of CD52-mediated T Cell-stromal Crosstalk in Sepsis-induced Acute Respiratory Distress Syndrome.
papers.authors: Li W, Cao Y, Gao R, Miao S, Li N, Sun H, Hua S.
papers.abstract: Introduction Acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS), frequently triggered by sepsis, is associated with high mortality and severe disruption of the alveolar-capillary barrier driven by immune dysregulation. This study aimed to characterize immune-stromal crosstalk in sepsis-induced ARDS and develop a predictive risk model. Methods Bulk transcriptomic datasets were used for differential expression analysis, immune deconvolution, and development of a sepsis-to-ARDS risk model. eQTL-based Mendelian randomization evaluated associations between genetically predicted gene expression and sepsis susceptibility. Human and mouse single-cell datasets were used for pseudotime and inferred ligand-receptor communication analyses. Results Ten core genes, including CD52 and MACF1, were prioritized by integrating ARDSassociated differential expression with genetic associations for sepsis susceptibility. CD52 showed dynamic expression changes in CD8+ T cells. CD52-low states were associated with stronger inferred MIF- and TGF-β-related communication and with transcriptional programs linked to immune recruitment and barrier dysfunction. The four-gene signature showed moderate discrimination in the external-validation cohort (AUC = 0.688). Discussion These findings identify CD52 as a marker of a dynamic immunoregulatory state in sepsis- induced ARDS and associate CD52-low states with altered inferred T cell-stromal communication. The four-gene signature provides proof-of-concept support for transcriptomic risk stratification but requires further clinical validation. Conclusion CD52 marks a time-dependent immune state associated with inferred T cell-stromal communication in sepsis-induced ARDS. The four-gene signature provides proof-of-concept support for risk stratification, while functional studies are required to determine whether CD52 directly modifies barrier-related signaling.
papers.venue: Endocrine, metabolic & immune disorders drug targets

papers.title: Role of LGALS9 and human milk oligosaccharides in modulating immune responses in food allergy: Insights from network pharmacology and molecular simulations.
papers.authors: Chen S, Ai K, Liu Y, Xiong Z, Zhong W, Yang A, Wu Z, Chen H, Li X.
papers.abstract: Background Food allergy is a growing global health concern, and effective strategies for restoring immune tolerance remain limited. Human milk oligosaccharides (HMOs) have potential immunomodulatory effects, but their molecular targets and mechanisms in food allergy are not fully understood. Objective This study aimed to identify potential protective genes associated with food allergy and to investigate the possible role of LGALS9 in HMO-related immune regulation. Methods Network pharmacology was used to identify overlapping targets between food allergy-associated genes and four selected HMOs: 2'-fucosyllactose, 3'-sialyllactose, lacto-N-neotetraose, and lacto-N-tetraose. Mendelian randomization analysis was performed to assess the association between candidate gene expression and food allergy. Single-cell transcriptomic analysis was used to examine LGALS9 expression across immune cell populations and treatment-response groups. Molecular docking and molecular dynamics simulations were conducted to evaluate predicted interactions between LGALS9 and the four HMOs. In vitro BMDC - naïve CD4 + T-cell co-culture assays were further used to assess T-cell differentiation and cytokine secretion. Results Network pharmacology identified 16 overlapping targets between the four HMOs and food allergy-associated genes. Mendelian randomization analysis showed a significant inverse association between LGALS9 expression and food allergy, supporting a potential protective role. Single-cell analysis of a peanut allergy oral immunotherapy cohort showed that LGALS9 expression was significantly higher in healthy controls than in the patient groups, particularly in Treg cells. Molecular docking suggested that all four HMOs could interact with the selected LGALS9 binding site, with lacto-N-tetraose showing the most favorable docking-derived binding score. Molecular dynamics simulations indicated that the predicted complexes remained structurally stable over the simulated period without major conformational changes in LGALS9. In vitro assays showed that HMO-treated BMDCs promoted CD25 + Foxp3 + Treg differentiation and increased IL-10 secretion. Conclusion The integrated computational, transcriptomic, genetic, and in vitro findings identify LGALS9 as a potential HMO-associated immunoregulatory target in food allergy. However, direct functional studies are still required to determine whether the immunomodulatory effects of HMOs are dependent on LGALS9.

papers.title: Integrative Single-Cell and Bulk RNA Sequencing Analysis Identifies Ion Channel-Related Biomarkers in Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease.
papers.authors: Xue C, Huang L, Mei H, Gao Y, Liu P, Ye J, Ma C, Zhao D.
papers.abstract: Background Human ion channel genes (HICGs), as core effectors of transmembrane signal transduction, play a critical role in the initiation and progression of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD); however, the underlying mechanisms remain largely unclear. This study aimed to investigate the potential value of ion channel genes in COPD. Methods Differential expression analysis was performed to screen HICGs in COPD datasets. A total of 107 machine learning models were employed to identify hub HICGs and evaluate their diagnostic performance, and SHAP analysis was used to assess feature contributions. GSEA, immune cell infiltration, and inflammatory cytokine correlation analyses were conducted on the hub HICGs. Consensus clustering and WGCNA were used to define two disease subtypes and key modules. Single-cell RNA-seq data were used to examine the expression patterns of the hub HICGs. Subsequently, virtual knockout, virtual drug screening, and molecular docking were performed. Results The nine hub HICGs showed high diagnostic performance in cross-dataset validation, with LRRC8D ranking first in the SHAP analysis. These HICGs were significantly correlated with immune cells and inflammatory cytokines. Consensus clustering revealed significant gender differences between the two subtypes (BH-adjusted P = 0.01), and the two subtypes were enriched in phagocytosis and MAPK signaling pathways, respectively. Single-cell RNA-seq analysis using the Ro/e index suggested enrichment of macrophages and a reduction in smooth muscle cells in the disease group. Virtual knockout of LRRC8D was predicted to preferentially affect CD68 and the affected genes were enriched in human cytomegalovirus infection. Virtual screening prioritized Tezacaftor as a potential therapeutic agent, and molecular docking predicted that Tezacaftor may exhibit high binding affinity for the hub HICGs. Conclusion We identified potential HICGs in COPD and suggested a potential role for LRRC8D, as well as the potential utility of hub HICGs in disease subtyping, particularly with respect to gender, and Tezacaftor may serve as a candidate therapeutic agent.

papers.title: Exploring the Molecular Mechanisms of Yinxieping Tablets in Psoriasis Treatment Based on Network Pharmacology, Bioinformatics, and Experimental Validation.
papers.authors: Zhu Z, Ma L, Sun D, Li W, Zhao J.
papers.abstract: Introduction Psoriasis is a prevalent immune-mediated chronic inflammatory skin disease, with a pathology defined by abnormal keratinocyte proliferation and immune cell infiltration. Yinxieping Tablets (YXPT), a traditional Chinese medicine formula consisting solely of rosin, have been clinically used to alleviate psoriatic symptoms. However, their underlying mechanisms of action remain to be fully elucidated. Methods We established an imiquimod (IMQ)-induced psoriasis-like mouse model and systematically screened the potential targets and pathways of YXPT using integrated network pharmacology, bioinformatics, machine learning, transcriptome sequencing, and molecular docking. Key findings were experimentally validated by Western blot and qPCR in a psoriasis-like mouse model. Results YXPT treatment improved psoriasiform skin lesions and was associated with lower lesional Ki67 expression and serum pro-inflammatory cytokine levels; high-dose YXPT also reduced the spleen index. Integrated analyses identified six candidate genes (BCL2, LYN, SYK, CCR2, AURKA, and ADRB2), with CCR2 emerging as the sole overlap with RNA-seq-derived genes. CCR2-based gene-set analysis showed enrichment of PI3K/Akt- and NF-κB-related pathways. Following YXPT treatment, lesional CCR2 protein and mRNA levels, phosphorylation of PI3K, Akt, p38, and p65, and mRNA levels of PI3K, Akt, p38, ERK1/2, and p65 were lower than in the IMQ group. Conclusion YXPT ameliorated psoriasis-like skin lesions in the IMQ mouse model, accompanied by lower CCR2 expression and changes in PI3K/Akt, MAPK, and NF-κB pathway components. These findings nominate CCR2 as a candidate for further study, while its causal role and relationship to the signaling changes remain to be established.

papers.title: CXCL12: a key gene in IPF-COPD pathogenesis and its therapeutic potential.
papers.authors: Lin Q, Chang H, Wang F, Zhou L, Deng B, Wang J, Dai Z, Ye H.
papers.abstract: Objectives Shared core genes and molecular mechanisms relevant to the pathological overlap between idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis (IPF) and chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) were investigated to inform future diagnostic and therapeutic research. Methods Gene expression profiles were analysed using differential expression gene (DEG) analysis, weighted gene co-expression network analysis (WGCNA), and functional enrichment. A random forest (RF) model incorporating a multi-feature selection mechanism was used to identify core genes in IPF patients with COPD. The expression levels, diagnostic performance, and immune cell relationships of these genes were analysed, and single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) was used to assess the expression patterns of the core genes. Finally, drug predictions were made based on the core genes. Molecular docking and 100-ns molecular dynamics simulations were further performed to evaluate candidate CXCL12-ligand interactions, and CXCL12 expression was experimentally validated in BEAS-2B cells after cigarette smoke extract, bleomycin, and combined stimulation. Results CXCL12 was identified as a core gene for IPF combined with COPD. This gene exhibited high expression levels in the dataset, with receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve area under the curve (AUC) values of 0.78, 0.67, 1.00, and 0.86, respectively. Exploratory analysis of CIBERSORT-estimated immune-cell proportions showed significant differences in CD8 + T cells and resting memory CD4 + T cells between the CXCL12-high and CXCL12-low groups. Single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) indicates that CXCL12 exhibits significantly increased expression in endothelial cells of COPD and fibroblast cells of IPF, providing valuable insights into the molecular mechanisms. Molecular docking results suggested that sitagliptin and LY-294,002 could serve as therapeutic candidates for IPF combined with COPD. Molecular dynamics simulations supported the sustained binding stability of both CXCL12-ligand complexes. In vitro validation further showed that CXCL12 was induced at the mRNA and protein levels after epithelial injury stimulation. Conclusions CXCL12 plays a key role in the pathogenesis of IPF combined with COPD and holds promise as a potential target for the diagnosis and treatment of this disease.
