papers.title: SerRS2 Identifies an Inflamed-Exhausted Hepatocellular Carcinoma Phenotype with Enhanced DNA-Sensing and Increased Anti-PD-1 Responsiveness.
papers.authors: Li P, Zhu G, Li D, Liang M, Zhang L, Li J, Jia Y, Zou B.
papers.abstract: Background Seryl-tRNA synthetase 2 (SerRS2, encoded by SARS2 ) is a mitochondrial aminoacyl-tRNA synthetase essential for mitochondrial protein translation and homeostasis. Its clinical and immunological significance in hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) remains unclear. Methods Transcriptomic and clinical data from 371 TCGA-LIHC patients were analyzed to evaluate SerRS2 expression, prognosis, immune infiltration, T-cell exhaustion, and DNA-sensing-related features. Four single-cell RNA-sequencing datasets were analyzed to characterize the cellular distribution of SerRS2. Public immunotherapy cohorts were evaluated for associations between SerRS2 expression and immune checkpoint blockade outcomes, and an independent HCC cohort was used for qPCR validation. Group comparisons were performed using Student's t -test or Wilcoxon rank-sum test, correlations using Pearson or Spearman analyses, and survival outcomes using Kaplan-Meier analysis with the Log rank test, as appropriate. Results SerRS2 was significantly upregulated in HCC and associated with advanced pathological stage and poorer survival. Elevated SerRS2 expression was consistently associated with increased CD8+ T-cell infiltration and exhausted T-cell abundance and positively correlated with PDCD1, TOX, LAG3, HAVCR2 , and CTLA4 . SerRS2 was also positively associated with cGAS ( MB21D1 ) and DDX41 , but not STING1 , and SerRS2-high tumors exhibited increased exhaustion and DNA-sensing scores. Collectively, these findings support a SerRS2-associated inflamed-exhausted immune phenotype characterized by increased CD8+ T-cell infiltration, T-cell exhaustion-related features, and enrichment of DNA-sensing-related transcriptional programs. Single-cell analyses revealed heterogeneous SerRS2 expression across multiple cellular compartments, supporting its interpretation as a tissue-level rather than tumor-cell-specific signal. In public cross-tumor immunotherapy cohorts, elevated SerRS2 expression was associated with improved outcomes following PD-1 blockade, whereas comparable associations were not consistently observed for PD-L1 or CTLA-4 blockade, suggesting potential relevance of the SerRS2-associated immune phenotype to PD-1 blockade. These immune associations were further supported by qPCR validation in an independent HCC cohort. Conclusion SerRS2 is associated with an inflamed-exhausted immune phenotype in HCC and may represent a candidate tissue-level biomarker for immune stratification. Its potential relevance to PD-1 blockade warrants prospective validation in HCC-specific immunotherapy cohorts.

papers.title: Integrated Transcriptomic Analysis and Experimental Validation Identify ATF3 as a Mesangial Cell-Associated Candidate Regulator in IgA Nephropathy.
papers.authors: Liang M, Gan X, Shadekejiang H, Hong H, Li X, Xia T, Wang J, Zhang X, Lu C.
papers.abstract: Background IgA nephropathy (IgAN) is an immune-mediated glomerular disease marked by mesangial proliferation, inflammation, extracellular matrix accumulation, and progressive renal injury. This study aimed to identify IgAN-associated genes and evaluate the relevance of activating transcription factor 3 (ATF3) to mesangial cell activation. Methods Public bulk transcriptomic datasets were integrated for differential expression, co-expression network, machine learning, and immune infiltration analyses. Single-cell RNA sequencing, mesangial cell-specific high-dimensional weighted gene co-expression network analysis, and single-cell regulatory network inference were used to assess cell type-specific expression and regulatory activity. The findings were further evaluated using Nephroseq and an aggregated IgA1-stimulated human mesangial cell model with ATF3 knockdown. Results Integrated analysis identified 47 shared differentially expressed genes and a 12-gene candidate set with reduced expression in IgAN. ATF3 was prioritized as a mesangial cell-associated candidate and showed reduced expression and regulon activity in the analyzed single-cell dataset. Nephroseq analysis showed lower glomerular ATF3 expression in IgAN-related kidney disease samples; ATF3 expression was positively associated with estimated glomerular filtration rate and negatively associated with serum creatinine and proteinuria. Aggregated IgA1 reduced ATF3 expression in human mesangial cells, whereas ATF3 knockdown further increased inflammatory cytokine expression and proliferative activity. Conclusion Reduced ATF3 expression is associated with IgAN-related mesangial cell activation. ATF3 may represent a mesangial cell-associated candidate regulator that warrants further mechanistic and clinical validation.

figure.label: Figure 1
figure.caption: Overall workflow of integrated transcriptomic analysis and validation for identifying ATF3 in IgA nephropathy. Public bulk transcriptomic datasets were integrated to identify IgAN-associated gene signatures, followed by WGCNA, machine learning-based feature prioritization, single-cell mapping, regulon analysis, external validation, and in vitro functional experiments in human mesangial cells.

papers.title: Targeting the IL-23-IL-23R Interface with Small Molecules: Challenges, Opportunities, and Emerging Strategies.
papers.authors: Vu TT, Thai KM, Mai QM, Nguyen NL, Tran QH, Tran TT, Dao TT, Le MT.
papers.abstract: Interleukin-23 (IL-23) is a validated therapeutic driver in psoriasis and inflammatory bowel disease, and selective IL-23p19 antibodies have established a high efficacy benchmark for pathway inhibition. Interest has therefore expanded toward oral, non-antibody approaches, including IL-23R-targeting macrocyclic peptides and conventional low-molecular-weight compounds. Direct antagonism of the IL-23p19-IL-23R interface is attractive because it acts upstream of intracellular JAK2/TYK2 signaling and is structurally separated from the p40-IL-12Rβ1 interaction shared with IL-12. The principal challenge is medicinal-chemical: the orthosteric site is a dynamic proteinprotein interaction surface with limited constitutive pocket character. This Mini-Review focuses on the evidence relevant to drug discovery rather than reiterating pathway biology. We distinguish experimentally validated interface binders from computationally prioritized candidates, summarize potency, selectivity, assay format and development status where available, and discuss lessons from program attrition. Recent advances include an induced orthosteric pocket on IL-23p19, live-cell competition pharmacology, highly potent oral IL-23R peptides, and early small molecule hits supported by cellular assays. Computational docking, molecular dynamics, MM/GBSA, QSAR, and AI-assisted design can enrich hypotheses but do not, by themselves, establish direct binding, selectivity, pharmacokinetics, or safety. The key unresolved question is whether a classical small molecule can demonstrate direct target engagement at this challenging interface while achieving sufficient potency, pathway selectivity, and drug-like exposure to compete with advanced biologic and peptide modalities.

papers.title: Prognostic value of cell differentiation-related genes in follicular lymphoma based on integrated single-cell and bulk RNA sequencing.
papers.authors: Xiang X, Deng W.
papers.abstract: Follicular lymphoma (FL) is the most common indolent B-cell lymphoma and follows a heterogeneous clinical course; however, reliable molecular markers for risk stratification are still lacking. We integrated single-cell RNA sequencing data (GSE182434) with bulk transcriptomic data from three GEO cohorts (GSE66166, GSE119214, GSE16131) and applied pseudotime trajectory analysis, consensus clustering, weighted gene co-expression network analysis, and LASSO Cox regression to derive a cell differentiation-related gene signature (CDRGS) and a prognostic risk model. Model performance was evaluated by time-dependent ROC analysis, the concordance index, calibration curves, decision-curve analysis, and multivariable Cox regression, and the expression of the signature genes was examined by RT-qPCR, western blot, and immunohistochemistry in lymphoma cell lines, in a SU-DHL-4 xenograft model, and in an independent cohort of patients with FL. Pseudotime analysis resolved three differentiation states, and consensus clustering based on the CDRGS stratified patients into three molecular subtypes with different overall survival. A three-gene model comprising SIRPG, FLT3LG, and LAG3 separated high- and low-risk patients in the training cohort and in the GSE119214 validation cohort, with separation in the same direction but not reaching significance in GSE16131, and remained associated with overall survival after adjustment for M7-FLIPI in the two cohorts in which that index was available. All three genes were expressed at higher mRNA and protein levels in lymphoma cell lines than in a non-malignant B lymphoblastoid line, indicating that the malignant cells themselves express them. In an independent patient cohort, the expression of the three-gene panel varied with risk score and with established clinical indices in the directions predicted by the model coefficients. We constructed a cell differentiation-related prognostic model for FL and found that SIRPG, FLT3LG, and LAG3 provide candidate biomarkers of the immune microenvironment that carry prognostic information beyond M7-FLIPI and merit prospective validation.

papers.title: Integrating network pharmacology, single-cell transcriptomics, and in silico knockout to explore the potential mechanism of taohong siwu decoction in osteoporosis: A computational approach focusing on the CXCL chemokine signaling axis.
papers.authors: Wang J, Fang G, Wang B, Huang Z, Gao X.
papers.abstract: Background Osteoporosis causes irreversible bone loss and microstructural damage, and elevates fracture risk, imposing a heavy public health burden on elderly and postmenopausal women. Conventional therapies have adverse side effects and poor compliance, and largely ignore bone marrow immune homeostasis. Taohong Siwu Decoction, a classic blood-activating herbal formula, promotes mesenchymal stem cell osteogenesis via Vascular Endothelial Growth Factor-activated Focal Adhesion Kinase signaling; however, its immunomodulatory mechanism against osteoporosis remains unclear. Methods A multiomics computational pipeline was constructed, integrating network pharmacology, weighted gene co-expression network analysis, three machine learning algorithms, CIBERSORT immune infiltration, single-cell transcriptomics, cell-cell crosstalk profiling, coordinate-based cell-state ordering, anoikis quantification, and CellChat-based in silico pathway knockout. Bioactive ingredients (83) and Taohong Siwu Decoction targets (244) were screened using the Traditional Chinese Medicine Systems Pharmacology Database and Analysis Platform with oral bioavailability/drug-likeness thresholds. Results A four-set intersection of Taohong Siwu Decoction targets, osteoporosis genes, GSE35959 differential expression genes, and key modules from the weighted gene co-expression network analysis yielded 5 core therapeutic genes (TGFB1, GSTM1, FOSL1, CTSD, and FOSL2). Gene Ontology and Kyoto Encyclopedia of Genes and Genomes analyses (BH-adjusted P Conclusions Our computations suggest that the CXCL chemokine axis is a prominent candidate mediator of communication within the pathological bone microenvironment. We hypothesize, on the basis of these computational associations, that Taohong Siwu Decoction may alleviate inflammatory bone loss by indirectly restraining CXCL hyperactivation through hub genes, including TGFB1. This multitarget computational model provides novel mechanistic insights into Taohong Siwu Decoction, although all omics-derived hypotheses require rigorous in vitro and in vivo validation. Our immune-focused predictions complement the existing osteogenic evidence, highlighting the potential multidimensional therapeutic value of this classical herbal prescription.

papers.title: DNA methylation-based classification and molecular characteristics of spinal cord gliomas with wildtype histone H3 reveal differences between adult and pediatric pilocytic astrocytoma.
papers.authors: Chai R, Chen H, An S, Shang H, Pang B, Sun Y, Sun H, Tang J, Wu Y, Jia W, Jiang T, Chang Q, Wang Y, Wang J.
papers.abstract: Objective Spinal cord gliomas with wildtype histone H3 (H3WT-SCGs) are rare but heterogeneous tumors for which pathological classification is challenging. Our aim was to characterize a methylation-based molecular classification of H3WT-SCGs. Methods We characterized H3WT-SCGs from 55 patients using data from DNA methylation arrays, whole-exome/transcriptome sequencing, proteomics, phosphoproteomics, single-cell RNA sequencing, and multiplex staining. Another 31 cases with DNA methylation data were used for validation. Results Using DNA methylation data, we identified six spinal cord methylation (SCM) subtypes: pilocytic astrocytoma (PA), PA-immune enriched (PA-IME), diffuse leptomeningeal glioneuronal tumor (DLGNT), subependymoma (SUBEPN), glioblastoma-like (GBM), and pleomorphic xanthoastrocytoma-like (PXA). These SCM subtypes exhibited a distinction from the traditional histology classification in 58.2% of the study cases. In comparison to histology, SCM subtyping better correlates with independent molecular features, as evidenced by significant enrichment of BRAF fusions in the PA and DLGNT classes, and notable enrichment of chromosome 1p losses and 1q gains in DLGNT. SCM-PA can be further divided into pediatric (SCM-PA-P) and adult (SCM-PA-A) subgroups. In comparison to SCM-PA-P, SCM-PA-A was associated with lower BRAF fusion frequency ( P P P = 0.036; all patients alive). Neoplastic cells in SCM-PA-A exhibited a less differentiated status with higher expression of neuronal markers and lower expression of cytokines and chemokines in comparison to SCM-PA-P. In addition, SCM-PA-A had a lower senescence-associated secretory phenotype, lower infiltration of immunosuppressive monocyte-derived macrophages, and less proliferative myeloid cells in comparison to SCM-PA-P. Conclusions This study defined clinically relevant H3WT-SCG molecular classes that reflect patient prognosis and molecular characteristics for potential therapeutic strategies.

papers.title: Single-Cell and Spatial Insights into Oral Squamous Cell Carcinoma: Towards Cell-State-Targeted Immunotherapy.
papers.authors: Chen Y, Hou L.
papers.abstract: Oral squamous cell carcinoma (OSCC) remains associated with substantial morbidity and mortality, and only a subset of patients derive durable benefit from immune-checkpoint blockade. Single-cell and spatial approaches reveal cellular states and tissue organization that bulk profiling cannot resolve. These findings suggest that therapeutic responses may depend on both cellular function and the local interactions that sustain it. This narrative review integrates single-cell transcriptomic, spatial, functional and clinical studies of the OSCC microenvironment. We distinguish OSCC-specific findings from broader head and neck squamous cell carcinoma and pan-cancer evidence. Computational inference, tissue association, experimental perturbation and clinical validation are considered separately. Malignant, myeloid, fibroblast, vascular and lymphoid states form spatially organized niches whose composition varies across anatomical sites and treatment settings. We examine their relevance to immune escape and chemotherapy resistance and assess strategies directed at specific cell states and intercellular circuits. Although selected circuits have functional support in experimental models, many spatial signatures remain observational and lack clinical validation. Clinical translation will require reproducible tissue assays, causal testing of candidate interactions and independent biomarker validation. Practical considerations include marker-panel selection, spatial scoring, tissue availability and the feasibility of sampling primary tumors and metastatic sites before, during and after treatment. Prospective studies must also determine whether biomarker-guided treatment improves outcomes, rather than assuming that a spatial association predicts therapeutic benefit. This review aims to critically synthesize current evidence, identify key knowledge gaps and define requirements for translating cell-state and spatial-niche insights into selective immunotherapeutic strategies for OSCC.

figure.label: Figure 1
figure.caption: Cellular states and spatial niches in oral squamous cell carcinoma. The schematic organizes representative malignant, stromal, myeloid and lymphoid programs across the tumor core, invasive front, stroma, vascular and lymphatic interfaces, and regional lymph nodes. The lower panels illustrate provisional niche archetypes. Cell labels represent context-dependent programs, not fixed functional lineages or validated treatment-selection categories. In particular, the INHBA-positive monocyte population reported in oral precancer should be distinguished from INHBA-positive macrophages described in other contexts. Fibroblast-mediated immune support or suppression also depends on the specific state and setting. papers.title: Deep Learning-Based Spatial Profiling Identifies MET-Associated Immune Exclusion and Therapeutic Vulnerability Underlying Racial Disparities in Head and Neck Cancer
Long non-coding RNA prompts immune-related adverse events risk and immunotherapy response in pan-cancer.
papers.authors: Dong L, Zhang L, Song L, Qu C, Wang X, Xiao S, Tian M, Wang P, Zhi H, Zhao Y, Ning S, Gao Y.
papers.abstract: Immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs) improve cancer outcomes but can cause immune-related adverse events (irAEs) that compromise treatment. Using FAERS real-world data, we developed a two-layer network algorithm to identify irAE-associated lncRNAs (irAEsLncs) across 18 cancer types. The irAEsLnc network showed organ-specific patterns and cancer-specific irAE susceptibility, while irAEsLncs were associated with immune infiltration, inflammatory responses, immune activation, and checkpoint molecules. Single-cell analysis of ICI-induced colitis linked irAEsLncs to inflammatory macrophage and T cell states and metabolic reprogramming. irAEsLnc-derived signatures independently predicted prognosis and responses to targeted therapy and immunotherapy, with ALAL-1/CD80/MEF2C predicting ICI efficacy in lung adenocarcinoma. Knockdown of ALAL-1 and SEC61G-DT suppressed tumor cell proliferation, migration, invasion, and macrophage-mediated inflammation. These findings connect irAE-associated lncRNAs with toxicity and antitumor immunity and support their potential as biomarkers for treatment stratification.

papers.title: Machine learning-guided multimodal analysis of APAF1-associated tumor microenvironment features prioritizes morellic acid for gastric cancer.
papers.authors: Jia B, Yan B, Li S, Yang J, Cheng Z, Zhou X, Song W, Hong X, Chen S, Wu Z, Sheng H, Yang Y, Xu F, Wang J.
papers.abstract: Background Gastric cancer (GC) exhibits substantial molecular heterogeneity and a complex tumor microenvironment (TME). Apoptotic protease-activating factor 1 (APAF1) is a core component of mitochondrial apoptosis; however, its association with immune characteristics, spatial heterogeneity and compound discovery in GC remains poorly defined. Methods The bulk transcriptomics, single-cell RNA sequencing and spatial transcriptomics with machine learning-based modeling, immune deconvolution and spatial niche analysis were integrated to characterize APAF1-associated features in GC. Machine learning-guided computational screening combining molecular docking and molecular dynamics (MD) simulations was used to prioritize morellic acid (MA). The biological effects of MA and the involvement of APAF1-associated signaling were evaluated through in vitro and in vivo assays using APAF1-targeting siRNA and shRNA, respectively. Results APAF1 expression was increased in GC, particularly in early-stage tumors and was independently associated with improved overall survival after multivariable adjustment (HR = 0.681, 95% CI: 0.494-0.940, P = 0.0196). However, its standalone prognostic discrimination was limited, with time-dependent ROC analyses showing poor predictive performance. Tumor-versus-normal ROC analysis demonstrated differential expression between GC and normal tissues (AUC = 0.875, 95% CI: 0.823-0.918). Single-cell and spatial analyses revealed that APAF1 expression was associated with distinct immune-cell patterns and tumor spatial niches. Machine learning-guided computational screening prioritized MA as a candidate compound. MA inhibited GC cell proliferation and migration (IC50: 1.807 ± 0.16 to 6.216 ± 0.23 μM) and suppressed tumor growth in vivo, achieving tumor inhibition rates of 79.32 ± 7.69%, 92.37 ± 4.21%, and 92.19 ± 2.99% at low, medium and high doses, respectively. APAF1 silencing attenuated MA-associated changes in cleaved Caspase-3 activation and GSDME-NT accumulation, suggesting the involvement of APAF1-associated cell-death signaling. Conclusion APAF1 is associated with distinct tumor microenvironment characteristics and clinical features in GC, supporting its potential relevance to tumor biology beyond its canonical role in mitochondrial apoptosis. The novelty of this study lies in extending the investigation of APAF1 beyond its canonical apoptotic function by integrating machine learning with multimodal transcriptomic and spatial analyses to characterize APAF1-associated TME features and computationally prioritize MA. All the findings provide a cross-scale framework linking APAF1-associated tumor biology with candidate compound screening and MA-related cell-death responses in GC.
papers.venue: Phytomedicine : international journal of phytotherapy and phytopharmacology

papers.title: Multi-Omics Machine Learning Framework Identifies CAPS, NUBPL, and RRBP1 as Hubs Linking Neuroinflammation and Mitophagy in Alzheimer's Disease.
papers.authors: An X, Cao M, Yi Z, Wang Y, Yu W, Ren Z.
papers.abstract: Introduction Alzheimer's Disease (AD) is a progressive neurodegenerative disorder characterized by cognitive decline and the accumulation of amyloid-beta plaques and hyperphosphorylated tau protein. The role of mitophagy in AD pathogenesis is not well understood. This study explores how mitophagy-related genes affect AD progression through transcriptomic analysis, machine learning, and immune profiling. Materials and methods Post-mortem transcriptomic data from the middle temporal gyrus (training dataset GSE132903, 97 AD cases and 98 controls) were analyzed. A total of 552 Differentially Expressed genes (DEGs) were identified using stringent criteria (unadjusted p-value 0.5). Weighted Gene Co-expression Network Analysis (WGCNA) was performed to identify gene modules associated with mitophagy. Results Three diagnostic biomarkers were identified and validated using LASSO, Random Forest, and XGBoost: CAPS (AUC = 0.83), NUBPL (AUC = 0.756), and RRBP1 (AUC = 0.78). CIBERSORT analysis revealed a distinct neuroinflammatory profile in AD, characterized by M1 macrophage polarization and CD4+ T cell depletion. Gene Set Enrichment Analysis (GSEA) showed that these biomarkers were associated with metabolic pathways, suggesting a role for metabolicepigenetic interactions in AD progression. Discussion The integration of differential expression analysis, WGCNA, and three machine learning algorithms consistently identified CAPS, NUBPL, and RRBP1 as robust diagnostic candidates, which were independently validated in an external cohort. These findings suggest that mitophagyrelated genes may contribute to AD through mechanisms involving neuroinflammation and metabolic pathways. Nevertheless, the generalizability of these biomarkers across demographics necessitates validation in larger, more diverse cohorts. Conclusion Our findings indicate that these mitophagy-related genes may serve as biomarkers for AD. A nomogram model incorporating these biomarkers showed promising diagnostic performance (training AUC = 0.834; validation with GSE29378: AUC = 0.716). In summary, our research suggests that mitophagy-related genes play a role in AD through immune and metabolic pathways. Understanding these mechanisms could lead to new approaches for the diagnosis and treatment of AD.

papers.title: Cancer-Associated Fibroblasts-Orchestrated Immune Remodeling as a Key Driver in Liver Cancer.
papers.authors: Porro N, Marri S, Salani F, Marra F, Gragnani L, Gentilini A.
papers.abstract: Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) and intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma (iCCA) develop within a highly immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment (TME) characterized by chronic inflammation, extensive stromal remodeling, and impaired antitumor immunity. Among stromal components, cancer-associated fibroblasts (CAFs) have emerged as key regulators of tumor progression and immune homeostasis. This review provides an overview of CAF-mediated immune remodeling in primary liver cancers, with particular emphasis on CAF heterogeneity, CAF-immune cell interactions, and their impact on disease progression and therapeutic response. Increasing evidence indicates that CAFs orchestrate multiple aspects of the tumor immune microenvironment through the secretion of cytokines, chemokines, growth factors, and extracellular matrix components. These signals promote immune exclusion, suppress cytotoxic T-cell activity, and favor the accumulation of immunosuppressive cell populations, including regulatory T cells, myeloid-derived suppressor cells, and tumor-associated macrophages. Advances in single-cell and spatial transcriptomic technologies have revealed substantial CAF heterogeneity and identified distinct CAF subsets with specialized immunomodulatory functions. These findings have uncovered novel therapeutic opportunities, including CAF-targeted approaches, extracellular matrix normalization, and strategies aimed at reprogramming CAF plasticity. Overall, CAFs are central orchestrators of immune remodeling in liver cancer and contribute to the establishment of an immunosuppressive microenvironment that supports tumor progression and therapeutic resistance. Targeting CAF-driven stromal-immune interactions may enhance antitumor immunity and improve the efficacy of current and emerging immunotherapies in HCC and iCCA.

figure.label: Figure 1
figure.caption: Origins, activation, and functional heterogeneity of cancer-associated fibroblasts in primary liver cancers. Cancer-associated fibroblasts (CAFs) originate predominantly from hepatic stellate cells (HSCs), but also from portal fibroblasts (PFs), mesothelial cells, fibrocytes, mesenchymal stem cells/hepatic progenitor cells (MSCs/HPCs), and, to a lesser extent, cells undergoing epithelial-to-mesenchymal transition (EMT). Tumor-derived factors and microenvironmental cues, including transforming growth factor beta (TGF-β), platelet-derived growth factor (PDGF), interleukin-6 (IL-6), exosomal microRNAs (miRNAs), extracellular matrix (ECM) stiffness, periostin (POSTN), and bile acids, promote CAF activation and transdifferentiation, leading to ECM remodeling, angiogenesis, fibrosis, and immune suppression. Distinct CAF subtypes with specialized functions are observed in hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) and intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma (iCCA), highlighting the transcriptional and spatial heterogeneity of the liver tumor stroma. papers.title: Single-cell and spatial transcriptome analyses unveil that MYH11 links stemness to immunotherapy resistance in non-small cell lung cancer.
papers.authors: Xie Y, Xue Y, Lai D, Zhang X, Li G, Zhou Q.
papers.abstract: Background Immunotherapy is an essential treatment strategy for lung cancer, yet resistance to it is often unavoidable, resulting in treatment failure and poor prognosis. The cancer stem cell (CSC) theory offers a valuable perspective for understanding tumor metastasis and resistance to immunotherapy. However, there is a scarcity of multi-omics studies that identify tumor stemness subpopulations and their associated signaling pathways. In this study, we combined single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) with spatial transcriptomics sequencing (ST-seq) to identify a myosin heavy chain 11 ( MYH11) -high stemness subpopulation linked to immunotherapy resistance. Methods We conducted quality control and removed batch effects from two scRNA-seq datasets, then annotated cell types using established marker genes. Malignant cells were distinguished from epithelial cells with fastCNV. Stemness subpopulations were identified using a machine learning-derived messenger RNA (mRNA) stemness index (mRNAsi) and CytoTRACE analysis. To functionally characterize the stemness subpopulation, we employed Monocle3 pseudotime trajectory analysis, CellChat cell-cell communication analysis, and predicted transcription factors (TFs). We also performed consensus clustering on bulk RNA sequencing (RNA-seq) data, followed by immune-related scoring, immune cell deconvolution, and drug sensitivity prediction. Clinical validation was achieved through multiplex immunofluorescence (mIF) and immunohistochemistry (IHC). Experimental validation included short hairpin RNA (shRNA)-mediated MYH11 knockdown, real-time quantitative reverse transcription PCR (qRT-PCR) and western blot analyses, and tumor sphere formation assays to assess cancer stemness. Results We identified nine major cell types and found a significant enrichment of epithelial cells in tumors resistant to immunotherapy. Using fastCNV, we identified malignant cells and defined seven malignant cell subtypes based on stemness scoring. Notably, the Stem-subtype was significantly enriched in resistant tumors. Functional analysis showed that the Stem-subtype could differentiate into other malignant cell subtypes, with a strong enrichment in the NOTCH signaling pathway. Analysis of fibroblast subpopulations revealed that MYH11 + fibroblasts were closely linked to the Stem-subtype, collectively contributing to immunotherapy resistance. Consensus clustering identified two stemness-related subtypes, with Stemness I associated with poor prognosis. Immune scoring and immune cell analysis further indicated an unfavorable response to immunotherapy in Stemness I. Drug sensitivity prediction identified potential therapeutic agents, and in silico knockout experiments revealed downstream target genes. Validation with clinical samples confirmed that MYH11 -high cancer cells were closely correlated with exhausted CD8 + T cell infiltration and poor immunotherapy outcomes. Experimental validation demonstrated that MYH11 knockdown significantly reduced the expression levels of CXCL12 and TUBA1A , as well as the expression of core NOTCH pathway genes. Furthermore, the tumor sphere-forming capacity was markedly suppressed. Conclusions In summary, our multi-omics analysis revealed a MYH11 -high malignant cell stemness subpopulation and a MYH11 + fibroblast subpopulation, both of which are closely linked to immunotherapy resistance and poor prognosis in lung cancer.

papers.title: Screening and experimental validation of prognostic genes associated with B cell exhaustion in lung adenocarcinoma based on ordinary transcriptome data.
papers.authors: Yang B, Wang GS, Zhang L, Yang P, Bao JQ, Li LX, Li L, Gao B, Li W, Li XH.
papers.abstract: Background B-cell exhaustion (BEX) has emerged as a critical mechanism in tumor immune evasion. However, the prognostic significance of B-cell exhaustion-related genes (BEX-RGs) and their potential as therapeutic targets in lung adenocarcinoma (LUAD) remain unclear. This study aimed to identify a BEX-RGs-based prognostic signature and elucidate its implications for LUAD immunotherapy. Methods Transcriptomic data and BEX-RGs were obtained from public databases. Prognostic genes were obtained through univariate Cox analysis and least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO) regression analysis. Afterwards, a predictive model was constructed and validated. Further analyses yielded independent prognostic factors, and a nomogram was created. Additionally, enrichment analyses and immune microenvironment analyses were conducted to elucidate the underlying mechanisms of LUAD. Drug sensitivity analysis was conducted to identify drugs with differential sensitivity between groups, providing a basis for personalized treatment strategies. Immunohistochemical (IHC) staining was used to assess the protein expression of BEX-RGs in 90 LUAD specimens and paired distant normal lung tissues, and overall survival (OS) analysis was performed to evaluate their prognostic associations. Results In this study, five prognostic genes were identified: heparin-binding epidermal growth factor-like growth factor (HBEGF) and CD79A, CD101, adrenergic receptor β2 (ADRB2), and dipeptidase 2 (DPEP2). The developed prognostic model and nomogram had robust risk evaluation capability. Enrichment analyses highlighted immune dysregulation and metabolic alterations. High-risk patients exhibited reduced immune/stromal scores and heightened sensitivity to 36 chemotherapeutic agents. Conclusions Five BEX-related prognostic genes associated with LUAD prognosis were identified, and the constructed model showed potential value for prognostic stratification. Differences in immune microenvironment, gene mutations and drug sensitivity between risk groups provide evidence for tumor immunity research and targeted therapy development. IHC and OS results confirmed that the expression trends of the five genes were consistent with the results of the bioinformatics analysis.

papers.title: A transcriptomic signature of mechanical-memory-related genes predicts progression in prostate cancer.
papers.authors: Sun T, Wu Y, Chen H, Wang F.
papers.abstract: Background Prostate adenocarcinoma (PRAD) is clinically heterogeneous, and conventional markers incompletely explain variation in disease progression. Mechanical memory is the persistence of a mechanically induced cellular state after the initiating cue has been removed. This study aimed to develop and validate a mechanical memory gene (MMG)-related transcriptomic risk score and characterise its prognostic and microenvironmental associations in PRAD. Methods We intersected differentially expressed genes from The Cancer Genome Atlas (TCGA)-PRAD cohort with a curated MMG set and defined molecular subtypes by consensus clustering. A progression-free interval (PFI) model was constructed using univariate Cox, least absolute shrinkage and selection operator Cox, and multivariable Cox analyses. The model was evaluated in GSE116918 and GSE94767. Bulk and single-cell transcriptomic analyses were used to examine genomic alterations, immune states, predicted drug response, and the cellular distribution and functions of core genes. Results Thirty-nine MMG-related differentially expressed genes defined two molecular subtypes with distinct PFI. An eight-gene model comprising MYL9 , EZH2 , COL1A1 , LMNB1 , KIF14 , POSTN , DDR2 , and PARVA stratified patients by PFI and retained independent prognostic value after adjustment for clinicopathological variables. Both external cohorts showed consistent relative risk stratification. Shapley additive explanations (SHAP) identified DDR2 , COL1A1 , and MYL9 as leading contributors to the model-derived risk score. The high-risk group had higher tumour mutational burden, increased immune-checkpoint expression, higher tumour immune dysfunction and exclusion (TIDE) and myeloid-derived suppressor-cell scores, and a lower microsatellite instability (MSI) score. Predicted drug-response analyses identified differential candidate compounds, while cell-cell communication and in silico perturbation analyses prioritised immune, vascular, and regulatory pathways for follow-up. Single-cell analyses localised the three core genes mainly to endothelial and vascular populations and associated them with angiogenesis, matrix remodelling, hypoxic adaptation, metabolic reprogramming, and intercellular communication. Conclusions The MMG-related transcriptomic risk score stratified PFI and delineated genomic, immune, and vascular-stromal differences in PRAD. COL1A1 , DDR2 , and MYL9 prioritised a collagen-related vascular-stromal programme for further investigation. The score provides an MMG-related transcriptomic framework for prognostic and microenvironmental stratification and prioritises testable hypotheses for functional validation.

papers.title: Immune function in burn patients: Pathophysiology, monitoring, and emerging therapeutic strategies.
papers.authors: Korkmaz HI, Boer DP, van der Ven F, Meeder M, Papendorp S, Pijpe A, Vries AM, Bosma E, van Zuijlen PPM.
papers.abstract: Severe burn injury causes extensive local tissue damage and systemic immune alterations that affect infection risk, wound healing, organ function, and survival. The immune response is characterized by rapid activation of innate immune cells, including neutrophils and monocytes, with elevated pro-inflammatory cytokines (IL‑6, TNF‑α, IL‑1β) and complement activity. Simultaneously, adaptive immunity is often impaired, with reduced T and B lymphocyte function, while diminished dendritic cell activity may further compromise antigen presentation and adaptive immune responses. This combined hyperinflammatory and immunosuppressive state, known as burn-induced immune dysfunction, contributes to delayed wound healing, increased susceptibility to secondary infections, sepsis, and multiple organ dysfunction. Monitoring immune function is essential but challenging. Routine markers, including white blood cell count (WBC) and C-reactive protein (CRP), provide limited insight, whereas procalcitonin (PCT), pancreatic stone protein (PSP), and cytokine panels (IL‑6, IL‑8, IL‑10) improve early detection of infection and immune classification. Flow cytometry allows characterization of immune cell populations and functional markers such as monocyte HLA‑DR and T cell PD‑1, while functional assays assess neutrophil, monocyte, and lymphocyte responsiveness. High-resolution molecular approaches, including transcriptomics, proteomics, and single-cell profiling, reveal persistent alterations not captured by conventional assays. Therapeutic strategies to restore immune balance include targeted cytokine modulation, immune checkpoint inhibition, hemoadsorption, metabolic and nutritional interventions, and novel approaches such as nanotechnology or microbiome modulation. Early surgical excision and topical treatments, including cerium-nitrate with silver sulfadiazine, may also attenuate systemic inflammation. However, robust clinical evaluation of these interventions is limited, and their timing, dosing, and patient selection remain under investigation. This review integrates mechanistic, translational, and clinical evidence to provide a framework for understanding burn-induced immune dysfunction. Future research should aim for standardized immune phenotyping, longitudinal multi-omics integration, AI-assisted monitoring, and evaluation of mechanism-based immunomodulatory strategies to improve patient outcomes.

papers.title: Single-cell heterogeneity of adipose eosinophils is shaped by sex and RELMα and linked to macrophage communication networks in obesity.
papers.authors: Ruggiero-Ruff RE, Qiu X, Vance L, He Y, Coss D, Godzik A, Nair MG.
papers.abstract: Eosinophils are immune cells with terminal effector functions in type 2 immune responses, yet recent findings suggest that they exhibit functional plasticity and heterogeneity dependent on tissue-specific cues. Building on our prior functional study showing that the immunoregulatory protein RELMα and eosinophils contribute to female protection from high-fat diet (HFD)-induced obesity, we used single-cell transcriptional profiling to study adipose eosinophil states at higher resolution. We identify six transcriptionally distinct eosinophil clusters whose relative abundance differs by sex, helminth infection, and RELMα status. Adipose tissue from females or helminth-infected mice is enriched for eosinophil clusters with type 2/homeostatic-associated transcriptional programs, whereas males and RELMα-deficient mice have increased representation of inflammatory/MHCII-associated clusters together with an altered predicted macrophage-eosinophil communication networks. Spectral flow cytometry and adipose tissue in situ hybridization independently support eosinophil heterogeneity and candidate chemokine-receptor interactions. Through single-cell regulatory network inference and clustering analysis, we further identified transcription factor regulons unique to the specific eosinophil clusters, including sex-differential and HFD-enriched regulatory programs supported by target-gene expression patterns. Collectively, these data provide a framework for describing adipose eosinophil heterogeneity within a previously established RELMα-macrophage-eosinophil axis and identify candidate transcriptional and communication programs for future functional testing.

papers.title: Integrated pharmacology and validation reveal Formononetin upregulates GSTM2 to modulate prostate cancer immune microenvironment via ROS/STAT3-driven chemokine reprogramming.
papers.authors: Yu T, Zhou Y, He F, Wu Y, Tang S, Zhu Z, Qian W.
papers.abstract: Background Prostate cancer (PCa) is responsible for a substantial proportion of male cancer cases worldwide. Biochemical recurrence (BCR) representing a critical challenge in its disease management. Formononetin, a natural isoflavone derived from traditional Chinese medicine, has demonstrated potential anticancer properties. We sought to determine the translational potential of Formononetin-targeted molecules in PCa. Methods A list of putative targets of Formononetin were identified through five public databases. Overlapping candidates underwent further refinement using an ensemble of bioinformatics tools, encompassing differential expression profiling, co-expression network construction, and multiple machine-learning classifiers. Docked complexes and complementary analyses were subjected to evaluate the binding stability. To functionally validate GSTM2, we assessed its functional role on PCa cell growth, motility, and invasiveness in vitro , as well as the expression of CXCL10 and CCL22 chemokines. Results Integrative analysis identified 413 Formononetin targets, with overlapped 335 PCa-associated genes. Through weighted gene co-expression network analysis and differential expression analysis, 22 candidate genes were identified as Formononetin-related genes in PCa. Machine learning algorithms and survival analysis further suggested GSTM2 as the most important target. GSTM2 was positively correlated with enhanced immune infiltration and sensitivity to Bicalutamide. Single-cell analysis revealed that GSTM2-positive malignant cells exhibited upregulated glutathione metabolism and suppressed respiratory burst pathways. Stable complex formation between Formononetin and GSTM2 was demonstrated by computational docking. Cell-based assays demonstrated that Formononetin upregulated GSTM2 and inhibited PCa malignancy in a GSTM2-required manner. In terms of mechanism, Formononetin attenuated ROS levels and suppressed STAT3 phosphorylation via GSTM2, leading to reprogramming of chemokine expression characterized by upregulated CXCL10 and downregulated CCL22. Conclusion Formononetin reprograms chemokine expression through the GSTM2-ROS-STAT3 axis to regulate the immune microenvironment, suggesting that it might have immune-modulating effects and is worth further in vivo studies.

papers.title: Integrative Multi-Omics Identifies a Causal Immune Gene Panel for Sepsis Diagnosis and Targeted Therapy.
papers.authors: Li J, Tan W, Zhu Z, Wu F, Yan J.
papers.abstract: Introduction Sepsis diagnosis remains challenging due to the lack of specific biomarkers that reflect immune dysregulation, as conventional markers lack immune specificity and causal grounding. Methods We performed a two-sample Mendelian randomization meta-analysis to identify immune phenotypes causally linked to sepsis, with associated genes mapped via multi- -omics annotation. Integrating three GEO datasets (n = 1,039), we constructed a diagnostic panel using six machine learning models, validated its cell-type specificity via singlecell RNA-seq, confirmed protein-level expression using public proteomic datasets, and predicted potential therapeutic compounds targeting the panel genes. Results We characterized protective and risk immune phenotypes in sepsis, identifying 119 genes enriched in immune-metabolic pathways. Machine learning refined these to a six-gene panel (LY9, CD244, OLFML2B, TMEM59, TBC1D2, and FCER1G), with NNET achieving an AUC of 0.973 (95% CI: 0.951-0.996). Single-cell transcriptomics revealed cell-type-restricted expression, while proteomic data corroborated differential expression of key genes in sepsis-related contexts. Drug repurposing analysis prioritized candidates, highlighting its translational potential. Discussion This six-gene panel links immune-based diagnosis directly to therapeutic intervention. The identified genes not only serve as diagnostic biomarkers but also point to repurposable compounds. By connecting causal immune genes to existing drugs, the panel provides a clinical pathway from biomarker detection to targeted sepsis therapy. Conclusion This study establishes a causally grounded, diagnostically robust six-gene immune panel for sepsis with demonstrated therapeutic potential, offering a translational framework for biomarker-guided diagnosis and targeted immunotherapy.

papers.title: Defining glioma ecosystem states with AI-driven single-cell and spatial multi-omics: immune-niche reprogramming and therapeutic vulnerabilities.
papers.authors: Qin Z, Zhang Y, Wen B, Li J, Chen Z, Li X, Kong D.
papers.abstract: Objective To define clinically relevant glioma ecosystem states (recurrent spatial configurations of malignant programs and microenvironmental niches) and identify immune-niche-dependent therapeutic vulnerabilities using single-nucleus, spatial, tissue, and machine-learning analyses. Methods Public multi-omics datasets were integrated with institutional single-nucleus RNA sequencing from 12 tumors, spatial transcriptomics from 6 IDH-wildtype glioblastomas, multiplex immunofluorescence in 138 FFPE cases, and glioma-macrophage co-culture assays. Results Three ecosystem states were identified. The hypoxic myeloid-mesenchymal state showed the highest MES-like, hypoxia, SPP1/APOE myeloid, and temozolomide-resistance scores, the lowest CD8 + T-cell density, and the shortest tumor-myeloid distance. In 96 IDH-wildtype glioblastomas, this state independently predicted shorter progression-free survival (HR 2.19, 95% CI 1.22-3.92) and overall survival (HR 2.07, 95% CI 1.12-3.81) after adjustment for major clinical and molecular covariates. Defactinib plus temozolomide reduced viability, colony formation, and migration by 56.0%, 61.3%, and 57.8%, respectively, under macrophage-conditioned culture. Conclusion Spatially organized tumor-immune ecosystems provide prognostic information and highlight potentially actionable SPP1-CD44/FAK-SRC signaling in glioblastoma as a candidate target for individualized therapeutic stratification approaches.

papers.title: Immune checkpoint gene-based tumor-immune phenotypes stratify prognosis and immunotherapy-associated remodeling in cutaneous melanoma: a multi-cohort transcriptomic and single-cell re-analysis.
papers.authors: Mao Q, Yang S, Gong M.
papers.abstract: Background Immune checkpoint inhibitor responses in cutaneous melanoma are heterogeneous. We investigated immune checkpoint gene (ICG)-based tumor phenotypes, their immune and survival associations, treatment-associated transcriptional changes, and interferon-γ (IFN-γ)-responsive gene expression in melanoma cell lines. Methods We clustered 47 immune checkpoint genes in 472 TCGA-SKCM tumors and assessed survival using one tumor per patient. Cox models adjusted for AJCC stage, age and sex, with a stage-stratified sensitivity model. GSE91061 comprised 109 RNA-seq samples from 65 patients, including 43 paired pretreatment/on-treatment cases. We reanalyzed all 16,291 GSE120575 immune cells using the deposited log2(TPM+1) values, aggregated expression and composition within 48 biopsies from 32 patients, and accounted for repeated patients, time point and therapy. Canonical marker plots and full gene-set definitions were supplied. Cell-line RT-qPCR assessed CD274, CXCL10 and HLA-A expression after recombinant human IFN-γ treatment at 10 or 100 ng/mL for 24 or 48 h (PeproTech), with four independent biological replicates measured in technical triplicate. Results ICG-high, ICG-mid and ICG-low phenotypes included 136, 203 and 133 tumors. The ICG score correlated with the CD8 T-cell signature (Spearman ρ = 0.828, P = 5.06 × 10 -120 ). In 454 evaluable unique patients, median overall survival was 4930, 2192, 1487 days (log-rank P = 1.50e-05). Among 404 complete cases with 190 deaths, ICG-high versus ICG-low was associated with survival after adjustment (HR 0.34, 95% CI 0.22-0.51; P = 2.68e-07), with a concordant stage-stratified estimate (HR 0.35, 95% CI 0.23-0.53; P = 6.40e-07). Paired on-treatment ICG scores increased (median change 0.115; P = 0.012). At the biopsy level, immune-cell IFN-α and IFN-γ scores were higher in nonresponders after adjustment for time point and therapy (P = 1.29e-04 and P = 0.004, respectively). Conclusion ICG phenotypes were associated with immune-expression profiles and overall survival after adjustment for AJCC stage, age and sex. Paired bulk transcriptomes showed increased IFN-related expression during treatment, whereas the single-cell cohort showed higher immune-cell IFN scores in nonresponders. Together, these findings describe the relationship of checkpoint and IFN programs to immune context, treatment time and clinical outcome.

papers.title: An FCN1 + macrophage-associated SEMA3C-NRP1 axis is linked to fibroblast reprogramming in RA-ILD.
papers.authors: Su R, Song L, Chen X, Liu Y, Yang Y, Zhang C, Du J, Song D, Xiao L, Xie L, Han Z.
papers.abstract: Introduction Rheumatoid arthritis-associated interstitial lung disease (RA-ILD) is a major extra-articular complication of rheumatoid arthritis and a leading cause of morbidity and mortality. Unlike idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis (IPF), RA-ILD develops in the context of systemic immune activation, but the cellular basis linking inflammation to fibroblast-state changes remains incompletely understood. Methods We performed single-cell RNA sequencing on lung tissues from healthy donors, patients with RA-ILD, and patients with IPF, complemented by spatial validation and in vitro experiments. Results In this cohort, RA-ILD lungs showed an increased proportion of FCN1⁺ inflammatory macrophages within the macrophage compartment, whereas IPF lungs were dominated by SPP1⁺ macrophages. Trajectory and cell-cell communication analyses identified an RA-ILD-enriched matrix-fibroblast-to-CXCR4⁺ lipofibroblast program and a predicted SEMA3C-NRP1 interaction between inflammatory macrophage populations and fibroblasts; these patterns were not detected in the IPF or healthy-control samples analyzed here. Multiplex immunofluorescence showed macrophage-associated SEMA3C signal in spatial proximity to NRP1⁺ fibroblasts within fibrotic regions. A flow-sorted inflammatory monocyte/macrophage-enriched population from RA-ILD lungs had higher supernatant SEMA3C levels and was associated with shifts in MRC-5 fibroblast markers from EBF1/PDGFRA toward APOE/CXCR4. Recombinant SEMA3C reproduced this marker-defined shift, whereas pharmacological NRP1 inhibition attenuated it; an orthogonal THP-1 overexpression model produced concordant results. Discussion These data support an association between an inflammatory macrophage-SEMA3C-NRP1 axis and fibroblast-state remodeling in the studied RA-ILD samples. Because the RA-ILD cohort was small and did not include other CTD-ILD subtypes, the findings should not be interpreted as establishing RA-ILD specificity or a fully profibrotic functional phenotype.

An inflammatory monocyte/macrophage-enriched fraction isolated from lung tissue and MRC-5 fibroblasts were used in complementary in vitro experiments. papers.title: Neutrophil-microglia communication through the C3-C3aR1 axis contributes to secondary neuroinflammation after traumatic brain injury.
papers.authors: Ma T, Zhang Y, Wang X, Ren X, Jiao L, Pang K, Liu C, Zhou Z, Zhao P, Zhang H, Fu Y, Li L, Li Y, Zhao Z.
papers.abstract: Background Traumatic brain injury (TBI) triggers a rapidly evolving neuroinflammatory response that contributes to secondary brain injury. Although infiltrating leukocytes and resident microglia are both prominent components of this response, the cellular signals that connect peripheral immune-cell recruitment to microglial state remodeling remain incompletely defined. Methods We integrated and reanalyzed publicly available single-cell RNA-sequencing datasets from mouse TBI models to define temporal changes in brain-cell composition and transcriptional states. CellChat and NicheNet were used to prioritize candidate neutrophil-to-microglia signaling pathways. The predicted cellular distribution of C3 and C3aR1 was evaluated by immunofluorescence and flow cytometry. The effects of JR14a treatment on microglial inflammatory responses, blood-brain barrier (BBB) integrity, and neurological outcomes were examined in a mouse TBI model. Single-Cell rEgulatory Network Inference and Clustering (SCENIC), CellOracle, a gene regulatory network inference and in silico transcription-factor perturbation framework, and scTenifoldKnk, a single-cell gene regulatory network-based virtual knockout framework, were used for gene regulatory network inference and in silico transcription-factor perturbation analyses in C3ar1 -high microglia. Results Analysis of 254,512 cells revealed a transient increase in infiltrating neutrophils during the acute phase of TBI and the emergence of inflammatory microglial states. CellChat and NicheNet independently prioritized C3-associated signaling between neutrophils and Microglia4. C3 expression was enriched in infiltrating neutrophils, whereas C3ar1 was preferentially expressed by inflammatory microglia. Flow cytometry showed that C3aR1-positive microglia expressed higher levels of IL-1β and TNF-α than C3aR1-negative microglia. JR14a treatment reduced microglial inflammatory cytokine production, preserved Claudin-5 expression, limited Evans blue extravasation, and improved neurological and cognitive outcomes after TBI. Exploratory regulatory analyses further prioritized Ets2, Fosl2, and Irf7 as candidate regulators of the C3ar1 -high microglial program. Conclusions These findings implicate a neutrophil-associated C3/C3a-C3aR1 communication pathway in inflammatory microglial remodeling after TBI and support further investigation of C3aR1-associated signaling as a therapeutic target for secondary neuroinflammation.

papers.title: The mucosal immune microenvironment in chronic pharyngitis: epithelial barrier dysfunction, inflammatory persistence, and therapeutic perspectives.
papers.authors: Sun Y, Hong Z, Guo Y, Cui H, Jiang Y, Yu Q.
papers.abstract: Chronic pharyngitis is a clinically heterogeneous condition in which persistent throat symptoms, visible mucosal abnormalities, and underlying biological processes do not necessarily coincide. This critical narrative review synthesizes evidence from human chronic pharyngitis, experimental injury models, adjacent upper-airway disorders, and other mucosal systems to examine how epithelial barrier function, innate and adaptive immunity, microbial ecology, sensory signaling, and tissue repair may contribute to disease persistence. Experimental studies identify epithelial injury and activation of shared inflammatory and stress-response pathways, while human observations highlight substantial variation in anatomical site, microbial findings, immune organization, and treatment response. Adaptive immune responses appear strongly context dependent; microbial community changes are most informative when linked to organism viability, metabolite production, host sensing, or colonization resistance; and sensory pathways may contribute to symptoms partly independently of measurable inflammation. We propose that persistent disease can arise through three overlapping routes: continued exposure, durable alteration of tissue responsiveness, and incomplete resolution or repair, with microbial and sensory processes acting as modifiers. This framework separates symptom improvement, biological target engagement, and durable restoration of tissue function as distinct therapeutic outcomes. Future studies should prioritize anatomically precise longitudinal cohorts, site-resolved single-cell and spatial profiling, functional perturbation in primary pharyngeal systems, and mechanism-informed trials with follow-up after treatment withdrawal. By linking clinical presentation to local biological function and recovery trajectories, chronic pharyngitis may be reclassified into reproducible biological subgroups that support more precise mechanistic investigation and treatment.

figure.caption: Evidence contexts and proposed mucosal interactions in chronic pharyngitis. Representative mechanisms discussed in Sections 3–8 include epithelial stress signaling, junctional and permeability changes, epithelial differentiation, ciliary function, and mucociliary clearance, innate immune sensing, adaptive immune regulation, and tissue repair pathways ( 8 – 13 ). papers.title: Bringing translational structure to complex immune-mediated conditions: the ACT (Activation-Constraint-Tissue Context) framework for divergent phenotypes.
papers.authors: Lorsung JJ.
papers.abstract: Immune-mediated outcomes diverge across individuals with similar genetic backgrounds and environmental exposures, reflecting trajectories through a dynamic, context-dependent, and partially stochastic state space rather than fixed molecular endpoints. Despite advances in systems immunology, computational modeling, and multi-omic profiling, translating this complexity into clinically actionable reasoning remains difficult: these disciplines generate increasingly detailed representations of immune behavior that deepen mechanistic understanding while raising barriers to integration across clinical, experimental, and computational domains. A clinician at the bedside cannot reason across tens of thousands of molecular variables, cell states, pathways, and contextual modifiers simultaneously. We adopt a reduction-oriented perspective - not because immune data are insufficient, but because high-dimensional biological information must be organized into a reduced representational space before it can support cross-domain reasoning. When a system is too complex to reason about directly, progress may depend on identifying a minimal set of variables that preserves explanatory power while enabling tractable inference. Rather than modeling the immune system in full mechanistic detail, we seek a constrained representation capturing the minimal structure necessary to characterize clinically observable immune phenotypes, consistent with principles from state-space modeling, dimensionality reduction, and systems biology. Here, we introduce ACT - Activation, Constraint, and Tissue Context - a reduced-dimensional immune phenotype space for reasoning about immune state across systemic and tissue-localized compartments. Within ACT, clinical observations, laboratory measurements, and multi-omic data are interpreted as projections of a latent immune state that evolves over time under environmental influence, host predisposition, therapeutic intervention, tissue context, and stochastic perturbation. Immune phenotype is thus represented not as a static label, but as a trajectory through reduced immune-state space. ACT does not infer molecular mechanism directly from phenotypic or reduced-state data. Instead, it provides a structured mapping from data to state, state to trajectory, and trajectory to pathway-level hypothesis generation - linking parsimonious state representation with trajectory-based reasoning to offer a conceptual scaffold for translating between clinical observation, multi-omic data, and pathway-level hypothesis generation in complex immune-mediated conditions. The goal is not to replace high-resolution molecular data, systems immunology, or mechanistic modeling, but to provide a common translational coordinate system for reasoning about immune phenotype across scales of observation and disciplinary boundaries - supporting communication, interpretation, and hypothesis generation across clinical, experimental, and computational domains.

figure.label: Figure 1
figure.caption: ACT as a reduced-dimensional representation of latent immune state. (A) Observed projections Y(t): clinical, laboratory, and molecular/omic measurements provide partial, noisy observations of immune state. (B) Latent immune state S(t), shaped by host predisposition, environmental exposures, therapeutic intervention, tissue microenvironment, and stochastic perturbation. (C) Reduced ACT state Z(t) = φ(S(t)), with the estimated position shown as a posterior distribution reflecting uncertainty. (D) Definitions of the Activation, Constraint, and Tissue Context axes.

papers.title: Immune-chondrocyte ligand-receptor axes in osteoarthritis: microenvironmental control of inflammation, matrix remodeling, and chondrocyte fate.
papers.authors: Liu M, Zhong C, Yuan L, Tu Y, Wang K, Wang W.
papers.abstract: Osteoarthritis (OA) is increasingly recognized as a whole-joint disease shaped by chronic low-grade inflammation, matrix damage, mechanical stress, and failed tissue repair. Beyond the traditional view of cartilage wear, emerging evidence indicates that immune-chondrocyte ligand-receptor (LR) communication plays a central role in translating microenvironmental cues into disease-relevant chondrocyte phenotypes. In this narrative review, we summarize major immune-derived or inflammation-amplified LR axes that regulate OA progression, including cytokine pathways such as IL-1β-IL-1R, TNF-α-TNFR, IL-6-IL-6R/gp130, and IL-17-IL-17R; chemokine axes such as CXCL12-CXCR4 and CCL2-CCR2; DAMP-PRR pathways involving HMGB1, S100A8/A9, TLRs, and RAGE; and ECM-associated signaling through CD44 and integrins. These axes collectively drive chondrocyte catabolic activation, hypertrophic differentiation, senescence, inflammatory cell death, autophagy dysfunction, and impaired matrix repair. We further discuss how single-cell sequencing, spatial transcriptomics, multiplex imaging, and computational LR inference are redefining OA as a spatially organized disorder of immune-chondrocyte and multicellular joint communication. Finally, we highlight therapeutic opportunities, including receptor-level modulation, macrophage reprogramming, local intra-articular delivery, and LR-axis-based patient stratification. Understanding immune-chondrocyte LR networks may enable precision strategies that suppress pathological inflammation while preserving repair-oriented signaling in OA.

figure.label: Figure 1
figure.caption: Cellular and tissue landscape of immune–chondrocyte communication in osteoarthritis. Immune cells, synovial fibroblasts, infrapatellar fat pad-associated cells, subchondral bone cells, vascular cells, and damaged extracellular matrix contribute soluble or matrix-derived signals that influence chondrocyte behavior. The figure distinguishes direct immune cell–chondrocyte signaling from stromal relay and matrix-derived communication and summarizes their convergence on inflammation, matrix catabolism, senescence, and impaired cartilage homeostasis.

papers.title: Development and temporal validation of an explainable machine learning model for predicting in-hospital diabetic foot ulcer in patients with type 2 diabetes using inflammatory-nutritional composite indices.
papers.authors: Wang X, Li C, Tuo Y, Zhao B, Xiahati A, Fan L, Wahafu P.
papers.abstract: Objective This study aimed to develop and temporally validate explainable machine learning models for predicting in-hospital new-onset DFU in hospitalized patients with type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) using routinely available admission variables and inflammatory-nutritional composite indices. Methods This retrospective prediction-model study enrolled 550 consecutive hospitalized patients with T2DM admitted between January 2022 and December 2024. Patients admitted during 2022-2023 ( n = 400) constituted the development cohort, whereas those admitted in 2024 ( n = 150) served as an independent temporal validation cohort. Candidate predictors included demographic characteristics, diabetes duration, routine laboratory biomarkers, ankle-brachial index (ABI), and inflammatory-nutritional composite indices, including neutrophil percentage-to-albumin ratio (NPAR), albumin-to-neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio (ANLR), hemoglobin-albumin-lymphocyte-platelet score (HALP), systemic immune-inflammation index (SII), and C-reactive protein-to-albumin ratio (CRP/ALB). Candidate variables were screened using univariable logistic regression followed by least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO) regression. Logistic regression, random forest, LightGBM, and XGBoost models were developed and evaluated using the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC), average precision (AP), sensitivity, specificity, F1-score, Brier score, calibration analysis, and decision curve analysis (DCA). Model interpretability was assessed using SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP). Results During hospitalization, 66 patients (12.0%) developed DFU. Eleven predictors were retained after feature selection, including age, diabetes duration, neutrophil percentage, C-reactive protein, high-density lipoprotein cholesterol, glycated hemoglobin, ABI, NPAR, ANLR, HALP, and SII. In the temporal validation cohort, logistic regression had the highest observed discrimination (AUC = 0.976; bootstrap 95% CI, 0.936-0.992), with a sensitivity of 0.944, specificity of 0.932, and F1-score of 0.773 at the prespecified threshold; however, its Hosmer-Lemeshow test indicated evidence of lack of fit ( P = 0.001). LightGBM had the lowest Brier score (0.064), whereas XGBoost achieved an AUC of 0.945, a Brier score of 0.067, and a Hosmer-Lemeshow P value of 0.350. At the prespecified thresholds, LightGBM and XGBoost sensitivities were only 0.056 and 0.389, respectively. SHAP analysis identified ANLR, glycated hemoglobin, HALP, age, and SII as the five most influential XGBoost predictors. Because the temporal validation cohort contained only 18 DFU events, these performance estimates should be interpreted cautiously. Conclusion Admission-based machine learning models showed high observed discrimination for in-hospital DFU risk stratification, but no model was uniformly superior across discrimination, calibration, and threshold-dependent sensitivity. The small number of validation events, possible redundancy among mathematically overlapping predictors, omitted established foot-risk variables, and the low sensitivity of LightGBM and XGBoost at their prespecified thresholds preclude direct use as screening tools. Prospective multicenter validation, formal assessment of predictor redundancy, threshold recalibration, and clinical-impact evaluation are required before implementation.

papers.title: FLT3 expression and immune-associated transcriptional signatures in prostate cancer.
papers.authors: Cui Y, Song T, Wang X, Wan Z, Mao L.
papers.abstract: Background Bulk transcriptomic profiles combine signals from malignant, stromal, and immune cells. This study examined immune-associated gene expression in prostate cancer using bulk and single-cell transcriptomic data, and separately assessed the effects of FLT3 knockdown in prostate cancer cell lines. Methods We screened 502 sample records from 497 patients and identified genes shared by ImmuneScore-associated differential expression and a weighted gene co-expression network module. Candidate genes were compared with four functional gene sets. We analyzed associations between FLT3 expression and immune-related signatures, examined single-cell expression patterns, and assessed FLT3 knockdown using two independent siRNAs in DU145 and 22Rv1 cells. Results The screening identified 64 shared genes, and comparison with the functional gene sets prioritized FLT3 and AIM2. FLT3 expression was associated with several immune-cell signatures; associations were stronger for total T-cell and B-cell signatures than for the CD8-positive T-cell signature. Single-cell analyses suggested FLT3 expression in cells annotated as monocytes. In DU145 and 22Rv1 cells, both FLT3-targeting siRNAs reduced growth and colony formation, reduced Transwell migration and invasion readouts, and altered epithelial-mesenchymal transition markers. Conclusion The tissue analyses support an association between FLT3 expression and immune-related transcriptional signals. The cell-line findings describe a separate in vitro phenotype and do not establish how FLT3 relates to lymphocyte infiltration. These findings do not establish a causal immune-regulatory mechanism or prognostic utility.

figure.label: Figure 1
figure.caption: Study workflow. TCGA-PRAD transcriptomic and clinical data were analyzed with ESTIMATE, differential-expression analysis, and weighted gene co-expression network analysis (WGCNA). Candidate genes were evaluated by survival, functional enrichment, immune infiltration, pan-cancer, and predicted drug response analyses. GSE221603 single-cell RNA sequencing data were used to localize FLT3 expression and infer intercellular communication. FLT3 was subsequently silenced in DU145 and 22Rv1 cells for in vitro functional assessment.

papers.title: Age-dependent differences in SARS-CoV-2 entry-factor expression and innate immune responses between pediatric and adult liver organoids.
papers.authors: Xue T, Hu J, Liu Z, Zhu L, Zhao Y, Ren X, Xu L, Li X, Lu J, Wang L.
papers.abstract: Background Since early 2022, a global surge in cases of severe acute hepatitis of unknown origin (AHUO) in children has been reported, with no definitive aetiology established. Epidemiological evidence suggests a potential link to SARS-CoV-2 infection, particularly during Omicron-predominant periods, yet the mechanisms underlying the apparently higher susceptibility of children to SARS-CoV-2-related liver injury remain poorly understood. This study used non-tumorous (tumor-adjacent) liver organoids derived from pediatric and adult donors to compare viral RNA accumulation and host immune responses to SARS-CoV-2 wild-type (WT) and Omicron (BA.1/BA.2) variants, aiming to explore the possible role of SARS-CoV-2 in pediatric acute hepatitis. Methods Liver organoids were established from non-tumorous (tumor-adjacent) liver tissue of three adult patients with hepatocellular carcinoma and three pediatric patients with hepatoblastoma, collected between February and December 2022. Organoids were infected with SARS-CoV-2 WT, Omicron BA.1 or BA.2 at a multiplicity of infection (MOI) of 0.1. Viral loads in supernatants and intracellular viral RNA were quantified by RT-qPCR at 24 and 48 h post-infection (hpi). At 48 hpi, RNA-seq was performed to profile transcriptomic changes and pathway enrichment. Additionally, single-cell RNA-seq data were used to compare baseline expression of SARS-CoV-2 entry-associated genes between pediatric and adult hepatocytes. Results Pediatric hepatocytes showed significantly higher basal expression of entry-related genes, including ASGR1, KREMEN1, CTSB, CTSL, and VIM, than adult cells. Both pediatric and adult liver organoids were permissive to WT and Omicron, but Omicron BA.1/BA.2 yielded higher intracellular viral RNA levels than WT, with notably higher intracellular viral RNA burden in pediatric organoids. RNA-seq revealed that Omicron infection induced a more pronounced innate-immune-associated transcriptional response in pediatric organoids-encompassing interferon signaling, RIG-I-like receptor and Toll-like receptor pathways-alongside relative downregulation of adaptive immune-pathway transcripts. In adult organoids, transcriptomic divergence between Omicron and WT was less pronounced. Compared with adults, Omicron-infected pediatric organoids upregulated interferon-γ signaling and other innate immune-associated transcriptional programs, while downregulating adaptive immune-pathway transcripts; key receptors such as ACE2 and TMPRSS4 remained consistently higher in pediatric organoids across all viral strains. Conclusion Pediatric liver organoids accumulate higher levels of Omicron viral RNA than WT-infected organoids and mount a stronger innate-immune transcriptional response alongside relative downregulation of adaptive immune-pathway transcripts, correlating with elevated expression of viral entry factors. These age-dependent in vitro differences raise the hypothesis that SARS-CoV-2, particularly Omicron, could contribute to hepatocyte injury in children; however, this organoid-based model does not include patients with acute hepatitis of unknown origin and cannot establish a causal or epidemiological link, which will require dedicated prospective clinical and mechanistic studies.

figure.caption: Differential expression of SARS-CoV-2 entry-related genes in hepatocytes from hepatoblastoma (HB) versus hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) peritumor liver tissues. Boxplots compare expression of ASGR1, ANPEP, VIM, CTSB, CTSL and KREMEN1. Each dot represents an individual patient donor. To avoid pseudoreplication, raw UMI counts of hepatocytes were aggregated per donor for donor-level pseudobulk analysis. Differential expression was assessed using DESeq2. p -values were corrected for multiple-gene testing by the Benjamini–Hochberg false-discovery-rate procedure; adjusted p -values are shown.

papers.title: MTA1 promotes hepatocellular carcinoma progression by remodeling the immune microenvironment and regulating drug resistance gene networks: an integrated multi-database analysis.
papers.authors: Jin W, Chen L, Yang M, Zhou J, Wang B.
papers.abstract: Background Resistance to immunotherapy, chemotherapy, and targeted therapy remains a significant challenge in hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC). The relationships between metastasis-associated protein 1 (MTA1), multidrug resistance (MDR) networks, and the tumor immune microenvironment remain poorly understood. This study investigated associations between MTA1 expression, prognosis, treatment-related genes, and immune-related features in HCC. Methods Bioinformatics analyses integrated data from the Tumor Immune Estimation Resource (TIMER), The Cancer Genome Atlas (TCGA), and the Human Protein Atlas (HPA). Pearson correlation analysis was employed to characterize the co-expression patterns between MTA1 and genes associated with different forms of therapeutic resistance. Clinical tissue immunohistochemistry assessed MTA1 expression and cellular localization. Candidate MTA1-associated compounds were screened using the Comparative Toxicogenomics Database (CTD), and their predicted interactions with MTA1 were assessed by molecular docking. Gene set enrichment analysis (GSEA) examined MTA1-associated signaling pathways. Results MTA1 was markedly upregulated in HCC tissues, and elevated expression was significantly associated with shorter overall survival (OS), disease-specific survival (DSS), and progression-free interval (PFI). MTA1 expression correlated positively with infiltration scores for T helper cells, central memory T cells, and T helper 2 cells, and negatively with scores for dendritic cells, plasmacytoid dendritic cells, and γδ T cells. Positive correlations were also observed with the immune checkpoint genes CD274 and PDCD1 . MTA1 expression was significantly and positively correlated with genes related to chemotherapy, lenvatinib, sorafenib, broader tyrosine kinase inhibitor (TKI) treatment, and immunotherapy. Immunohistochemistry showed predominantly nuclear localization of MTA1. Estradiol and ethinyl estradiol were identified as candidate compounds, with predicted docking scores of -8.1 and -8.8, respectively. GSEA associated MTA1 expression with enrichment of treatment-related signaling pathways, including phosphoinositide 3-kinase/protein kinase B/mechanistic target of rapamycin (PI3K/AKT/mTOR) and Wnt signaling. Conclusions MTA1 expression was associated with prognosis, immune-related features, and treatment-related gene expression in HCC. These findings support further evaluation of MTA1 as a prognostic biomarker and candidate therapeutic target, and provide a basis for experimental investigation of MTA1-related mechanisms and candidate compounds.
