papers.title: Integrated single-cell and bulk transcriptomic profiling reveals coagulation-associated heterogeneity and prognostic SPINT2 in acute myeloid leukemia.
papers.authors: Wang Z, Han M, Zhang D, Cui L, Zhang L, Wang B.
papers.abstract: Background Coagulation-associated genes (CARGs) have been implicated in tumor progression and immune regulation, but their cellular heterogeneity and prognostic relevance in acute myeloid leukemia (AML) remain incompletely understood. Here, we sought to characterize the cellular and molecular landscape of CARGs in AML and to identify CARG-associated prognostic determinants with potential functional relevance. Methods Single-cell RNA sequencing data were first analyzed to characterize CARG activity across distinct cellular populations in AML. Bulk transcriptomic datasets were subsequently integrated to identify CARG-related molecular subtypes and establish a prognostic scoring system using machine-learning approaches. The associations of the CARG prognostic score with biological pathways, immune characteristics, and drug sensitivity were further evaluated. Single-cell expression patterns, cell-cell communication, and computational perturbation analyses were used to investigate key prognostic genes, followed by experimental validation in AML cells. Results Single-cell transcriptomic analysis revealed marked heterogeneity of CARG activity across AML cell populations, with particularly high activity observed in erythroid and cycling erythroid populations. Building on these cellular-level observations, bulk transcriptomic analysis identified three distinct CARG-related molecular subtypes with significantly different survival outcomes and biological characteristics. An integrated machine-learning framework established a seven-gene CARG prognostic score that showed prognostic stratification in both the development and independent external validation cohorts. High CARG prognostic scores were associated with distinct metabolic and immune-related transcriptional programs and differential ex vivo responses to several therapeutic agents. Among the model features, SPINT2 showed prominent prognostic importance and displayed cell-type-specific expression at single-cell resolution. Single-cell analysis revealed cell-type-specific SPINT2 expression, while computational perturbation analyses suggested associations with erythroid/heme-related and oxidative metabolic programs. Functional experiments further demonstrated that SPINT2 silencing suppressed AML cell proliferation and promoted apoptosis. Conclusion Our study defines a cellular and molecular landscape of CARG heterogeneity in AML and establishes an integrated CARG-based framework for prognostic stratification. The combination of single-cell and bulk transcriptomic analyses, computational perturbation, and functional validation supports SPINT2 as a candidate gene with functional relevance to AML cell growth and survival and provides a basis for further investigation of coagulation-associated biology in AML.
papers.venue: Frontiers in cell and developmental biology

papers.title: Interferon regulatory factor 1: a key transcriptional node orchestrating macrophage polarization: mechanisms and therapeutic potential.
papers.authors: Cao S, Feng S, Gao Y, Sun Z, Bai S, Su X.
papers.abstract: Macrophageexhibit remarkable functional plasticity and adopt M1-like pro-inflammatory or M2-like anti-inflammatory/pro-resolving states in response to microenvironmental stimuli. Notably, this binary functional classification originates largely from in-vitro experimental systems; tissue-resident macrophages in vivo display a continuous spectrum of activation phenotypes rather than discrete subsets. Dysregulated macrophage polarization drives the pathogenesis of infectious diseases, malignancies, and metabolic-inflammatory disorders. Interferon regulatory factor 1 (IRF1) is a pivotal transcription factor governing macrophage fate, yet its multilayered regulatory circuits and context-dependent dual impacts on M1-like and M2-like transcriptional programs remain to be systematically summarized. This review synthesizes recent advances in IRF1-centered regulatory networks of macrophage polarization. We recapitulate IRF1 crosstalk with core signaling cascades including JAK/STAT, TLR/MyD88 and IFN-γ pathways, as well as its transcriptional control of target genes such as iNOS, IL-12, and CXCL10. Multi-layer regulatory mechanisms modulating IRF1 activity are outlined, including transcriptional, epigenetic, non-coding-RNA-mediated post-transcriptional, and post-translational modifications. We further dissect IRF1-linked immunometabolic reprogramming and epigenetic remodeling, and describe its versatile pathophysiological roles in infection, cancer and metabolic inflammatory diseases based on multi-omics and single-cell sequencing evidence. Collectively, this review illustrates IRF1 as a key transcriptional node that orchestrates macrophage polarization, and highlights prospective therapeutic targets and intervention strategies for IRF1-associated immune-mediated disorders.

papers.title: Overexpression of TUBA1A suppresses bladder cancer progression with potential modulation of autophagic activity and macrophage polarization.
papers.authors: Song DM, Lu H, Shu YC, Xu JJ, He YB, Duan H, Jin YY, Chen SL, Duan SC, Jing GH, Wen JM, Tong M.
papers.abstract: Background Bladder urothelial carcinoma (BUC) exhibits high recurrence and poor prognosis, with limited efficacy of current immunotherapies. The role of the aggrephagy-related gene TUBA1A in the BUC immune microenvironment remains unclear. Methods Single-cell transcriptomic data from public repositories were analyzed to characterize the immune microenvironment. Non-negative matrix factorization identified aggrephagy-related immune-stromal subtypes, and CellChat mapped intercellular interactions. TIDE validation and KEGG enrichment defined functional modules. TUBA1A expression and function were evaluated through qRT-PCR, Western blot, proliferation, migration, apoptosis assays, and transmission electron microscopy. THP-1-derived macrophages were treated with conditioned medium from control or TUBA1A-overexpressing bladder cancer cells in the presence or absence of the autophagy inhibitor chloroquine (CQ), and polarization markers were assessed by flow cytometry and qRT-PCR. In vivo xenograft models verified tumor growth effects. Results Single-cell analysis identified a TUBA1A-high macrophage subset with strong immune communication and immune activity. TUBA1A was significantly downregulated in BUC tissues and cell lines. TUBA1A overexpression inhibited proliferation, migration, and invasion, promoted apoptosis, and enhanced autophagic activity (increased LC3-II and ATG5, reduced SQSTM1/p62, and elevated autophagic vesicles). Conditioned medium from TUBA1A-overexpressing cells promoted M1-like polarization; CQ abolished the induction of the M1 markers IL-12 and CD86. In vivo , TUBA1A overexpression significantly suppressed xenograft tumor growth and reduced Ki-67 expression. Conclusion TUBA1A is downregulated in BUC and acts as a candidate regulator of autophagic activity and macrophage polarization. TUBA1A overexpression is associated with inhibition of BUC progression, and its promotion of M1-like macrophage polarization appears to require autophagic activity. TUBA1A may represent a promising biomarker and therapeutic target for BUC.

papers.title: MR-supported candidate genes and pathway analysis between ischemic stroke and osteoporosis: an integrated multi-omics study.
papers.authors: Li X, Lou Y, Zhao J, Xiong Z, Zhou X.
papers.abstract: Background The global prevalence of ischemic stroke (IS) and osteoporosis (OP) is rising, posing significant public health challenges in aging populations. We aimed to uncover shared genetic factors and elucidate the molecular mechanisms linking IS and OP to identify potential targets for integrated preventive and therapeutic interventions. Methods A comprehensive multi-omics analysis was performed to assess associations and molecular pathways connecting IS and OP. Summary statistics for IS and OP were integrated with expression quantitative trait loci data from the eQTLGen consortium (n = 4,463) to identify common significant single nucleotide polymorphisms (SNPs) related to both diseases. Follow-up transcriptomic profiling and single-cell RNA sequencing were employed to investigate functional pathways, regulatory networks, and cell-type-specific expression patterns associated with these loci. Finally, the expression levels of shared molecules were confirmed using animal models, and subsequent functional analyses were conducted on these genes. Results Two-sample Mendelian randomization identified FCGR2B and CYBB as exploratory MR-supported candidate genes with shared eQTL instruments. Transcriptome-wide analysis linked these loci to immune-metabolic pathways, including oxidative stress response (FDR = 0.003) and interferon-γ signaling (FDR = 0.01). Mouse-derived ischemic-stroke single-cell RNA-seq provided exploratory cell-type localization: Fcgr2b and Cybb were preferentially enriched in monocytes and macrophages (FDR Sirt1 was predominantly localized to endothelial cells and tissue stem cells in the diseased mouse microenvironment. Of note, the osteoporosis single-cell dataset (GSE147287) contained only one OP patient, and its cell-type patterns should therefore be interpreted as exploratory case observations rather than generalized findings. Regulatory network analysis identified the cisbp:M1399 transcription factor motif (NES = 4.12) with the highest enrichment score, which is predicted to separately regulate the transcription of FCGR2B, CYBB and SIRT1 . Pathway enrichment analysis revealed metabolic reprogramming (AUC = 0.78, p=0.004) as a key mechanistic node differentiating high-and low-expression cell groups. The expression levels of the shared molecules were validated in a mouse model. Conclusions This multi-omics study implicates immune-metabolic dysregulation as a shared pathological feature of ischemic stroke and osteoporosis. FCGR2B , CYBB and SIRT1 are exploratory MR-supported candidate genes putatively associated with both diseases, offering potential clues for dual-purpose preventive and therapeutic strategies for age-related IS-OP comorbidity.

papers.title: Viruses in the tumor immune microenvironment: implications for immunotherapy.
papers.authors: Chen X, Ni P, Li W, Wu M, Li J, Lu W, Li X, Wang L.
papers.abstract: The intricate interplay between viruses and the tumor immune microenvironment (TIME) plays a pivotal role in tumor initiation, progression, and response to immunotherapy. Viruses can directly infect tumor cells, modulate immune cell functions, and reshape cytokine networks, thereby influencing the composition and functionality of the TIME. This review systematically examines how viral infections impact TIME by altering tumor-infiltrating lymphocytes, cytokine profiles, and immune checkpoint expression. Additionally, the role of virus-associated antigens as immune targets and the mechanisms of virus-induced immune evasion that undermine immunotherapeutic efficacy are discussed. By integrating recent advances from single-cell omics, spatial transcriptomics, and clinical studies, this article aims to elucidate the core mechanisms underlying virus-TIME interactions. Furthermore, it highlights the therapeutic potential and challenges of virus-based immunotherapies, including oncolytic virotherapy and viral vector vaccines. This comprehensive overview provides a theoretical foundation for optimizing immunotherapeutic strategies that leverage viral components to enhance anti-tumor immunity and overcome immune resistance.

papers.title: Large-scale plasma proteomics identifies proteins and pathways associated with incident interstitial lung disease.
papers.authors: Kang Z, Zhu Y, Zhang J, Zhu C, Li P, Li K, Tong Q, Dai SM.
papers.abstract: Objective Reliable biomarkers for early interstitial lung disease (ILD) risk stratification are limited; therefore, we aimed to identify prediagnostic proteins associated with incident ILD and develop a long-term prediction model. Methods We analyzed 52,743 UK Biobank participants without baseline ILD and measured 2,923 plasma proteins. Cox models were used to identify proteins associated with incident ILD. Key predictors were selected using LASSO and sequential forward selection within a LightGBM framework. Model performance was assessed using the area under the curve (AUC) and SHAP. Prediagnostic protein trajectories were evaluated using LOESS and clustering. Single-cell transcriptomic data from human idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis lungs were used to explore cellular sources. Results During a mean follow-up period of 14.4 years, 814 ILD cases were identified in the cohort. A total of 277 proteins were significantly associated with incident ILD and enriched in immune activation and cytokine signaling pathways. Five proteins (GDF15, LAMP3, SFTPD, EDA2R, and WFDC2) were identified as dominant predictors. Trajectory analysis showed that several ILD-associated proteins deviated from control levels years before diagnosis and could be grouped into four distinct temporal clusters. GDF15, LAMP3, SFTPD, WFDC2, and EGFR showed detectable prediagnostic alterations more than a decade before ILD onset. Furthermore, connective tissue disease (CTD)-ILD displayed a distinct inflammatory proteomic profile, including CXCL13, CCL7, PDCD1, and TNFRSF4. When the five protein biomarkers were combined with clinical variables, the integrated model achieved relatively good predictive accuracy for ILD, with AUCs of 0.938 and 0.908 for 5-year and 10-year ILD risks, respectively. Single-cell analysis indicated that these proteins may predominantly originate from dysregulated alveolar and airway epithelial cells. Conclusion Plasma proteomics identified prediagnostic protein signatures associated with future ILD risk and improved long-term prediction when combined with clinical variables.

papers.title: Rational design of a multi-epitope vaccine targeting the stress-associated proteins for Mycoplasma fermentans via immunoinformatics.
papers.authors: He J, Mi J, Tang H, Zhang Z, Chen Z.
papers.abstract: Mycoplasma fermentans : ( M. fermentans ) is a clinically important opportunistic pathogen with intrinsic antibiotic resistance, highlighting the need for targeted intervention strategies. To address this, we applied immunoinformatics and reverse vaccinology to develop a multi-epitope vaccine (MEV) directed against its heat shock proteins (HSPs). The final construct comprised six computationally predicted linear B-cell epitopes, four cytotoxic T lymphocyte (CTL) epitopes, and five helper T lymphocyte (HTL) epitopes, sequentially joined by the specific linkers KK, AAY, and GPGPG. For improved antigen presentation, the vaccine was further equipped with a beta-defensin at the N-terminus and a dendritic cell-targeting signal peptide at the C-terminus. The MEV demonstrated promising antigenicity, as well as favorable structural stability and solubility. In silico cloning into pET-28a (+) indicated that efficient heterologous expression is feasible. Immune simulations predicted that a three-dose immunization schedule would trigger a robust and long-lasting secondary immune response. Additionally, the predicted mRNA secondary structure exhibited high thermodynamic stability, supporting the feasibility of the proposed construct for further expression evaluation. Although experimental validation and clinical evaluation are still required, these computational results strongly support the vaccine candidate's potential.

papers.title: Integrating proteomics to map immune landscape and protein biomarkers for risk stratification in childhood Langerhans cell histiocytosis.
papers.authors: Liu J, Shan H, Yuan J, Zhang W, Zheng Q, Liu H, Wang P, Lin H, Kuang C, Huang M, Guo K, Wang J, Jiang H, Xiao X.
papers.abstract: Background Langerhans cell histiocytosis (LCH) is a rare pediatric disease with marked clinical heterogeneity. Current risk stratification relies on the extent of organ involvement and risk-organ status, yet reliable protein biomarkers for distinguishing LCH subtypes are lacking. Methods We performed proteomic analysis on 56 formalin-fixed paraffin-embedded (FFPE) pediatric LCH tissue samples and 10 normal skin controls, quantifying 6, 914 proteins. Machine-learning approaches were integrated with weighted correlation network analysis for exploratory identification of candidate protein biomarkers and internal classification analysis. Candidate markers were validated by immunohistochemistry. The CIBERSORT deconvolution algorithm was employed to estimate the immune cell infiltration. Results Proteomic profiling clearly distinguished LCH from controls. Functional protein modules and candidate protein biomarkers were identified across different LCH subtypes. Significant differences in immune cell infiltration were also observed, revealing enhanced innate immune activation and cytotoxic T cell responses in multisystem LCH compared with single-system LCH, as well as in LCH with risk-organ involvement versus those without. In exploratory internal classification analyses, the SVM model yielded an accuracy, AUC, and F1 score of 1.000 (95% CI: 1.000-1.000) for distinguishing multisystem from single-system LCH. For risk-organ involvement, the KNN model yielded an accuracy of 0.800 (95% CI: 0.500-1.000) and an AUC of 0.880 (95% CI: 0.600-1.000). Conclusion To our knowledge, this is the first large-scale FFPE-based proteomic study in pediatric LCH to reveal subtype and risk specific protein signatures and associated immune cell profiles changes. These findings provide novel biological insights into LCH heterogeneity and identify candidate protein biomarkers associated with disease extent and risk-organ involvement. Further validation in larger independent cohorts is required before their predictive or clinical utility can be established.

papers.title: Microbiome-mitochondria crosstalk in neuro-oncology: molecular mechanisms, immunometabolic reprogramming, and therapeutic opportunities.
papers.authors: Dash D, Rajak M, Manothiya P, Koiri RK.
papers.abstract: Although the gut microbiome is increasingly recognized as an important regulator of metabolic, immune, and neurophysiological functions, and mitochondrial dysfunction is considered a hallmark of metabolic flexibility, oxidative stress, and resistance to therapy in cancers, the role of microbiome-derived cues and mitochondrial processes in brain tumors remains poorly understood. The Microbiome-Gut-Brain-Mitochondria Axis in Neuro-Oncology provides a framework for understanding metabolism and immunity in neuro-oncology by highlighting this axis and emphasizing its role in glioblastoma. Metabolites produced by the microbiome, including short-chain fatty acids, bile acid metabolites, tryptophan metabolites, and other microbial compounds, have been shown to affect the immune system, barrier function, cellular metabolism, and neural signaling. Mitochondria are capable of functioning as intracellular communication mechanisms that will help to decipher those signals in order to create energy, ROS, calcium communication, biogenesis of mitochondria, quality control, and apoptosis. These processes may contribute to metabolic plasticity in glioblastomas, including glycolytic, oxidative phosphorylation, and amino- and lipid-metabolic adaptations, mitochondrial transfer, adaptation to hypoxia, tumor cell stemness, and immune suppression in the tumor microenvironment. The article also discusses the relationships between microbiome-derived cues, mitochondria, and tumor-associated immune populations. Microbiome-derived and mitochondrial biomarkers, combined with multi-omics approaches, single-cell technologies, spatial biology, artificial intelligence, and new experimental models, may help to identify relevant microbiome-mitochondria signatures. Modulating the microbiome, mitochondria, and combination therapies appears promising for glioblastomas. However, the causative link between microbiome-derived mitochondrial mechanisms and human brain tumors remains unproven. The necessity of prospective and mechanistic studies of the microbiome, mitochondria, metabolism, immunity, and clinical aspects arises.

papers.title: Exploring biomarkers and regulatory mechanisms associated with 20 protein post-translational modifications in acute myocardial infarction based on transcriptomics.
papers.authors: Zhang J, Li B, Yang M, Lu J, Jiang H, Chen F.
papers.abstract: Background Acute myocardial infarction (AMI) is a critical condition resulting from coronary occlusion, leading to myocardial necrosis and dysfunction. Protein posttranslational modifications (PTMs) regulate key inflammatory and signaling pathways in its pathogenesis. Accordingly, exploring transcriptomic signatures of genes encoding PTM-regulatory factors may provide valuable insights for improving early diagnosis and therapeutic stratification in AMI. Methods Candidate genes were obtained by integrating transcriptomic data on AMI from public databases with a previously published gene set encoding regulators for 20 categories of protein PTMs. Differentially expressed genes (DEGs) were intersected with this PTM-regulator gene set to identify PTM-related DEGs. Machine learning approaches together with expression analyses were employed to identify diagnostic biomarkers. Their potential mechanisms were systematically elucidated via multidimensional analyses, including deep neural network (DNN) model construction, biological pathway analysis, immune landscape profiling, regulatory network reconstruction, and therapeutic compound prioritization. Clinical validation of the key biomarkers was performed using RT-qPCR. Results This study identified three biomarkers among PTM-regulator-related genes for AMI: GABARAPL1 , PELI1 , and NLRP3 . Enrichment profiling showed that all three biomarkers were prominently linked to pathways related to Leishmania infection. Correlation analysis of immune cell profiles showed that all three biomarkers were most strongly associated with plasmacytoid dendritic cells. Molecular regulatory network analysis uncovered their associated transcription factors, targeted miRNAs, and lncRNA interaction networks. Drug prediction and molecular docking identified several potential targeting compounds, among which 1,4-chrysenequinone exhibited docking scores of -7 kcal/mol and -8.9 kcal/mol with GABARAPL1 and PELI1 , respectively, while calcitriol showed a docking score of -10.1 kcal/mol with NLRP3, indicating strong predicted binding affinity. RT-qPCR clinical validation confirmed significant upregulation of GABARAPL1 , PELI1 , and NLRP3 in AMI patients (all P Conclusion Using transcriptome-based bioinformatics, this study identified and validated three transcriptomic biomarkers ( GABARAPL1 , PELI1 , and NLRP3 ) among genes encoding PTM-regulatory factors for AMI, offering molecular resources for future investigations into diagnostic and therapeutic targets in AMI.

papers.title: Identification and expression analysis of intergenic long non-coding RNAs (lincRNA) associated with stripe rust resistance in wheat.
papers.authors: Fang X, Wang X, Yang T, Wang Y, Ao X, Cao P, Gong P, Ma D.
papers.abstract: Introduction Long intergenic non-coding RNAs (lincRNAs) have emerged as important regulators of plant immune responses, yet their functional landscape in wheat ( Triticum aestivum ) during stripe rust ( Puccinia striiformis f. sp. tritici ) infection remains largely unexplored. Methods In this study, a genome-wide identification of lincRNAs was performed using strand-specific RNA-seq data from wheat leaves following Pst inoculation. Functional enrichment, co-expression, lincRNA-miRNA-mRNA network prediction, and AlphaFold-based protein-RNA structure prediction were used to characterize candidate lincRNAs. Results A total of 2,736 expressed lincRNAs were identified, of which 515 were differentially expressed during infection. Functional enrichment of genes located within 100 kb of the differentially expressed lincRNAs revealed significant associations with defense-related pathways, including MAPK signaling and plant-pathogen interaction. Coordinated expression patterns between lincRNAs and adjacent defense-related mRNAs suggested putative cis-regulatory associations. Furthermore, lincRNA-miRNA-mRNA network prediction identified 65 differentially expressed lincRNAs as potential endogenous target mimics for 21 conserved miRNAs, revealing a widespread competing endogenous RNA (ceRNA) regulatory network. Importantly, AlphaFold-based protein-RNA structure prediction demonstrated that the co-expressed lincRNA MSTRG.56980 forms a stable complex with the RGA1-type resistance protein TraesCS6B03G0179100. Discussion This provides a first computational prediction of a possible physical interaction between a wheat lincRNA and an immune receptor. These integrative findings substantially expand the current understanding of non-coding regulatory networks in wheat immunity and provide a foundational resource for prioritizing candidate lincRNAs as targets for enhancing stripe rust resistance.

papers.title: Single-cell profiling of dysfunctional NK cells in COVID-19: from immunization to acute infection and beyond.
papers.authors: Frigo A, Terzoli S, Marzano P, Coianiz N, Calvi M, Orlandi L, Balin S, Cazzetta V, Carletti A, Della Bella S, Mikulak J, Tarkowski M, Bonfanti M, Ferrari P, Ricciardelli E, Peano C, Riva A, Testa G, Voza A, Calcaterra F, Di Vito C, Mavilio D.
papers.abstract: Introduction Vaccination and natural infection with Severe Acute Respiratory Syndrome CoronaVirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2) confer immune protection through distinct mechanisms, however, their effects on Natural Killer (NK) cell responses remain poorly understood, particularly in relation to COVID-19 disease severity. NK cells, key mediators of anti-viral immunity, have been implicated in coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19) pathogenesis, where severe disease is associated with hyperactivated yet dysfunctional NK-cell states that likely impair viral control and contribute to tissue damage. Methods To define how vaccination and infection shape NK-cell biology, we performed longitudinal single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) of NK cells from SARS-CoV-2-naïve individuals receiving two doses of the BNT162b2mRNA vaccine. These longitudinal vaccine profiles were integrated with cross-sectional scRNA-seq datasets from unvaccinated patients with acute COVID-19 and from independent convalescent individuals, all enrolled before vaccine introduction. Results We identified distinct NK cell transcriptional programs associated with vaccination, acute infection and convalescence, with the most pronounced infection-related alterations observed in the severe form of the disease. These diverging transcriptional signatures correlate with differences in NK-cell subset composition and activation markers between vaccinated and infected individuals. Conclusions Taken together, these findings provide a rationale for future studies examining whether vaccine-associated NK-cell transcriptional programs contribute to durable immune protection.

papers.title: Single-cell and spatial transcriptomics in intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma: spatial immune ecosystems, metabolic remodeling, and immunotherapeutic implications.
papers.authors: Yan Y, Teng T, Luo X, Liu J, Wang J.
papers.abstract: Intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma (iCCA) is an aggressive liver malignancy characterized by pronounced cellular, spatial, and metabolic heterogeneity. Single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) and spatial transcriptomics (ST) are beginning to resolve this complexity by linking malignant, immune, stromal, and metabolic states to their tissue context. This review synthesizes recent single-cell and spatial studies of iCCA across four spatial contexts: adaptive immune regions containing tertiary lymphoid structures (TLSs), barriers formed by stromal and myeloid cells at the invasive front, myeloid niches shaped by hypoxia, and metastatic ecosystems involving immune and stromal cells. These niches connect tumor heterogeneity with immune regulation, stromal remodeling, metabolic adaptation, and therapeutic vulnerability. We also evaluate how crosstalk between metabolism and immunity shapes macrophage polarization, T-cell dysfunction, and treatment response, while distinguishing computationally inferred interactions from functionally supported mechanisms. The field is therefore moving from cataloging additional cell states and spatial niches toward establishing which ecosystem features are reproducible across cohorts, mechanistically supported, clinically measurable, and informative for treatment response. Current evidence supports a view of iCCA as a spatially organized and metabolically regulated tumor ecosystem that can guide biomarker development and rational immunotherapeutic strategies.

papers.title: Integrated time-series multi-omics reveals temporal reprogramming and inter-organ divergence in diabetic cardiorenal syndrome.
papers.authors: Gao SS, Wan G, Wang Q, An J, Yang Q, Liu C, Cai Y.
papers.abstract: Diabetes induces progressive transcriptional reprogramming in the heart and kidney, yet their tissue-specific temporal dynamics and cellular mechanisms remain incompletely understood. In this study, we employed a longitudinal design with dense sampling intervals, performing time-series bulk RNA-seq on heart and kidney tissues across six bi-weekly intervals from Control, high-fat diet (HF), diabetes (DM), and insulin-treated (INS) mice (n=38 total samples). To cross-validate and resolve cell-type-specific variations, these data were integrated with a public single-cell RNA-seq dataset (16 mouse kidneys) spanning Control, diabetic kidney disease (DKD), and SGLT2 inhibitor (SGLT2i) treatment groups. Principal component analysis and differential expression sequencing revealed a more pronounced, earlier transcriptional divergence in the kidney than in the heart under diabetic conditions. Using maSigPro regression analysis, we identified 74 core time-dependent genes in the kidney; hierarchical clustering showed that the major dynamic module was enriched in immunometabolic and inflammatory pathways. Single-cell dissection localized Enpp2 upregulation within injured proximal tubule cells (Inj.PT) of the DKD group, while MHC class I molecules (H2-K1 and H2-D1) were suppressed in immune cells. UpSet plot analysis demonstrated an overlap of these dynamic hub genes between bulk and single-cell cohorts. While insulin reversed systemic metabolic and early-phase immune aberrations in the bulk cohort, the single-cell dataset-derived from an independent SGLT2i-treated cohort-provided cellular resolution for key dynamic genes (Enpp2, H2-K1, H2-D1) and suggested that SGLT2i may similarly suppress Enpp2 in injured proximal tubule cells. These parallel observations from two distinct therapeutic interventions are hypothesis-generating and warrant direct comparative studies. These discovery-phase findings were validated by independent qPCR and immunohistochemical analyses. Taken together, this exploratory longitudinal analysis identifies tissue-specific temporal transcriptional reprogramming in diabetic heart and kidney, with evidence of partial modulation by insulin treatment.

papers.title: Epithelial-mesenchymal plasticity is associated with transcriptional variation in regulated cell death and immune signaling programs in lung adenocarcinoma.
papers.authors: Liu K, Liu J, Meng T, Liu J, Wu F.
papers.abstract: Background Epithelial-mesenchymal plasticity is associated with variation in regulated-cell-death (RCD) transcription and tumor-immune communication in lung adenocarcinoma (LUAD). We examined these relationships across single-cell, bulk-transcriptomic, and cell-line expression data. Methods GSE131907 UMI counts underwent quality control, normalization, dimensionality reduction, and Leiden clustering. Epithelial and mesenchymal programs were scored against expression-matched control genes; 40th/60th-percentile state assignments were compared with median and quartile rules. CNV profiles were inferred in 300 malignant-label cells and 100 normal epithelial references. Malignant-cell count pseudobulk and separate pro-/anti-apoptosis and pro-/anti-ferroptosis scores were analyzed. TCGA-LUAD included 539 tumors and 59 normal samples; overall survival was evaluated by median-split Kaplan-Meier analysis and Cox models adjusted for age, sex, and stage. RT-qPCR compared BIRC3, CXCR4, MALAT1, and GPX4 between TGF-β1-treated (10 ng/mL, 48 h) and vehicle-treated control groups in A549 and NCI-H1975 cells. Results The single-cell analysis retained 203,157 cells, including 24,341 malignant-label cells. Median inferred CNV burden was 3.15-fold higher in the malignant-label subset than in normal epithelial references. The malignant EMT-high fraction correlated positively with the myeloid fraction (ρ = 0.539, P = 0.012; BH-adjusted q = 0.059 across five comparisons). Tumor-versus-normal fold changes showed 91.5% direction concordance among genes significant in both platforms (ρ = 0.82). The EMT-RCD composite score was not independently associated with survival (HR = 0.973, 95% CI 0.829-1.141; P = 0.736). CXCR4 expression increased 2.43-fold in A549 and 2.12-fold in NCI-H1975 cells; BIRC3 and MALAT1 increased significantly only in A549 cells. Conclusion LUAD EMT-associated transcriptional heterogeneity coincides with variation in death-regulatory programs and myeloid composition. CXCR4 showed a consistent expression response in both cell lines, whereas the composite transcriptional score had no independent association with overall survival. These findings prioritize CXCR4-associated cell-state biology for further investigation.
papers.venue: Frontiers in cell and developmental biology

papers.title: Overcoming primary non-response to infliximab in ulcerative colitis: monocyte-derived PTGS2 as a therapeutic target.
papers.authors: Pu D, Kang X, Gou L, Li X, Wang P, Qi G, Liu JL, Zhang D.
papers.abstract: Background Primary non-response (PNR) to infliximab (IFX) remains a major therapeutic challenge in ulcerative colitis (UC). However, the molecular mechanisms underlying this treatment failure remains unelucidated. Therefore, there is an urgent need to identify the key drivers of PNR and develop effective interventions to improve therapeutic outcomes. Methods Human colonic RNA-sequencing data were analyzed to identify molecular features associated with PNR to IFX. Immune infiltration analysis, clinical sample validation, virtual gene knockout, and single-cell RNA sequencing were performed to characterize the immune landscape, identify the key regulatory molecule, and elucidate its underlying mechanisms and cellular source. Network pharmacology and molecular docking were employed to identify a potential therapeutic strategy targeting the key regulatory molecule, followed by mechanistic and functional validation in cell-based assays and therapeutic evaluation in a DSS-induced murine colitis model. Results Excessive colonic neutrophil infiltration marked PNR in UC prior to IFX treatment. PTGS2 positively correlated with neutrophil infiltration and was predominantly expressed in colonic CD14 + S100A9 + inflammatory monocytes. Virtual knockout of PTGS2 altered genes related to neutrophil chemotaxis, which were primarily enriched in the NF-κB signaling axis. Gegen Qinlian Decoction (GQD), a traditional Chinese herbal formula, was identified to target PTGS2 through multiple bioactive constituents, with quercetin exhibiting the highest binding affinity. Quercetin suppressed LPS-induced PTGS2 expression in inflammatory monocytes, thereby inhibiting the NF-κB/CXCL8 signaling and attenuating neutrophil chemotaxis, as further supported by PTGS2 knockdown and overexpression experiments. In vivo , GQD markedly reduced PTGS2 expression and neutrophil accumulation in the inflamed colon, thereby significantly ameliorating disease severity and enhancing IFX responsiveness in DSS-induced colitis. Conclusion Monocyte-derived PTGS2 contributes to primary IFX non-response by promoting neutrophil recruitment in UC. GQD improves IFX responsiveness by suppressing PTGS2-associated inflammatory signaling and neutrophil recruitment, highlighting its potential as a therapeutic strategy to enhance IFX efficacy.

papers.title: Development and validation of the IFN-γ FlowCytoScreen for cytokine-based potency assessment of advanced therapy medicinal products.
papers.authors: Carloni S, Piccinini C, Arienti C, Leone DA, Pancisi E, Fanini F, Pignatta S, Soldati V, Stefanelli M, Granato AM, Foca F, Bulgarelli J, Ridolfi L, Petrini M.
papers.abstract: Introduction Robust quality control methods are required to ensure the safety, efficacy and consistency of advanced therapy medicinal products. Potency assays play a critical role in evaluating their biological activity. While ELISpot remains the reference method for single-cell cytokine analysis, it has several limitations such as a lack of standardisation and limited capacity for multiparametric characterisation. This study aimed to develop and validate a flow cytometry-based potency assay for the assessment of single-cell IFN-γ secretion. Methods The commercially available Miltenyi Biotec IFN-γ Secretion Assay - Detection Kit, based on flow cytometry, was modified to assess the potency of dendritic cell-based vaccines. To ensure its reliability, our assay was rigorously evaluated for specificity, linearity, accuracy, robustness and precision. Comparative analysis with the ELISpot assay was also performed to assess agreement between the two methods. Results Method development resulted in reduced sample requirements and optimisation of cytokine secretion conditions to generate a response to antigen-presenting cell stimulus. Validation showed that the specificity, linearity, accuracy, robustness and precision consistently met the acceptance criteria. Comparative analysis with ELISpot demonstrated high correlation and agreement, with no evidence of systematic or proportional error. Discussion The developed assay provides a reliable, scalable and efficient flow cytometry-based approach for cytokine secretion analysis and represents an alternative method to ELISpot. Its advantages in sensitivity, efficiency and cost effectiveness make it a valuable tool for advanced therapy quality control and immune monitoring in clinical research. The flow cytometry further enhances its potential by enabling multiparametric immune profiling, supporting comprehensive characterisation of cellular products in both preclinical and clinical applications.

papers.title: Dendritic cells in atherosclerosis: integrating ontogeny, functional states, spatial organization, and therapeutic implications.
papers.authors: Shao W, Zhang Y, Luo H, Huang J.
papers.abstract: Atherosclerosis arises from the interaction between lipid accumulation and sustained innate and adaptive immune activation, and residual cardiovascular risk despite intensive lipid-lowering therapy underscores the need to clarify vascular inflammatory mechanisms. Dendritic cells (DCs) link antigen sensing and presentation to T-cell regulation, but their roles in atherosclerosis remain incompletely resolved. This review synthesizes evidence on conventional type 1 and type 2 DCs, plasmacytoid DCs, and monocyte-derived DC-like cells using a lineage-state-location-validation framework that asks which cells are present, which functional programs they exhibit, where they are located, and what evidence supports the proposed function. Current evidence indicates that lineage defines functional potential but does not determine pathological activity; lipid loading, oxidative and metabolic stress, extracellular nucleic acids, cytokines, anatomical compartment, and disease stage can shift DCs toward inflammatory, regulatory, or dysfunctional states. Single-cell and spatial profiling have improved resolution of plaque-associated myeloid populations, but rare human DCs, overlap with macrophages and monocytes, cross-sectional sampling, and the inability of expression or proximity to establish causality remain important limitations. Therapeutic strategies should be distinguished as direct or DC-enriched delivery, state- or pathway-directed modulation, and indirect effects on DC function. Current interventions remain preclinical and generally lack sufficient cellular or state selectivity. Future work should prioritize reproducible human DC-state identification, lineage-resolved spatial and functional validation, established-disease models, and biomarkers of pathway activity and target engagement. No specific human DC state is yet clinically actionable.

papers.title: Hupehenine suppresses tumor cell phenotypes and modulates macrophage marker profiles in a diabeticmimetic colorectal cancer model.
papers.authors: Zhu MQ, Shi ZT, Hu HM, Xue QD, Gu XY, Li XC, Wang QY, Zhao Y, Zhang YW, Zhao JZ.
papers.abstract: Background Diabetes is associated with increased colorectal cancer (CRC) risk and mortality, but the molecular links remain incompletely understood. We aimed to characterize shared molecular features of diabetes and CRC, and identify compounds capable of modulating the candidate axis at this interface. Methods Shared disease-associated genes were identified using integrated bioinformatics and protein-protein interaction network analysis, followed by analyses of TCGA and single-cell RNA-sequencing data. Deep learning-based (DeepPurpose) and structure-based (AutoDock Vina) virtual screening were used to prioritize multi-target ligands. Binding was assessed by surface plasmon resonance (SPR) and molecular dynamics simulations. Cellular effects were evaluated in a diabetic-mimetic model using high glucose, insulin, and palmitic acid (three factors; TF), with HCT116 cells and THP-1-derived macrophages. Results The IL1β-CXCL8-CXCR2 axis was prioritized as a candidate inflammatory module at the diabetes-CRC interface. TCGA and single-cell RNA-seq analyses associated axis-related expression with immune infiltration and macrophage polarization-related transcriptional signatures; higher axis expression was also associated with longer overall survival. Hupehenine (HU), a steroidal alkaloid, was identified as a multi-target ligand engaging IL1β, CXCL8, and CXCR2. SPR showed concentration-dependent binding (KD: CXCR2, 505 nM; CXCL8, 2.2 μM; IL1β, 12.7 μM) and interference with CXCL8-CXCR2 binding. In a diabetic-mimetic model, HU reduced HCT116 cell viability, migration, and invasion. TF-conditioned cells were more sensitive to HU than non-TF cells, whereas a corresponding increase in sensitivity was not observed for 5-fluorouracil or oxaliplatin. HU also decreased M2-associated and increased M1-associated macrophage markers. Conclusion These findings support the IL1β-CXCL8-CXCR2 axis as a candidate immunomodulatory module at the diabetes-CRC interface and identify HU as an in vitro multi-target ligand. The observed changes in macrophage markers and differential sensitivity under diabetic-mimetic conditions warrant further mechanistic and preclinical evaluation, including direct assessment of macrophage function.

papers.title: NLRP3 signalling in NSCLC: distinguishing expression, inflammasome activation and context-dependent function.
papers.authors: Wang X, Zhong Y, Pan B, Yang K, Tan H, Huang L, Li X.
papers.abstract: Non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) remains a major cause of cancer-related mortality despite advances in targeted therapy and immune checkpoint blockade. NLRP3-associated inflammation has attracted increasing interest in NSCLC, yet interpretation of the available evidence remains challenging because molecular expression, inflammasome activation, cytokine processing, pyroptotic execution and pathway dependence are frequently considered together. Here, we present a structured narrative review and an evidence framework that separates the biological event directly measured from the level of NLRP3-specific mechanistic support, while independently considering cellular source, disease relevance and treatment context. Current evidence indicates that NLRP3-specific mechanistic dependence in NSCLC has been demonstrated only in selected experimental settings, particularly treatment-conditioned macrophage models. Treatment-naïve human evidence reveals compartment-specific inflammasome-associated responses in alveolar macrophages and peripheral leukocytes but does not establish NLRP3 dependence. Tumour-cell studies support treatment-induced inflammasome- and pyroptosis-associated phenotypes, although causal attribution to NLRP3 is often incomplete. Single-cell and spatial studies mainly identify NLRP3-related transcriptional states or candidate microenvironmental niches and cannot, by themselves, demonstrate functional inflammasome activation or NLRP3-dependent interactions. Clinical trials targeting IL-1β provide evidence for downstream inflammatory modulation but do not directly evaluate NLRP3 inhibition. Overall, current evidence supports context-dependent NLRP3-associated biology in NSCLC rather than a uniform biomarker or therapeutic target. Future studies integrating cell-resolved localisation, activation-specific measurements, pathway perturbation and longitudinal validation are required to determine whether clinically relevant NLRP3-dependent states can be reproducibly identified.

papers.title: SPP1 promotes anoikis resistance and metastatic phenotypes in hepatocellular carcinoma through PI3K-sensitive signaling.
papers.authors: Zhang X, Wei H, Pan R, Ying Q, Dong Y, Xia M.
papers.abstract: Background Anoikis resistance enables tumor cells detached from the extracellular matrix to survive during metastatic dissemination, yet its relationship with the immune microenvironment of hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) remains incompletely understood. Secreted phosphoprotein 1 (SPP1), which encodes osteopontin (OPN), has been implicated in HCC progression. This study investigated the role of SPP1 in anoikis resistance and metastatic phenotypes and evaluated the clinical relevance of circulating OPN in HCC. Methods SPP1 was prioritized through integrated analyses of TCGA-LIHC data, including differential expression, survival association, intersection with anoikis-related genes, and pathway enrichment, followed by characterization of the associated tumor microenvironment. Single-cell transcriptomic analysis was performed to determine the cellular distribution of SPP1 and infer potential intercellular communication. SPP1 expression was validated in HCC tissues and cell lines. Gain- and loss-of-function experiments assessed cell viability, clonogenic growth, migration, invasion, and apoptosis under poly-HEMA suspension. The involvement of PI3K signaling was examined using LY294002. Subcutaneous xenograft and experimental pulmonary colonization models were used to evaluate in vivo phenotypes. Serum OPN and alpha-fetoprotein (AFP) were measured in 58 patients with HCC and 36 healthy controls. Results SPP1 was upregulated in HCC and associated with shorter overall survival. Tumors with high SPP1 expression exhibited a myeloid- and stroma-enriched microenvironmental profile. Single-cell analysis identified prominent SPP1 expression in myeloid populations and inferred potential SPP1-mediated communication between macrophage subsets and malignant hepatocytes. Increased SPP1 expression was independently confirmed in HCC tissues and cell lines. SPP1 overexpression enhanced cell viability, clonogenic growth, migration, invasion, and resistance to suspension-induced apoptosis, whereas SPP1 silencing produced reciprocal effects. LY294002 attenuated SPP1-induced AKT activation, anoikis resistance, motility, and mesenchymal-marker expression, supporting the involvement of PI3K-sensitive signaling. Bidirectional manipulation of SPP1 produced reciprocal effects on xenograft growth and pulmonary colonization-related phenotypes. Serum OPN concentrations were elevated in HCC and were higher in patients with advanced-stage or metastatic disease. High OPN was associated with shorter overall survival (HR, 1.93; 95% CI, 1.01-3.69) and disease-free survival (HR, 2.29; 95% CI, 1.19-4.39).In the same cohort, the areas under the receiver operating characteristic curve for distinguishing patients with HCC from healthy controls were 0.819 for OPN, 0.781 for AFP, and 0.879 for their combination. These findings represent exploratory same-cohort discrimination and require validation in an independent, clinically representative at-risk population. Conclusion SPP1 contributes to anoikis resistance and metastatic phenotypes in HCC, and these phenotypes are sensitive to PI3K inhibition. Single-cell analyses place SPP1 within a myeloid-associated tumor microenvironment, while the inferred communication signals require further experimental validation. Circulating OPN was associated with aggressive HCC features in the present cohort, and its combination with AFP warrants exploratory evaluation in independent, clinically representative at-risk populations.

papers.title: Single-cell sequencing reveals immune networks and metabolic reprogramming in gynecological malignancies.
papers.authors: Ren L, Li X.
papers.abstract: Gynecological malignancies, encompassing ovarian cancer (OC), endometrial cancer (EC), and cervical cancer (CC), represent a group of aggressive neoplasms that pose substantial threats to women's health worldwide. The complex tumor microenvironment (TME) plays a pivotal role in disease progression and therapeutic resistance. In recent years, single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) has enabled systematic characterization of the heterogeneity, functional states, and metabolic reprogramming features of tumor-infiltrating immune cells at unprecedented cellular resolution. Although remarkable progress has been achieved in this field, critical challenges persist, including insufficient understanding of the dynamic mechanisms governing immune cell subset transitions and the intricate regulatory networks underlying metabolism-immune crosstalk. This review summarizes recent advances in single-cell technologies applied to gynecological malignancies, focusing on immune cell subset diversity, intercellular communication networks, and the interplay between metabolic reprogramming and immunosuppression. Furthermore, we discuss potential therapeutic targets and biomarkers derived from these findings, aiming to provide a novel theoretical framework and translational strategies for precision immunotherapy.

papers.title: Single-cell profiling of physically interacting immune cells using image-guided sorting
papers.venue: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology

papers.title: Translating fibroblast heterogeneity into prognosis and immune stratification in pancreatic cancer using machine learning.
papers.authors: Liu YZ, Liu Y, Zhang X.

papers.title: Single-cell profiling reveals GABBR1 as a cuproptosis-regulated prognostic biomarker in pancreatic cancer.
papers.authors: Gong J, Zhang W, Tang L, Long Y, Wang X, Yang J, Yang Y, Montalti R, Troisi RI, Wang H.
papers.abstract: Background and aims Cuproptosis is a recently identified copper-dependent form of cell death with potential therapeutic applications. However, its activity in cancer-associated fibroblasts (CAFs) and its association with pancreatic cancer (PC) prognosis remain poorly understood. This study aimed to address this gap. Methods We performed integrated analyses of scRNA-seq data from patients with PC (GSE212966) and The Cancer Genome Atlas-pancreatic adenocarcinoma dataset. Based on cuproptosis-related AUCell scores, fibroblasts were stratified into high-score (cuproptosis-high) and low-score (cuproptosis-low) groups. Weighted gene coexpression network analysis (WGCNA) was used to identify modules associated with cuproptosis-related genes (CRGs), followed by random survival forest modeling to screen prognostic genes. Functional assessments included gene set variation analysis, immune infiltration analysis via CIBERSORT, and immunohistochemistry for experimental validation. Results scRNA-seq analysis identified fibroblasts as the principal cell type with elevated cuproptosis activity. By integrating WGCNA with survival analysis, we identified GABBR1 as a key gene whose expression decreased with increase in tumor progression. Fibroblasts expressing higher GABBR1 levels also exhibited increased expression of immune checkpoint genes and T-cell activation markers. A nomogram integrating GABBR1 expression with clinical features showed strong prognostic performance. Immunohistochemical validation confirmed that GABBR1 , LIAS , and LIPT1 were expressed at significantly lower levels in tumor tissues than in adjacent normal tissues. Importantly, GABBR1 expression negatively correlated with PC progression and was linked to CRGs ( LIAS and LIPT1 ), emerging as a novel CAF-specific biomarker. Conclusion Modulating GABBR1 can reshape cuproptosis pathways, thereby influencing apoptotic sensitivity and modulating immune responses.

papers.title: Breakthroughs in the Pathological Mechanism and Comprehensive Management of Pulmonary Hypertension.
papers.authors: Zhou K, Gong Y, Zhang J, Chen D, Liu Y, Xu Z.
papers.abstract: Pulmonary hypertension (PH) is a rare and life-threatening vascular disorder characterized by complex and multifactorial pathogenesis. Emerging evidence indicates that pulmonary vascular remodeling is driven by coordinated abnormalities in genetic susceptibility, epigenetic regulation, metabolic reprogramming, immune-inflammatory crosstalk, and DNA damage repair. Recent advances in multi-omics profiling, single-cell technologies, and high-resolution imaging have substantially improved the understanding of PH pathobiology and disease heterogeneity. Current therapeutic strategies mainly target the three classical vasoactive pathways to alleviate vasoconstriction and improve hemodynamics. Notably, (bone morphogenetic protein) BMP/transforming growth factor‑β1 (TGF-β) pathway-targeted therapy, represented by sotatercept, has initiated a new era of disease-modifying treatment aimed at reversing pulmonary vascular remodeling. In addition, emerging therapies targeting immune, hormonal, and metabolic pathways have demonstrated promising therapeutic potential. Despite significant progress in both basic and clinical research, major challenges remain, including precise phenotypic stratification, long-term therapeutic safety, and individualized treatment optimization. This review summarizes recent advances in the molecular mechanisms and comprehensive management of PH and highlights future directions for translational research and precision medicine.

papers.title: Lactylation-associated CXCL12-mediated intercellular communication in rheumatic heart disease valves.
papers.authors: Zhai J, Zuo Z, Yan T, Liu F, Liu J, Zhu K, Lai H, Wang C, Li J.
papers.abstract: Background Rheumatic heart disease (RHD) is characterized by persistent valvular inflammation and fibrosis. Lactate-driven lysine lactylation may couple metabolic stress to inflammatory transcription, but its relationship with CXCL12-mediated immune recruitment in RHD valves remains unclear. Methods Paired aortic and mitral valve single-cell RNA-sequencing data from three patients with RHD were analyzed, yielding 47,237 quality-controlled cells. CXCL12-producing cell populations were identified, and lactylation-related transcriptional states and inflammatory pathways were assessed in CXCL12-high structural cells using complementary scoring and pseudobulk approaches. CellChat was used to infer CXCL12-mediated intercellular communication, with GSE153555 used for external validation. Human valve interstitial cells (VICs) were treated with lactate, the p300 inhibitor A-485, or the NF-κB inhibitor BAY 11-7082. CXCL12/CXCR4-dependent monocyte chemotaxis was evaluated using THP-1 cells, AMD3100, and a CXCL12-neutralizing antibody. Results VICs and myofibroblasts were the principal CXCL12-producing cells. Within CXCL12-high structural cells, a higher lactylation-related transcriptional state was associated with enhanced NF-κB and TNF signaling and increased IL6, BIRC3, REL, and TNFAIP3 expression. CellChat supported CXCL12-CXCR4 communication from structural cells to myeloid and lymphoid cells, while external validation confirmed increased CXCL12, IL6, and TNFAIP3 expression in diseased valves. In VICs, lactate increased Pan-Kla, H3K9la, H3K14la, and CXCL12 expression and secretion. A-485 attenuated lactylation-associated CXCL12 induction, whereas BAY 11-7082 suppressed NF-κB activation and CXCL12 expression. Lactate-conditioned medium enhanced THP-1 migration and inflammatory gene expression, which were reduced by pathway inhibition or CXCL12/CXCR4 blockade. Conclusion These findings link lactylation-associated metabolic signaling in RHD valve structural cells to NF-κB-dependent CXCL12 production and CXCL12-CXCR4-mediated monocyte recruitment, providing a mechanistic framework for stromal-immune communication in RHD.

papers.title: LILRB4 expression is associated with macrophage enrichment and differential survival in hepatocellular carcinoma.
papers.authors: Liu Q, Liu Y, Chen J, Wan T, Li C, Zhang N, Yang Z.
papers.abstract: Background and aims The clinical and immune-cell context of leukocyte immunoglobulin-like receptor B4 (LILRB4) in hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) remains incompletely characterized. This study aimed to characterize LILRB4 expression across cell types and examine its associations with survival outcomes and macrophage-related immune features in HCC. Methods Public liver hepatocellular carcinoma (LIHC) resources were analyzed using survival, transcriptomic, functional enrichment, immune deconvolution, and single-cell analyses. Survival analyses included 373 patients for overall survival and 365 for disease-specific survival. Kaplan-Meier analyses compared two expression groups (high and low), defined using outcome-selected cutpoints obtained from maximally selected rank statistics. Continuous-expression Cox models provided complementary analyses. Results Higher LILRB4 expression was associated with shorter overall survival (OS) in an outcome-selected analysis ( n = 373; low-expression group, 250; high-expression group, 123; Cox hazard ratio [HR], 1.524; 95% confidence interval [CI], 1.074-2.162; log-rank p = 0.017). Continuous LILRB4 expression was associated with OS in univariable and adjusted Cox models (adjusted HR, 1.246; 95% CI, 1.010-1.537), whereas continuous expression was not significantly associated with disease-specific survival (HR, 1.137; 95% CI, 0.916-1.412). LILRB4 expression correlated with macrophage enrichment (Spearman r s = 0.755) and M2-like macrophage estimates from quanTIseq ( r s = 0.544) and CIBERSORT-ABS ( r s = 0.753). Single-cell resources localized LILRB4 mainly to monocyte/macrophage populations. Conclusion LILRB4 expression is associated with macrophage-enriched immune features and adverse survival patterns in LIHC. These findings identify LILRB4 as a candidate marker of the macrophage-rich HCC microenvironment that warrants further investigation of its prognostic and immunoregulatory relevance.

papers.title: Single-cell atlas of fetal immunity across lung, spleen, and umbilical cord blood in nonhuman primates.
papers.authors: Doratt BM, Wagner SB, Keen KE, Avila U, Varlamov O, Messaoudi I.
papers.abstract: The fetal immune system develops within a tightly regulated environment that balances immune tolerance with readiness for postnatal antigen exposure. However, limited fetal tissue access constrains understanding of immune ontogeny across compartments. Here we present a multi-tissue single-cell transcriptional atlas of the late-gestation (GD130-135) rhesus macaque fetal immune system, profiling leukocytes from lung, spleen, and umbilical cord blood (UCBMC) spanning myeloid, lymphoid, innate lymphoid, and hematopoietic stem cell lineages. Fetal lung is enriched in myeloid cells and ILC2s and shows a proinflammatory bias. Spleen is dominated by T and B cells, with B cells showing enhanced signatures of V(D)J recombination and isotype switching and CD4 T cells showing increased activation and Treg frequency. UCBMC is predominantly composed of T cells with a regulatory transcriptional landscape. Spectral flow cytometry and functional assays corroborate these tissue-specific differences revealing elevated secretion of inflammatory mediators in fetal lung at rest, while spleen and UCBMC show greater inducible responses following stimulation. Together, these data provide a comprehensive cross-tissue atlas of late-gestation primate fetal immunity, revealing tissue-specific immune specialization, functional capacity, and intercellular communication networks that shape immune readiness prior to birth.

papers.title: Physiopathology of severe drug-induced skin reactions.
papers.authors: Oro S, Contassot E.
papers.abstract: Severe cutaneous adverse drug reactions (SCARs) and targeted therapy-induced skin toxicities are major challenges in modern oncology and immunology. Classical SCARs, including Stevens-Johnson syndrome/toxic epidermal necrolysis (SJS/TEN), drug reaction with eosinophilia and systemic symptoms (DRESS), and acute generalized exanthematous pustulosis (AGEP), are associated with significant morbidity and mortality. In parallel, immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs), EGFR inhibitors (EGFRi), and MEK inhibitors (MEKi) have introduced novel inflammatory skin toxicities that often overlap clinically with classical SCARs but involve distinct pathogenic mechanisms. These disorders are now recognized as highly organized immune-mediated syndromes involving complex interactions between keratinocytes, cytotoxic T cells, eosinophils, neutrophils, dendritic cells, and inflammatory cytokine networks. SJS/TEN is driven by HLA-restricted cytotoxic CD8+ T-cell responses causing widespread keratinocyte death through granulysin, perforin/granzyme B, and Fas-FasL pathways. DRESS is characterized by systemic Th2/eosinophilic inflammation and viral reactivation, whereas AGEP is dominated by neutrophilic inflammation involving CXCL8, IL-17, and IL-36 signaling. EGFRi- and MEKi-induced toxicities primarily reflect epithelial stress and barrier dysfunction, while ICI-induced SCAR-like reactions result from loss of peripheral immune tolerance and exaggerated autoreactive T-cell activation. Despite recent advances, predictive biomarkers and mechanisms underlying tissue specificity remain poorly understood. Emerging technologies such as single-cell transcriptomics, spatial omics, and T-cell receptor sequencing are expected to improve mechanistic understanding and therapeutic targeting. Selective modulation of pathways including IL-17, IL-23, JAK/STAT, and IL-36 may offer novel strategies to control severe cutaneous inflammation while preserving antitumor efficacy. This review summarizes current knowledge on the immunopathogenesis, clinical features, and therapeutic perspectives of classical SCARs and anticancer therapy-induced severe skin toxicities.

papers.title: Inflammasomes in Atherosclerosis and Atherothrombosis.
papers.authors: Grigoriou K, Antoniadis AP, Lamprou V, Ktenopoulos N, Theofilis P, Iliakis P, Vlachakis PK, Apostolos A, Fyntanidou B, Karagiannidis E, Fragakis N, Karakasis P.
papers.abstract: Atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease and its thrombotic complications, particularly myocardial infarction and ischemic stroke, remain leading causes of morbidity and mortality worldwide. Atherosclerosis was historically considered primarily a lipid accumulation disorder; however, it is now well recognized as a chronic inflammatory disesse driven in large part by innate immune signaling. Inflammasomes, particularly NOD-like receptor protein 3 (NLRP3) and absent in melanoma 2 (AIM2), play important role in this process, linking vascular inflammation, plaque progression, and thrombosis through caspase-1 activation, interleukin-1 beta (IL-1β) and IL-18 release, and gasdermin-mediated pyroptosis. In this narrative review we integrate mechanistic and translational evidence defining inflammasome activity across the continuum of atherosclerosis and atherothrombosis. We highlight inflammasome signaling in endothelial cells, macrophages, vascular smooth muscle cells, platelets, neutrophils, and perivascular adipose tissue, and discuss how these pathways contribute to early inflammation, necrotic core expansion, fibrous cap destabilization, and ultimately to acute thrombus formation. Emerging data on AIM2 activation, clonal hematopoiesis, platelet inflammasomes, and cell-free deoxyribonucleic acid (DNA) further expand current paradigms beyond macrophage focused models on macrophages. We also review single-cell and spatial transcriptomics, circulating biomarkers, and advanced vascular imaging approaches that may enable the identification of inflammasome-high atherothrombotic phenotypes. Finally, we appraise therapeutic strategies targeting inflammasomes and downstream pathways. These include IL-1β and IL-6 inhibition, colchicine, direct NLRP3 inhibition, and cardiometabolic therapies with indirect effects on inflammasome activity. By examining the role of inflammasomes in linking plaque pathogenesis to thrombosis, this review outlines key translational opportunities and challenges for the precision prevention of atherothrombosis.

papers.title: Treatment-naive status and thyroid autoimmunity as determinants of early biochemical thyroid outcome after radioiodine therapy for Graves' disease: A retrospective cohort study.
papers.authors: Zhang S, Ding X, Liu J, Wang G.
papers.abstract: ObjectiveEarly biochemical thyroid outcomes after iodine-131 ( 131 I) therapy for Graves' disease are heterogeneous. We aimed to identify baseline determinants of 3-month biochemical outcome and assess whether the FT3/FT4 ratio, thyrotroph thyroxine resistance index (TT4RI), or machine-learning algorithms added predictive value.MethodsWe retrospectively reviewed 637 consecutive patients with clinically documented Graves' disease treated with 131 I between November 2022 and November 2024. Graves' disease was identified from contemporaneous endocrinologist-recorded diagnoses rather than uniform thyrotropin-receptor antibody confirmation. Three-month thyroid status was classified as persistent overt hyperthyroidism, euthyroidism, or hypothyroidism using institutional biochemical reference ranges; remission was defined as euthyroidism or hypothyroidism. A prespecified multivariable logistic model included age, sex, treatment-naive status, disease duration, goiter grade, administered dose, 24-hour radioactive iodine uptake, thyroid peroxidase antibody (TPOAb), and thyroglobulin antibody. Cross-validated prediction models assessed derived indices and machine-learning algorithms.ResultsAt 3 months, 464 patients (72.8%) achieved remission and 369 (57.9%) were hypothyroid. Treatment-naive status and higher TPOAb were independently associated with remission (OR 1.67, 95% CI 1.06-2.62; TPOAb OR 1.11 per log-unit, 1.01-1.23) and hypothyroidism (OR 1.95, 1.29-2.97; TPOAb OR 1.16, 1.06-1.27). Lower goiter grade and higher administered dose were also associated with both outcomes. Discrimination was modest (remission AUC 0.59; hypothyroidism AUC 0.62). Derived indices and machine-learning algorithms did not consistently improve clinically meaningful prediction; an isolated positive continuous NRI for hypothyroidism was not supported by improved AUC or IDI. By 6 months, 273 patients, all hypothyroid at 3 months, had not returned; among reassessed 3-month hypothyroid patients, 21% reverted to euthyroidism.ConclusionsTreatment-naive status and TPOAb were associated with early biochemical outcome after 131 I therapy, but baseline prediction remained limited. Early hypothyroidism should be interpreted as a 3-month biochemical state rather than definitive ablation.

papers.title: Inhibition of G6PD-Mediated MAPK Signaling Triggers Mitochondrial Apoptosis and Cell Cycle Arrest in Hepatocellular Carcinoma.
papers.authors: Ma X, Liu J, Xu J, Bu Y, Liu K.
papers.abstract: Background Glucose-6-phosphate dehydrogenase (G6PD) has been implicated in tumor progression. This study investigated the biological role of G6PD in the malignant progression of hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) and explored the underlying molecular mechanisms. Methods RNA-sequencing data and corresponding clinical data for patients with HCC were obtained from The Cancer Genome Atlas (TCGA). Independent validation datasets were obtained from Gene Expression Omnibus (GEO). We performed bioinformatics analyses to assess the expression of G6PD in HCC, as well as its relationship with clinical features and prognostic outcomes. Immunohistochemistry and western blotting were used to validate G6PD expression in human HCC tissues and cell lines. Stable G6PD-overexpressing and knockdown cell lines were established using lentiviral transduction. Functional assays were performed using G6PD-overexpressing and G6PD-knockdown cell lines to evaluate cell proliferation, cell cycle progression, apoptosis, mitochondrial function, and oxidative stress. Western blotting was conducted to assess the protein levels of key regulators of cell cycle progression, apoptosis, and the MAPK pathway. Finally, a BALB/c nude mouse xenograft model was used to evaluate the in vivo effects of G6PD on tumor growth. Results G6PD was significantly overexpressed in HCC tissues and was significantly associated with histological grade ( p p = 0.039), vascular invasion ( p = 0.002), and pathological stage ( p = 0.031). Patients with high G6PD expression exhibited significantly shorter overall, disease-specific, and progression-free survival. Multivariate analysis identified high G6PD expression as an independent predictor of mortality in patients with HCC. G6PD knockdown significantly inhibited HCCLM3 cell proliferation and induced G0/G1 cell-cycle arrest, accompanied by the downregulation of cyclin-dependent kinase 4 (CDK4), cyclin-dependent kinase 6 (CDK6), and cyclin D1 protein levels. In addition, G6PD silencing triggered mitochondrial apoptosis, including decreased mitochondrial membrane potential, BCL-2-associated X protein (BAX) and cysteine-aspartic acid protease-3 (caspase-3) upregulation, B-cell lymphoma 2 (BCL-2) downregulation, elevated reactive oxygen species (ROS) levels, and suppressed MEK1/2 and ERK1/2 phosphorylation. In vivo , G6PD knockdown significantly reduced xenograft tumor size and weight and decreased Ki67 and proliferating cell nuclear antigen (PCNA) expression. Conclusions G6PD is an independent prognostic biomarker in HCC and promotes disease progression through pleiotropic mechanisms, including modulation of the MAPK/ERK pathway, promotion of cell proliferation, and suppression of mitochondrial apoptosis. These findings suggest that G6PD and its downstream signaling pathways may be promising therapeutic targets for HCC.
